descriptions.c8d2c13e-fd9a-466c-9fdc-fc26ee798ded: Discovered in 2011 by a sonar treasure-hunting crew, a 60-metre circular object with straight edges sits on the seabed. Its origin remains hotly contested and unexplained.
descriptions.8cead41d-19f8-45cf-9dc0-144583641e4f: Royal palace of the Silla dynasty from 57 BC to 938 AD, its crescent-moon-shaped walls gave it the name Half Moon Fortress. The palace grounds are today a public park in Gyeongju.
descriptions.fd42ae8f-5d57-4764-9d0e-5020eaf3eb13: Caves and stone buildings on a forested Rhone valley hill, inhabited continuously from the Neolithic until the early 20th century. A chapel from 1706, partly built in a cave, still stands.
descriptions.fae3bb4b-85fb-427a-a896-f32f4a2aa69c: Bronze Age burial mounds in Somerset, its medieval name 'Battlegore' attached after a Danish raid in 918 AD. Three round barrows, possibly a long chambered barrow, referenced since the 14th century.
descriptions.393368d9-3c73-4e8c-b174-d898bbe31862: Iron Age hill fort perched 290 metres above the Heddon Valley. A commanding lookout above Devon's ancient valleys, its earthworks still read the shape of an Iron Age community.
descriptions.df4987a2-4247-4be4-8d1c-89e3e6f816fe: Iron Age hill fort crowning Long Mountain at 408 metres, possibly crossed by a Roman road linking Wroxeter to Forden Gaer. The summit lies within one country while the mountain straddles two.
descriptions.f54065ac-566a-476e-9261-76c541fdc0b6: 3rd–4th century Romano-British farm in North Yorkshire. First explored in 1928, a 1966 excavation revealed a mosaic pavement measuring over 11 by 7 metres in the northern building.
descriptions.312d9851-989c-4b8d-9c24-094af1acc582: Six standing stones aligned on a flat Cork pasture, dating to the Bronze Age. A quiet monument on open land — no burial, no inscription, just six stones still pointing at the sky.
descriptions.ce34d01c-2590-4713-b2f3-d2f088307e71: Occupied from 2460 BC, transhumant pastoralists wintered here in the piedmont steppes, herding sheep and goats. Their burials shifted from cist graves to kurgans over the centuries.
descriptions.434a12f5-3cdd-4669-9db0-4cb31fd322d4: Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age settlements layered on one hill. Excavations in 1999-2000 uncovered over 350 pit houses and 40-50 large structures from successive eras.
descriptions.511f2e4b-9e01-4999-9e7f-55ec56946708: Iron Age earthwork in Devon once known as 'bigulfesburh' -- Beowulf's burgh. Whether hill fort or livestock enclosure, its name links it to the oldest hero in Anglo-Saxon literary tradition.
descriptions.e8fea646-0b0c-466c-913a-9a99c7dd786d: A layered ruin complex including the Keykubat Castle built with Roman mortar, grave remains from an old settlement called Heik, cave systems, and ceramic-strewn mounds across multiple areas.
descriptions.c1448f84-e07a-436a-8110-087f293a6564: Bronze Age tumuli dot a 3.5-kilometre ridge rising to 173 metres above the Hanover plain. The hill's name comes from the village of Benthe below — the mounds remain its most ancient feature.
descriptions.8bcea3e7-dfdc-4af5-8b75-70fb9e34d7ee: Occupied from the Paleolithic through classical antiquity, this Peloponnese valley yielded a Late Mycenaean Potter's Quarter holding over 175,000 ceramic sherds — a snapshot of ancient industry.
descriptions.27d651ad-32dc-4bbc-bbb9-9218d9aec357: Iron Age earthwork in Devon sitting on a hillslope rather than a hilltop — defying the usual hill fort pattern. Its incomplete enclosure shape has never been fully explained by archaeologists.
descriptions.cdde5a6a-ab08-42ae-a3e7-ab1d0d2c0f20: Iron Age hill fort on a forested promontory 95 metres above Devon. Recent tree clearance in 2015 revealed a rectangular shape with entrances at both ends, suggesting it may be a Roman camp.
descriptions.dcb2b187-5d69-4824-bb7a-d098ba39231c: Late Iron Age or early Roman hillslope enclosure in Somerset, protected as a scheduled monument. Multiple surviving earthworks mark the outline of a community poised between two eras.
descriptions.2a535811-de40-4aa8-9768-ebbd9c43f22a: Iron Age hill fort above the River Lemon in Devon, 75 metres up on a promontory above Bradley Manor. Its single limestone rampart and sunken approach were first described in print in 1950.
descriptions.133ef307-1b56-4af3-9411-cd66947d8cc0: Iron Age hillfort on a sandstone outcrop in Staffordshire, 320 metres long and defended by contour-following ramparts. Known variously as Bryth, Bruff, and Burgh Hill — identity still debated.
descriptions.ee94fe5e-d975-4ed9-940d-16056532293e: Ancient Hellenistic rock tombs cut directly into the cliff face. Carved in the 3rd–1st centuries BC, these chamber tombs represent the Carian tradition of monumental burial in living stone.
descriptions.b159a282-c65f-448b-9839-c1581d6a263f: 2nd century AD catacombs that became the primary Jewish burial site outside Jerusalem after the second revolt against Rome. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, compiler of the Mishnah, was buried here.
descriptions.a61f0c60-94d8-43c4-9c2f-e30ffff8da13: Iron Age plateau fort on a chalk ridge in Hampshire, enclosing 1.7 hectares with a single bank and ditch. Largely destroyed and overgrown, the southern ramparts preserve the best evidence.
descriptions.59267588-ef6b-40b7-9990-c93b2b6d08f4: An unfinished Jain statue carved only to the knees in soft soapstone — depicting Bharateshwara, brother of Bahubali and son of the first Tirthankara. The sculptor stopped, and never returned.
descriptions.bc879dfc-3a9d-4007-832b-ecf2bd8fbe75: Eight ancient temples carved into a cliff face beneath a 200-metre waterfall sacred to Shiva. The roar of the falls has accompanied worship at this site for nearly two thousand years.
descriptions.87d83a5b-d7a2-45dc-b8fd-1bed588bbeec: Rock-cut caves near Junnar, part of the Hinayana Buddhist tradition. Among roughly 200 such caves cut into these hills between the 3rd century BC and 3rd century AD.
descriptions.8ef3e56e-3dd8-4576-a5bf-eab965bcd0a7: Rock-cut cave complex near Junnar belonging to the Hinayana phase of Buddhism. One of roughly 200 Buddhist cave sites carved into these hills from the 3rd century BC onward.
descriptions.58733868-7f7f-42e3-9d30-2fb9feb7fd05: Ancient Cretan city-state listed by the Byzantine geographer Hierocles among 22 cities of Crete. Positioned 170 stadia from Hierapytna, it appears in myths tied to Otus and Ephialtes.
descriptions.8fe4115a-617d-4cfc-ab35-272e8b2c1db2: A 186-hectare reserve containing Aboriginal rock art sites in New South Wales, with occupation evidence stretching back to around 8000 BC — deep roots beneath suburban Sydney's outer ring.
descriptions.b46b6969-3160-4cbd-a574-8727ee7c53c5: Built mid-4th century AD in ancient Philippopolis, this is the largest late antique early-Christian church on the Balkans. Its marble presbyterium and colonnaded atrium once rivalled Constantinople.
descriptions.1f3c04f4-4025-4779-9968-6aa298127478: A Bronze Age megalithic structure — likely a dolmen burial chamber — on a hillside near Grossa in southern Corsica, dating to around 2000–3000 BC in the island's dense prehistoric landscape.
descriptions.608c6936-8fdb-4a2a-a6f2-8c250ca524c1: Iron Age promontory hill fort covering 6 hectares in Somerset, with two ramparts and two ditches. The west and south flanks relied on natural steep drops rather than earthworks for defence.
descriptions.dc951bdb-a70d-4346-9e7d-fdc0d908d4c5: Neolithic flint mine with over 64 infilled shafts, each up to 6 metres across, on a West Sussex hillside. Levelled around 1950, Bronze Age barrows share the same scheduled site.
descriptions.ea159045-9163-41c2-9026-71edd41683ec: Archaeological site in the municipality of Pozega, inscribed on the national cultural heritage list in 1987. Its era and full extent remain unknown pending excavation.
descriptions.b92a39fb-f7fe-4f78-a967-7d6370c88f0e: Founded around 1400 BC in northern Majorca, this pre-Roman city later became a federated ally of Rome, as recorded by Pliny the Elder. One of the oldest settlements in the Balearic Islands.
descriptions.9db1409d-3216-4448-b9c9-c42d5071ba4d: Bronze Age axial stone circle of 13 stones — four now missing — with a diameter of 9.1 metres in Cork. Its portal stones stand nearly 2.5 metres tall, among the tallest in the region.
descriptions.a9530765-9f35-44df-b2dc-2b7b029fee7f: Stone artifacts and charcoal in this Tasmanian limestone cave date to 29,000 years ago. Between 16,000 and 14,000 BC it became a stone-tool workshop — most intensive use after the glacial maximum.
descriptions.543c85d7-47af-4b78-a412-e55f6836d6ea: Saka Iron Age kurgan necropolis covering 430 hectares on the outskirts of Almaty, with 47 burial mounds from the 5th to 3rd centuries BC. Declared a protected monument in 2010.
descriptions.f51d767d-66b7-47bc-b2ca-2d5ca3594b52: Large multivallate Iron Age hill fort near Sawston, oval-shaped at 430 by 300 metres. Its broad enclosure hints at a substantial community once settled on this Cambridgeshire rise.
descriptions.8df8659c-49be-4a66-b25a-ecbf96541515: A cluster of natural hills near Visoko claimed since 2005 to be the world's largest ancient pyramids. Every mainstream archaeologist and geologist has rejected the claim as pseudoscience.
descriptions.740c492e-c3fb-41ad-8d93-339ff4b24598: Late Iron Age courtyard houses with walls surviving up to 1.5 metres in west Cornwall. One structure later had a medieval cowhouse built inside it — layers of habitation millennia apart.
descriptions.29f84776-1d97-4e09-ad40-95ea6e2d7247: Aboriginal hunting camp on the shores of Lake Tyrrell with radiocarbon dates of 24,600–33,000 BC — among the earliest known occupation evidence between the Murray River and the mallee.
descriptions.09895c88-e3d8-4ad2-b23e-eef85097ab6e: The smallest of Cheshire's seven Iron Age hill forts, and the furthest north — in a county where hill forts are rare. A scheduled monument marking the frontier of Iron Age territory.
descriptions.add7a025-751a-4335-98f4-8808ccc1221f: Iron Age hill fort later reused as a Roman fort, with a roughly triangular enclosure 250 by 260 metres in Herefordshire. Two eras of occupation share the same defended hill.
descriptions.356a2f8e-8174-48e6-ae7f-8c53b9ae6124: 2nd century AD Roman villa discovered in 1941 at a stone quarry. A 1961 dig found a mosaic floor measuring 11 by 7 metres; a 1983 excavation turned up earlier Iron Age remains beneath.
descriptions.ad9470d2-0225-4dec-b6a3-b4135df95403: Iron Age oppidum on the River Rib that grew into a Roman town in Britannia. Its Latin name is unknown. Iron Age ditches, enclosures, and Roman-era remains overlap in Hertfordshire's soil.
descriptions.5a440726-598a-48a2-87fc-ae833a534da6: The largest known open-air Aurignacian settlement site in western Eurasia, from the early Upper Palaeolithic -- when anatomically modern humans were first colonising Europe.
descriptions.15f94167-4c6b-4d02-b46f-6b6dcb147c19: Iron Age defended settlement on Hawkridge Ridge Wood in Somerset, close to Mounsey Castle. Its earthworks survive on a wooded ridge about 3 kilometres from the market town of Dulverton.
descriptions.4caf5522-6a45-44b4-bba0-e98186c081f1: A square 58-by-68-metre earthwork that may be a Roman marching camp or Iron Age civilian settlement. The heritage authority notes the interpretation, but firm evidence is still lacking.
descriptions.b10bc2a8-f979-4096-a3e2-2e9c88c814ef: Univallate Iron Age hill fort in Somerset. A 1968 trench through its bank and ditch produced Iron Age pottery, confirming occupation in the Late Prehistoric or early Roman period.
descriptions.c3131199-f90a-43c9-901d-87857f47a6f6: Bronze Age cist cemetery and the first Iron Age roundhouses confirmed by excavation in Argyll, uncovered before quarrying destroyed the site. A 19th-century standing stone was added much later.
descriptions.f151db5d-5515-495e-ba5e-bde2a46c553a: Roman auxiliary fort built around 160 AD near Leintwardine, abandoned by 196 AD. Entirely buried, its outline was first spotted from the air in 1959 — a ghost fort visible only from above.
descriptions.739f3b71-4f87-4f30-9a58-de5e2c95f0af: Multivallate Iron Age hill fort overlooking the Avon Gorge in Somerset, one of three Iron Age fortifications defending this strategic river approach. Also known as Bower Walls and Burwalls.
descriptions.f7dc1fe7-5ed8-4083-ab72-c4a3b8baa206: Dilmun burial mound field dating to the 3rd millennium BC, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019 as part of the broader Dilmun Burial Mounds complex.
descriptions.732c789d-d491-4614-85f0-0d08890acaf8: 1st century AD Roman auxiliary fort covering 3 hectares, built in at least two phases in Lancashire. An initial sandstone fort was later expanded, its second phase built over the eastern rampart.
descriptions.449c3f0a-6666-4355-8dbf-db881bd8866a: Iron Age hillfort on an imposing hill above the River Teifi, its defences enclosing 1.5 hectares with a drystone rampart. The name Gwrtheyrn connects it to a legendary early Brittonic king.
descriptions.7b92eca0-e4cb-45f7-89ea-8403e5123add: Neolithic chambered cairn on an uninhabited Orkney island, excavated in 1936–37. Rectangular in plan, it holds two chambers: one with two compartments, another with four stalls added later.
descriptions.c70f0de4-5bfb-43d9-990c-ade222df557f: Bronze Age, Iron Age, and Roman rural occupation layers on a single Somerset site. A 2009 excavation found burnt mounds, roundhouses, and a Late Iron Age field system that persisted into Roman times.
descriptions.5bf42cbd-5082-43a3-b064-91ca60423e51: Among the most significant rock art discoveries in the world, ranked in the top 10 finds of 2021. Twenty-one carvings -- 17 camels, two equids, and one unidentified figure -- on a remarkable scale.
descriptions.9230af4b-1e48-4628-ab38-3ed4d44200d7: Two graves from the 3rd millennium BC on the Corsican hillside near Bisinchi — a quiet twin tomb from a time when Corsica's megalithic tradition was at its height.
descriptions.ffb35fc7-24f7-4722-8036-e4173ac6d8e6: Late Neolithic dolmen (stazzona) built around 4000-3000 BC. Its back slab is wedged between side stones — a signature style shared with the Fontanaccia dolmen on the same megalithic plateau.
descriptions.86207cd7-b3f0-45e0-b589-97f8a04cc300: A 3-metre standing stone near Penzance also called Cuckoo Rock. Excavated over New Year 1957–58, it was found wedged into an elliptical pit with small stones — the exact ancient method preserved.
descriptions.0e0531f8-6b94-43ab-b6db-81611a30e297: One of only four Aboriginal stone arrangements in Victoria and the only one in a boomerang design. Sixty metres long, with a double arc of boulders, cairn, and small stone circles.
descriptions.fa63ee12-8c34-4e02-9c52-64b9ddcce64e: A Bronze Age cairn group on the ridge northwest of Foel Dduarth. The main mound is 13.75 m across with concentric slate rings and a central burial cist
descriptions.5928dcb7-1a73-4bf6-8bd3-3fe6ba8c6b90: Bronze Age inauguration mound near Rathcroghan, believed to be the cairn of the Connacht warrior Fráech. Kings of Connacht were inaugurated here well into medieval times, atop ancient bones.
descriptions.90aea48d-7062-4d8a-b650-266b1478ae5b: Neolithic or Early Bronze Age deer carvings discovered in 2021 inside Dunchraigaig Cairn -- the first of their kind found anywhere in this part of the world. Two stags with full forked antlers.
descriptions.bf673fda-ff81-4dda-b31f-11025b1a6382: A crossroads city of ancient Campania, where the Via Appia met the Via Latina at a three-arched bridge still standing today. Its strategic position made it a contested prize during the Roman Republic.
descriptions.86383b38-f1a1-4f04-9b7e-8a49c3495829: Late Bronze Age hilltop casteddu occupied from ~1500 to 800 BC. Walls were built with storage silos packed inside them; pottery workshops and domestic debris mark a community that stored and traded.
descriptions.3cde520c-1af6-47b0-84e0-00ec2db63478: Late 3rd century AD Roman fortress on the Danube's left shore. Part of the Roman limes defensive network, inscribed on the national cultural heritage register in 1995.
descriptions.7fe95d48-f215-4dfd-8c1b-84420764a73d: Iron Age promontory hill fort 100 metres above a bow in the River Tamar on the Devon-Cornwall border. A second earthwork sits lower on the same promontory, with further works across the river.
descriptions.74c060c0-0099-4efb-a59c-5967e7f9712a: Univallate Iron Age hill fort in Somerset's Taunton Deane with Roman coins found scattered through its defences — evidence of occupation stretching from the Bronze Age into the Roman period.
descriptions.7fae9578-5fff-4689-9141-2b9edc533b8e: Iron Age promontory fort overlooking the River Irwell in Bury, occupied from 200 BC to 250 AD. Excavated pottery pins its active lifespan to a span bridging the Iron Age and Roman eras.
descriptions.b5494a21-b48f-454f-b0c7-687274173f4c: Iron Age fortified village covering 3 hectares with two concentric stone walls — the outer reaching 5.2 metres high and 4.2 metres thick. Thirty-six circular buildings packed the interior.
descriptions.7ee94c43-3a26-44db-8dee-bd7829b5a171: Chalcolithic settlement from the 4th millennium BC that became a Bronze Age metallurgical centre, then a Moorish stronghold. Multiple civilisations found this hilltop worth defending.
descriptions.ccb5fcce-35d3-463a-bb98-0cfc09918465: Proto-historic fortified settlement in the Douro valley, later occupied by Romans and medieval settlers. It fell under the Suevic kingdom and was mentioned in the reign of Ordoño II of León.
descriptions.6d04a9ad-3da8-415b-a69a-2f3343244e67: Chalcolithic fortified settlement with finds dating from 900 BC, inhabited until the 5th century AD. A medieval castle was built here later -- each era recognising the same strategic high ground.
descriptions.99b48063-3d7a-4107-b510-2cf4b6191129: Hillside castro overlooking an open valley, occupied from the Neolithic through the Middle Ages. Two thousand years of successive communities chose this vantage for protection and survival.
descriptions.67b015db-bcdf-4250-92e0-d43ef1237e4b: Iron Age Castro culture settlement on the Lima River estuary, occupied during initial Roman colonisation of northwest Iberia — from the late 1st century BC to around 70 AD.
descriptions.45c293d7-6d69-47e5-adec-68b8e1ce6ec0: Ruins of Constantina, a Roman and Byzantine city on the Syrian frontier. An arch, cut stone blocks, and structural remains survive from the city known to the Assyrian population as Tella.
descriptions.0f785541-1f36-4dc8-9daa-3ebc5c540bd0: Roman fort and town that evolved into modern Catterick. Bronze Age cairns and Iron Age enclosures predate the Roman settlement, with activity on both sides of the River Swale from ancient times.
descriptions.4f32070e-25b0-4f96-a895-37499099f745: Neolithic timber circle in Staffordshire dated 4100–2500 BC, with around 225 postholes invisible at ground level but visible as cropmarks from the air. Scheduled and still largely unexcavated.
descriptions.90ec5b47-7488-4bb4-8c4d-1259d30ac328: Plateau of armed statue-menhirs carved with faces, hands, and daggers. Two alignments — I Stantari (55 stones) and Rinaghju (46 stones) — flank the best-preserved dolmen on Corsica;
descriptions.917cd017-9d91-4c24-a8e2-1af2f6d04c1e: Cave 20 of 24 rock-cut chambers at Pandavleni, carved 1st century BC–3rd century AD on a hill's north face. A large vihara housing Buddha statues 3 metres tall alongside other deities.
descriptions.010c0b09-760b-44f6-ba68-1f0353c7b3e6: Cave with Paleolithic pigment markings -- revealed in a 2021 paper. Art within its chambers pushes the story of early human creativity further back than previously documented in the region.
descriptions.aa90c7b3-4a88-4ea9-9ef2-4db7e5bba024: Paleolithic to Neolithic cave in the Mágina mountain range. Archaeological campaigns since 2015 found Middle Paleolithic remains — some of the earliest evidence of human presence in the region.
descriptions.d36f14bc-4d2d-46a0-bcc8-9940b16adc42: The only known prehistoric cave painting of its kind in this region, hidden near Knjazvac. Five surviving images link the end of the Bronze Age to the start of the Iron Age.
descriptions.043054e2-55c8-4b1a-8ad1-3f9092f0efea: Two prehistoric bison paintings survived here until a scouting association erased them during a graffiti-removal attempt. The act won the 1992 Ig Nobel Prize in Archaeology.
descriptions.1e9f1c86-dabd-4cf8-90f8-87c64a8ccc5c: Neolithic herding cave 630 metres above sea level on Naxos, occupied from Late Neolithic to Early Cycladic III. No crop residue found — archaeologists believe it served as a seasonal animal shelter.
descriptions.9ffa8a42-7b0a-4cd3-8b4f-5cb16c916a97: 1350 BC. A Torrean casteddu — circular stone tower — 12 metres across, built on a rocky outcrop by Bronze Age herders who brought the first farming techniques to the island.
descriptions.35fedad2-8a41-4fd4-8327-86fd30853551: Iron Age hillfort commanding the River Severn confluence at Caersws, orientated northeast-southwest along the hill's spine at 437 metres long. Its ramparts enclose around 6 hectares.
descriptions.c68277be-8cf6-431d-a95f-d5ac6ccbc3f3: La Tène Celtic settlement from 450 BC on a Weinviertel ridge, unfortified yet wealthy. Its scale and trade connections make it one of the most significant middle La Tène sites in Central Europe.
descriptions.7cd35ee0-c6fb-4215-a37f-ee5de2255a8f: Capital of the Carnutes on the Loire, stormed by Julius Caesar in 52 BC during the Gallic Wars. Locals who resisted Roman law faced massacres — the town was nearly wiped from the map.
descriptions.0b7f8fc6-0c2b-40c1-bfa2-f493afe1698a: Inca-era urban centre on the road to Machu Picchu, with massive polygonal retaining walls and three rock-outcrop shrines. Its precisely fitted masonry still stands beside the colonial church.
descriptions.1c53f8e7-180d-491c-aece-68cc625891e0: Neolithic site near Skopje that yielded a remarkable figurine known as the 'Adam' -- one of the earliest prehistoric male figurines ever found. A single clay figure, unique in this region.
descriptions.ac3877a0-04fc-4049-b918-ebf41b0a1501: Wari culture city from 350–1000 AD, remarkably preserved by desert air. Artefacts of the northern Wari tradition distinguish this coastal site from the Ayacucho heartland far to the south.
descriptions.89bdbe2c-a19b-484d-b6ef-2ed464b1311b: Maya ruins largely unexcavated in the Macal River catchment, positioned as a satellite site of Xunantunich. What lies beneath this jungle floor remains mostly untouched.
descriptions.9e91dedc-7e74-4056-8dcc-ad340cb8e92b: Continuously important for 3,500 years, this Swat River confluence site is littered with remains spanning the Bronze Age through medieval eras — a crossroads that every empire noticed.
descriptions.6053be26-eeb4-4e14-8d37-c4fef97a82d4: 5th–3rd century BC town in ancient Thessaly known only through its demonym — the name Chalai is extrapolated. Archaic and Classical pottery sherds mark where the city once stood.
descriptions.22a7c5e7-a5dd-46b3-a168-ab73f7cf77d4: Late Classic Maya highland site colonised from the lowlands around 700 AD. Chama developed a distinctive and short-lived ceramic style before its cultural tradition faded within a century.
descriptions.627ffcd0-ad25-4ff3-ae0d-5bc37d2053ef: Indus Valley city occupied 4000–1700 BC, the civilisation's centre for manufacturing carnelian beads. Three low mounds conceal a single 7-hectare settlement 130 kilometres south of Mohenjo-daro.
descriptions.a44a209e-67dd-4d92-b976-d6f601d3b8e5: 7th century BC chapel built by Kushite pharaohs Taharqa and Tantamani south of Karnak's Tenth Pylon. Their reliefs survive inside -- African rulers commemorated at the heart of ancient sacred ground.
descriptions.4faa104c-1f92-4968-aa85-ec1450813997: Rock painting site in the Andes above Cusco, spread across multiple named sectors on mountain slopes. The Llamachayuq Qaqa section is dominated by llama figures painted across an open cliff face.
descriptions.1941620d-0f59-46a3-9e13-d10e9c05cdfa: Inca-period archaeological site north of San Jeronimo in the Cusco Region, part of the pre-Columbian settlement network spread across the highland terrain.
descriptions.cb672d70-399c-4bf5-8032-3259832f53eb: Neolithic house near Kazanluk excavated using early flotation technology. Carbonised emmer, barley, and bitter vetch were found alongside post holes and a clay hearth — life frozen 8,000 years ago.
descriptions.e59377f7-18eb-459e-adc4-b9c40274ddfa: Stone chullpa tombs, walls, houses, and squares at 2,800 metres elevation in Carabaya Province. A highland community built in stone, set high on the Andean plateau.
descriptions.bdd4c703-8f60-419f-a2ef-d7181692d59f: 950-1200 AD Maya complex over 20 km² — only 3% open to visitors. Palaces and temples bear murals that possibly depict the Popol Vuh, the sacred Maya creation text.
descriptions.3de5129d-3b47-470f-b3c5-a60344eda4dd: 4th-century early Christian church with a Latin cross plan and varied apses, burials inside and out. Destroyed in the Carolingian era, rebuilt, current form dates to the 1600s.
descriptions.1e934cb8-9f3a-4536-9c9c-4656e031b680: Iron Age hillfort in Hampshire, excavated 1928. Ramparts so thoroughly levelled that 1960s houses now ring the site — original bank survives only in the eastern quadrant.
descriptions.fa7e3956-6d81-4cc4-95ce-80e2c06b9f7a: Neolithic stone tool workshops on Chimei Island, active 3,800-4,500 years ago. Three coastal village sites produced tools across the mid-Neolithic period of prehistoric Taiwan.
descriptions.c4446aa8-4d88-4d40-be5b-129bca6a68aa: 500-1000 AD site declared National Cultural Heritage in 2003. Chipaw Marka lies in the Ayacucho Region, Lucanas Province, Chipao District.
descriptions.c0686246-3b52-4218-85c3-9d7b8bf63ae7: Iron Age hillfort in Wiltshire, 2 hectares, levelled in 1931. 19th-century digs yielded ceramics, worked stone, animal bone, and human burials — now at Wiltshire Museum, Devizes.
descriptions.565a3dc3-f8a7-4d38-a672-17c57f9401e9: 2nd-century BC Gojoseon fortification near Pyongyang, crescent-shaped walls 3,450 m long, built in alternating soil, rock, and sand layers. A gilded crown dissolved in mercury was found here.
descriptions.c129ff07-ab55-4bae-8855-0628b14e6b46: 4th-century AD Koguryo mountain fortress on Mt. Jongbang, encircled by 12+ km of 6-metre stone walls. Rebuilt in 1632, sheer cliffs were cut steep on the outer face as natural defence.
descriptions.3842aca5-13d3-4166-80cf-92f8dac3514f: Wari site in the Cusco valley, active from 400 AD into the Colonial Period before abandonment around 1530 AD. Situated in Quispicanchi Province near the village and lake of Huacarpay.
descriptions.9845a5a2-4ecc-412f-8455-7e156e0cbb16: An Inca-era spring and water shrine on the outskirts of Cusco, part of the sacred landscape linking Pumamarka to Choquequirao. Puquio means natural spring
descriptions.df07f4a1-9e45-42ac-875e-372263d4f541: 1438-1530 AD Inca rock-cut cave site near Cusco. Chukimarka sits beside the ruins of Templo de la Luna and Salapunco — a tight cluster of Inca monuments.
descriptions.d449ef58-cccc-4975-aff8-083d69e809da: Neolithic-Bronze Age flint mine on the South Downs with ~36 shafts, active 4100-800 BC. Excavated 1932-1939 and 1945-1949 by John Pull; invisible on the ground but clear from the air.
descriptions.dc9fd8fe-77ad-439d-8374-2b5563c00b15: 8th-7th century BC tower on the Acropolis of Arpino, a key site for Megalithic Cyclopean wall architecture in southern Lazio. An educational display inside traces its full history.
descriptions.695ecfa5-bd4e-4e81-9a5c-8251127d724e: 2nd-century AD Roman castle reused by Byzantines, Arabs, and Akkoyunlus, built on a rocky limestone hill. All four sides ringed by a rock-cut defence ditch, with caves underneath.
descriptions.487d2c72-b4f0-4993-82a1-e096950e82ab: Megalithic site in West Java dated to 1000 BC. Cipari Archaeological Park in Kuningan Regency preserves stone monuments from one of Indonesia's documented prehistoric cultures.
descriptions.cf49332c-0a05-4ba7-bf4f-48a703ee7a1e: Built c. 100 AD by order of Fidus Macer on the Via de la Plata trade route. The only four-fronted tetrapylon arch in the Iberian Peninsula
descriptions.8aa48093-66ab-456b-bbd6-b2ba884d47ed: 6th century BC-1st century AD Pre-Columbian Maya city in the Petén Basin, peak population ~10,000. Located 40 km east of Tikal on a ridge above the Holmul River.
descriptions.a16a45df-5e26-47da-838d-e61f63826f21: Three Bronze Age Clava cairns near Aviemore, spanning the 3rd-1st millennium BC. The Delfour Stone Circle survives ruinously with one striking stone still upright.
descriptions.6497dda4-f24a-40fa-92b5-85b16554d2fe: 1st century BC-5th century AD Roman sewer on the island of Capri, still visible at Marina Grande. It drained much of the northern island; its gradient was reversed at some unknown point.
descriptions.0fc900b2-23a7-4664-ac47-0bce2852babf: Limestone cave along the Snowy River gorge with Aboriginal deposits from 15,000 BC. The roof is blackened by ancient campfires; a passage leads to a cathedral-ceilinged inner chamber.
descriptions.dc38ed07-f75e-4d92-b932-cd8275b35a09: One of Devon's largest Early Iron Age hillforts at 210 m above the coast. Clovelly Dykes covers 8+ hectares in a complex of multiple earthwork banks and ditches across the plateau.
descriptions.6880170a-df11-4dbf-8c6c-02aa4e39ec7b: 1st-century AD Roman city at Feldkirch on the Tabula Peutingeriana, a waystation between Brigantium and Milan. Geophysics in 1998 confirmed it was Vorarlberg's second largest Roman settlement.
descriptions.300d302c-f6fd-4688-b21a-a8189bf53995: Built c. 1350–1450 AD by Túpac Inca Yupanqui at 2,800 m elevation as an administrative hub to control the Chachapoya people. Rectangular Inca structures overlie earlier circular Chachapoya forms.
descriptions.0286a741-77f2-4148-8e62-487041920281: Inca hilltop mound overlooking the Cusco valley. Name means 'lake-terrace' in Quechua. Terraced slopes and stone foundations survive, largely unexcavated — one of Cusco's least-visited Inca sites.
descriptions.54a9488b-698d-4c49-94a4-c50dd43847fe: One of the earliest Maya sites, occupied 3400 BC-1300 AD — spanning the full arc of Maya civilisation. A specialist tool-production centre supplying tools across the northern Maya lowlands.
descriptions.bf43132d-1cbc-4dd2-9cf9-914a917e78d9: Site at 2,970 m on a mountain called Coyor in the Cajamarca Region, east of Lake San Nicolas. Collor sits in the northern Andes at a height of nearly 3,000 metres.
descriptions.03ebb1eb-834c-46f9-a038-9231d40f8072: A Phoenician rock-cut columbarium over 1,000 years old, carved directly into the cliffside. Discovered in Ribeira dos Bispos, it shows Phoenician funerary presence on the Atlantic coast.
descriptions.a511e195-58d5-40e8-af84-baa83518f5e8: Ruins of a Roman city with a rock-cut tomb reached by 18 steps, entrance carved as a low arch with a Medusa head inside. Necropolis preserves Ionic temple remains and eagle-motif sarcophagi.
descriptions.c9358837-e3ee-4daa-aedc-34e45afa1692: Linear earthwork on Charlton Down in Dorset, once 6.4 km long, dated 800 BC-4th century AD. Combs Ditch forms the boundary between several parishes — its bank still visible after 2,000 years.
descriptions.a248f085-788e-4bda-9e22-77af77edd258: Augustan-era temple remains inside a Roman provincial forum. Modeled on the Aedes Concordiae Augustae in Rome, its columns broadcast imperial authority across Hispania during the 1st century BC.
descriptions.132d4298-f6ef-4099-b360-a80ea4202afa: Chavín culture archaeological zone in the Cajamarca region, dated to 1000 BC. Condorcaga is also a natural viewpoint; rock formations crown the upper part of the mountain.
descriptions.b5899722-5118-41e0-8324-5da705ace4a2: Small multivallate Iron Age hillfort in Somerset, triangular, 0.8 km south of Portbury near Bristol. A 0.9-metre bank survives on the south-western side of this Scheduled Monument.
descriptions.5b74783d-882a-4cc7-a2df-857b5a00c454: Occupied 600 BC-750 AD and again 1000-16th century AD. A ball court and two temples uncovered so far; a clifftop lookout held a stone possibly used for sacrifices — excavations ongoing.
descriptions.2101b2c7-9dd5-4dbf-b140-9c24ae364da8: Neolithic coastal settlement on the Gargano peninsula, human presence 7th-5th millennium BC. Occupied into the Bronze Age, it sat on a coastal lagoon with easy sea access and rich resources.
descriptions.79f94fa1-4d25-4181-a0da-3fa7d794bdbc: Ancient Cretan town on the northwestern peninsula cited by Ptolemy and Juvenal. When the Florentine traveller Buondelmonti visited in 1415, he found remains still standing.
descriptions.20278c61-19b0-4712-a808-418cab607b25: 4300-2500 BC Neolithic site on Blue Bell Hill preserving a lost group of Sarsen stones — possibly a chambered long barrow and one of the Medway megaliths. Identified 1951, excavated 1982.
descriptions.0e942695-743b-4144-bf9f-f5687fc61447: 4th-millennium BC causewayed enclosure in West Sussex, built 3700-3300 BC. Identified 1951, excavated 1982 — whether it was a settlement, meeting place, or ritual site remains unknown.
descriptions.8ef67a96-2590-4382-b575-4a15f7c468fe: Karst cave near Oliva where the most complete Neanderthal skeleton ever found on the Iberian Peninsula was excavated in 2010. Archaeological work has continued here since 1977.
descriptions.7279cb69-c5d2-4b9b-b307-96ef43164e7f: Sealed since 3000–2500 BC and undisturbed until 1998. Three cloverleaf cells of drystone masonry, under 1 m tall. Only disarticulated bones survived
descriptions.56f32f70-ee56-4778-a3b3-d490a482f6c8: Neolithic or Early Bronze Age ring cairn on the uplands near Cras, Wales — one of a cluster of burial monuments marking a landscape used for ceremony from around 4000 BC.
descriptions.7bab6020-97a0-46a2-9d2b-a8f7d00332f7: Neolithic or Early Bronze Age round cairn near Cras, Wales — part of a hilltop burial cluster. Stone-built mound marking a funerary landscape active from around 4000 BC.
descriptions.acfdb5fb-0c3b-436e-811e-cd2385a0d203: Neolithic or Early Bronze Age round cairn sited north of the Cras round cairn — one of at least three burial monuments forming a ceremonial cluster on the Welsh uplands, c. 4000 BC.
descriptions.4f89dada-27a0-4c49-bc79-5fc5ef812766: 4th-century BC monument at Delphi built by Craterus, Alexander's general, attributed to Lysippos. A 15 x 6.35 m building between the Temple of Apollo and the theatre.
descriptions.72cd16e3-8fc7-49a6-8f6d-efc56c40508d: Forty-two Bronze Age barrows, cairns, and clearance cairns on a Weardale moorland slope, active 2500-800 BC. The clearance cairns indicate land was being opened for agriculture at the upland margin.
descriptions.3329c7e1-5714-4e5f-b101-21c35f905e9e: One of the most ancient cities of Greece in Phocis, 2nd-1st millennium BC. Per the Homeric Hymn to Apollo, Crissa was founded by Cretans led by Apollo — chosen to be his priests at Pytho.
descriptions.bc85d3d5-a47e-4c4d-be70-aaa1c18915d1: 5th-millennium BC Vinča culture settlement near Belgrade. Research since 1962 gives unprecedented scope to study an uninterrupted Neolithic occupation; declared a cultural monument in 2014.
descriptions.217b6292-d8ee-403b-a8ad-236304ac481d: Two sets of human footprints in the Cuatrociénegas Basin, dated to 10,550 and 7,240 years ago. The older is the earliest known in Mexico; the younger forms a trackway of 11 in-situ prints.
descriptions.9e82a4ae-0ef3-4f0f-a1a9-965aa94e55da: Rock painting site in the Yauyos Province near lakes Mullucocha and La Escalera in the Lima Region. Cuchi Machay's images survive in a remote Andean highland setting.
descriptions.d6fabe8c-061f-4885-8e02-cc6276c6f23c: Palaeontological claypan on an ancient lake bed with the first unequivocal evidence of megafauna-human coexistence in Australia. Fossils survived because the lake refills and dries slowly after rain.
descriptions.4d9739d5-0517-4d26-a66c-d668e20f745a: 1200 BC Maya farming village with a long occupational history. Inhabitants built on plaster-coated platforms around central patios. A steam bath dated ~900 BC is the oldest known in the Maya lowlands.
descriptions.9110faff-beed-40af-b688-354c57fa97d3: ~1425 AD cliff hamlet built into a canyon wall in Durango, once home to the Xiximes tribe. Cueva del Maguey is one of the region's most striking examples of pre-contact cliff-dwelling architecture.
descriptions.a5e8bcfc-012b-4e7f-b3ee-906891955899: Iron Age hillfort on a promontory above the River Yeo near Loxhore in Devon at ~110 m elevation, commanding views over the valley.
descriptions.d0fafe30-c48a-4939-8e97-af0ff2a10689: Cup and ring marks on natural rock at Achnabreck, Cairnbaan, Ballygowan, and Baluachraig — among Scotland's most impressive decorated rock surfaces. Carved 4th-2nd millennium BC, purpose unknown.
descriptions.0dcce77c-ef2f-481b-8069-ad5818b26aaa: Iron Age univallate hillfort in West Somerset, nearly destroyed by quarrying. What remains of Curdon Camp still stands 2.5 metres high on the southern and western sides — a Scheduled Monument.
descriptions.09b07712-628c-4c14-bf87-62c586f1ced3: Bronze Age settlement on the Levie plateau, 3000–1500 BC. Part of Corsica's Torre culture — builders of granite tower-fortresses. Yielded atypical pottery now housed in the Alta Rocca Museum.
descriptions.8442fc68-e408-4b2f-9aad-a5f42139685e: 5th-millennium BC Indus Civilisation trading post in Balochistan, mound 457 m across — a major regional centre. Finds include stone beads, copper pieces, and figurines with Harappan connections.
descriptions.1a85971c-56a9-411e-bfa9-eda3004219a5: 3500 BC-500 AD multi-period site in the Nam River valley, home to one of the earliest ditch-enclosed settlements in East Asia. Daepyeong spans 4,000+ years, making it critical to Korean prehistory.
descriptions.e7ab9b35-e0bb-4fe4-a1cb-fbe5a17c63d6: Iron Age settlement in southwest Jutland, 500 BC-800 AD. Excavations 1965-70 found 4th-5th century AD houses, making Dankirke one of Denmark's earliest documented urban centres.
descriptions.7c5cfb65-93b9-4f0b-ba6f-c998b5cd460f: 1st-century AD Roman military frontier along the Danube through Bavaria, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, and Romania. The line shifted north or south with Roman conquest.
descriptions.049c8637-f2b9-4d6c-ad6d-5fa0ab23e1e3: 1st-century BC Dacian town in Moesia between the Danube and Balkan Mountains, in the corridor between Nicopolis and Abritus. Part of the Dacian urban network before Roman conquest of the region.
descriptions.0f42edd7-0a93-46bd-a65c-9382e076fac9: 2nd-century BC multi-layer site at the confluence of the eastern and western Prone rivers. Spans from Acheulean tools and Bronze Age burials to a 2nd-1st century BC religious complex.
descriptions.6aa4c8de-3794-42fe-b68e-6b6ab77bd8ed: 5th-century BC temple of Apollo Delphinios at Miletus, protector of ports and ships. The rectangular temenos stands mostly intact, preserving a stone altar with volute acroteria.
descriptions.30f619e1-3e2d-4b40-9c9b-49eda0590995: 2050-1750 BC pre-Inuit site at the head of Jørgen Brønlund Fjord in northern Greenland, discovered 1948 by Eigil Knuth. One of the largest sites in Peary Land, with Independence I culture features.
descriptions.92424ead-7e63-40d3-8796-76f8ef82ae86: Six Roman-era mausoleums line an ancient road near Silifke. The Twin Mausoleums blend Corinthian columns with eastern styling — sarcophagi were found inside both multi-storey towers.
descriptions.1d7cca0c-fb61-4b09-8692-52781474ed3e: 3rd-7th century AD rock-cut caves at Dhank village in calcareous sandstone. The Jain cave holds figures of Adinath, Shantinath, and Pārśva — earliest Jain sculptures in Kathiawad.
descriptions.142eecf9-2327-40c2-87ac-4b0f7445bb30: One of the oldest sites in West Africa, occupied 2500-500 BC along Saharan sandstone cliffs. Dhar Tichitt is one of four Tichitt culture sites, key to understanding early sub-Saharan farming.
descriptions.8ecc6f04-cd18-4293-869d-8a0bd537aa65: Dilmun-period burial mound field in Bahrain's Northern Governorate, dating to the 3rd millennium BC. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019 as part of the Dilmun Burial Mounds.
descriptions.d8c32771-f319-4432-9333-aa646e273001: 4th-century BC Illyrian hilltop city 450 m above the Adriatic, in the territory of the Parthini tribe. Dimale peaked in the Hellenistic period before passing to Macedonian, then Roman control.
descriptions.db9de243-cfb1-43ad-941a-66e656681236: Iron Age hillfort on a Gwynedd cliff so eroded by the sea that only a double semi-circular rampart survives. Roman pottery shows Dinas Dinlle was occupied well into the Roman period.
descriptions.52bee5c8-1689-4b47-b5e3-e416e2bfd919: 2nd-3rd century BC Iron Age hillfort in Glamorgan, built in two phases: northern main fort and Southern Banks added later. One of thousands of British hillforts, its exact purpose remains debated.
descriptions.b2cb59ca-a7ed-4cc6-be6b-7cf1b95791e5: Iron Age univallate hillfort south of Churchill in Somerset, encircled by a 2-3 m scarp and a fosse. Dinghurst Fort has yielded bones, rings, and weapons — direct traces of its inhabitants.
descriptions.db4bbdf7-ca01-419d-ba8c-038520196c2c: Iron Age univallate hillfort in Somerset's Mendip district, later reused as a Medieval enclosure. Dinies Camp sits on an earlier earthwork, layering multiple periods onto one strategic hilltop.
descriptions.59b08d5d-d319-43da-9607-2b0138c4dc1b: 5th-3rd millennium BC settlement on the Sharur plain, left bank of the Arpachay River. The Ovchular tepesi mound sits at a crossroads of ancient routes linking the South Caucasus to Mesopotamia.
descriptions.afbbd0e7-ca10-4aa7-942f-7d1293e3e79e: 550 BC Achaemenid rock-cut tomb carved into a mountainside 3 km from Sar Pol-e-Zahab — one of the most important rock-cut tombs in the region.
descriptions.8ac446bf-0be4-4e16-b471-010717a3445d: 5th-millennium BC rock-cut tomb known as the "painted tomb" and the Queen of the Domus de Janas. Features a double-sloped roof, carved columns, and trachyte symbols from a prehistoric funerary cult.
descriptions.6cf0f76b-6f95-411c-b94b-7a1133429ea6: 1200 BC multivallate Iron Age hillfort on Drakelow Hill at the southern tip of Kinver Edge in Worcestershire. A commanding promontory above the lowland — a Scheduled Monument.
descriptions.ce64147f-624e-474d-92af-b6e84001d54d: 4th-7th century AD Iron Age broch on the island of Barra with two distinct occupation phases centuries apart. Dun Cuier is considered complex and controversial — one of Scotland's most debated brochs.
descriptions.8a87a57e-4e29-42e7-9dca-08f3c6c16539: Iron Age hillfort in Dorset enclosing 3.6 hectares, with a rampart 7 m wide and an external ditch 13 m wide. Active 2nd millennium BC into the 1st century AD — a Scheduled Monument on a low hill.
descriptions.46838746-5160-40bb-a0e7-5bb88bd33db9: 400 BC-1000 AD Maya site partly buried under a modern town. Main Palace blends Chenes decorated facades with Rio Bec design; ceramics push its origins back to the Middle Preclassic period.
descriptions.7cabe5b9-0710-4205-a52a-55f3b4003896: 1st-century AD Roman house within the Paphos Archaeological Park in Cyprus. Foundations and floor plans preserved from one of the island's imperial-era urban developments.
descriptions.f35475c3-21c3-4cfe-9226-887e38b7d0ec: 2nd-century AD Roman villa in Kent, nearly 112 m long with 135+ identified rooms. Abandoned in the 4th century and demolished in the 13th to build Aylesford Priory on the east Medway slope.
descriptions.d2cffaa4-e1cb-4b2e-9907-76abf47411d1: 2670-2610 BC step pyramid south of Edfu, one of seven near-identical small pyramids built far from Egypt's main centres. Builders and purpose remain essentially unknown.
descriptions.5f478ce8-5cb2-4a8f-bd80-95f64bae677a: Assyrian castle with tunnels carved into rock and royal tombs in an area called the King Cemeteries. Eğil Kalesi has functioned as a fortification across thousands of years.
descriptions.46243017-7de4-4851-8742-5061bc856904: 1200 BC-1st century AD Iron Age hillfort in Somerset with a triple bank on the north and double out-turned bank on the south. Elborough Hill is an oval univallate fort between Hutton and Elborough.
descriptions.bc308dd3-8a3b-47b5-bb19-84b08ddfb193: Zapotec temple precinct in Oaxaca dating from about 300 BC. El Palenque is an ancient village or settlement at the heart of the Oaxacan highland region.
descriptions.4a4937bf-ef17-43d7-b7c4-28afa1b0f230: 500 BC-800 AD Maya city-state capital known as Waka', 60 km west of Tikal near the San Pedro River. El Perú controlled a strategic Petén corridor and held political ties to major Classic-era powers.
descriptions.bdbce80c-eee9-4842-800a-1cf3e440c500: 250-950 AD ruined Maya Classic city in Petén, its original name lost. El Porvenir is the modern name for a pre-Columbian Maya site in the Petén department.
descriptions.acec1746-35a0-4d0e-be03-1d240bad074c: 600-909 AD Maya settlement in Petén with three groups of platforms on a north-south axis. Group A's pyramid stands over 10 m tall in a wooded hilltop — largely unexcavated.
descriptions.35da8e0f-6bf0-43c8-bce4-3ebda143277a: 500 BC-16th century AD capital of the Acalanes province, named Itzamkanac — "Place of the Iguana/Crocodile House" in Chontal Maya. Two plazas, four large structures, and a ball court form its core.
descriptions.fb56e557-87f8-4675-881f-a6f8c0885649: A Neolithic enclosed hut circle settlement set in marshy upland ground. Two round houses roughly 9 m across survive as grass-covered stone banks, part of a wider field system dating to the 5th–4th.
descriptions.0be2f25c-0545-4329-b65e-fcd3c29ff85d: Occupied since the Early Neolithic ~4000 BC, Endebjerg on Samsø has yielded pithouses, longhouse post holes, and evidence of multiple cultural phases across thousands of years.
descriptions.0999c397-1333-4ff3-aa26-fe854f46de9c: 16th-12th century BC Bronze Age trading city, possibly the capital of Alasiya. Enkomi was an important centre for copper with strong ties to Ugarit — settled near a sea inlet now completely silted up.
descriptions.dcda1568-0730-4cba-a9ce-c50c80ed941d: 16th-12th century BC Bronze Age city, likely capital of Alasiya, with copper smelted on-site and traded across the eastern Mediterranean. Enkomi had deep cultural ties to Ugarit in Syria.
descriptions.eb379653-acb9-464d-af06-a0c15a7d6304: Founded 6th century BC as a Greek colony, renamed Epidaurum under Rome in 228 BC. Now Cavtat, 15 km south of Dubrovnik; besieged in Caesar's civil war but saved by consul Publius Vatinius.
descriptions.5cd47e05-c322-4510-b40f-c1f75072c147: 5400 BC Sumerian city — believed the earliest in southern Mesopotamia. Buildings of mud brick were stacked atop one another as temples grew upward and the village expanded outward.
descriptions.3e483113-87b4-4219-86ef-cd56a034f8c8: Roman gravity dam built c. 50 BC–AD 66, enlarged to 16.8 m tall and 87 m long by AD 206. Ranked fifth-tallest in Iberia and seventh in the entire Roman Empire.
descriptions.9f230ad4-cb35-4ba9-8552-ba1e4b4fae40: The world's earliest known multiple arch dam, 1st century AD: 320 m long, 5.6 m high, with 12 buttresses spaced 8.6 m apart. The curved wall arching between buttresses was a Roman engineering first.
descriptions.5fffbfc9-f83c-4cd3-9b8d-d2570ce63dbd: Likely the Paeonian royal capital, in a region occupied 5th-4th centuries BC by tribes along the Axius basin. Štip preserves Paeonian and Roman urban layers in its ancient core.
descriptions.20851f57-93d5-4643-81ea-60aba5b58d9c: 14th century BC-323 BC ziggurat to Marduk in ancient Babylon, sometimes identified with the Tower of Babel — a link archaeologists reject. Now in ruins 90 km south of Baghdad.
descriptions.45a26f12-c56f-4ebb-bc65-ba9488b84826: 7th-6th century BC Etruscan altar carved from a single volcanic block, used by haruspices for divination. Surrounded by Etruscan inscriptions, tombs, medieval ruins, and a tower linked to Pasolini.
descriptions.94c02471-3aaa-4736-84e6-a1b52bc7e23b: 1st-millennium BC Arcadian settlement mentioned by Pausanias, who recorded a sanctuary in the Tanos valley. Eva lay between Astros and Kato Doliana, near the Monastery of Loukou.
descriptions.865d8fa5-a3a9-4084-8a07-a91813583263: 4th-century BC bronze statue group at Delphi, dedicated by the Arcadians after 369 BC. The oblong Sacred Way base honoured their victorious campaign in Laconia together with the Thebans.
descriptions.ac25c4c9-451a-4e9e-a06b-df4e34e8e457: 3rd-2nd century BC Attalid monument at the top of Delphi's Sacred Way. Hellenistic kings competed in bronze and stone here — the Attalids of Pergamon claimed the prime position near Apollo's temple.
descriptions.dc833106-7100-474e-8f39-c3f74b8a9d44: 405 BC Spartan victory monument at Delphi after Aegospotami. Bronze figures of Castor, Pollux, Zeus, Apollo, Artemis, and Lysander receiving a wreath from Poseidon — divine sanction for Sparta.
descriptions.8c532808-61b4-4d36-ae73-0e1c6ad05982: 5th-century BC bronze ex voto by Tarentum at Delphi, marking victory over the Messapians. First monument on the Sacred Way — a statement of Italian Greek military pride beside the Polygonal Wall.
descriptions.acc0d56c-1803-43c4-a5c6-b7c8c217c8f1: 4th-century BC Argive dedications at Delphi — a semicircular pedestal after 369 BC celebrating their role founding Messene alongside the Thebans. Multiple Argive ex votos lined the Sacred Way.
descriptions.05afa876-bd9b-4285-8aa3-cb1f71fb3707: 4th-3rd millennium BC settlement in Nakhchivan, a 0.8-hectare mound near the Araz River. Ɗrəbyengicə sits at a crossroads of ancient routes linking the South Caucasus to Mesopotamia.
descriptions.cb637b1a-4f1b-4856-815f-67f2424a717f: 700-1200 AD Polynesian site on Huahine, waterlogged enough to preserve wooden patu clubs, canoe parts, and adze handles — rare organic artefacts in Polynesian archaeology.
descriptions.6933ea78-a024-455d-981e-fe4c09dfad75: 13th-century BC Hittite colossus of Storm-God Tarhun, 8 m tall and ~70 tons in basalt. Found near its quarry, never delivered — some sections still rough, frozen mid-creation for 3,000 years.
descriptions.c8e0a91d-298d-40f1-aef8-f8503e44b05a: 1st-century AD Roman road, 39 km across the Fens from Denver, Norfolk to Peterborough. Fen Causeway linked East Anglia to the north and west, joining Ermine Street at its western end.
descriptions.9ca828d9-f880-4675-b304-0718ddce9010: 1st-century BC Roman theatre built on a natural hillside slope, still in use through the 7th century AD — over 700 years of continuous performance on the same stage.
descriptions.fee01523-1686-437c-97ef-9e3566fba1c3: Bronze Age round cairn on Craig y Llyn's plateau edge, sited for maximum northern views. Excavated from beneath its stones were two cist burials, a jet necklace, and a decorated bowl.
descriptions.027622e9-b85c-454a-a5ac-4703b26575bd: A cairn raised before 4500 BC, its builders left no name, no script — only stone piled on stone on an upland plateau, looking out across ancient valleys.
descriptions.77b9b433-376a-468e-8af3-13197a31ed28: Earthwork enclosure older than 4500 BC, raised on an upland plateau before metal or writing existed. One of the earliest traces of deliberate human landscape-making in the region.
descriptions.58a2be59-ec1e-4667-96b9-3313ce406bc1: Ancient Pyrenean spring used by horses, villagers, and muleteers on the main road between Seu d'Urgell and the capital. The street it sits on was once called Knights' Street.
descriptions.3ff2ae0e-9095-48ed-a45e-0d8c9f455527: Built 1641–1648 as part of the fortress complex defending Elvas, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. One of the most complete surviving examples of Vauban-era star-fort military engineering.
descriptions.4a049415-9283-41e6-8428-11275c0aecfe: 2nd–3rd century AD funerary temple with a six-columned Corinthian portico leading to underground burial chambers. Elaborate stone grapevines and floral carvings still frame the entrance.
descriptions.cde70126-4a96-4d67-aba4-bd453c55f78e: Middle Neolithic settlement 3,700 years old, giving rise to the named Fushan Culture. Discovered in 1997 and split into two excavation zones — a key site for understanding island prehistory.
descriptions.bc46a23e-737f-4dd8-adfc-8c83317edb75: Celtic Iron Age hillfort near Trellech, occupied from around 800 BC through the Roman period. One of nearly 600 hillforts once believed to have existed in the region — far fewer remain today.
descriptions.7aee6833-f789-49f0-8643-afa9830e90ce: Around 2500 BC, Ganweriwala was one of the Indus Valley's largest cities — yet it remains unexcavated. Surface finds include unicorn figurines and copper seals from its buried streets.
descriptions.879a16b1-ba54-49c0-8b61-6a9265f23758: Built 47–44 BC, this gate bears a carved head of Hercules with beard, curly hair, and club. A critical inscription naming officials Piso and Cassius Longinus has been badly damaged.
descriptions.9a669e25-6ea4-450a-ae37-b816f9d64b53: 5th-century BC fortification on Thasos blending Macedonian, funerary, and palatial architecture — an unusual fusion for a gateway dedicated jointly to Zeus and Hera.
descriptions.559a729a-01e4-4161-bdc6-730494fb785b: A 2nd-century AD tomb of unique design — no similar form exists in Pisidia, Lycia, or Phrygia. Two monuments cut from the rock: one triangular-roofed, one flat-roofed, both with reliefs.
descriptions.29651376-c3fa-484e-b3bd-a6a64e97d0c6: Hittite Empire rock carvings depicting three deities in pointed horned hats — signs of divinity. Two armed male figures with swords stride toward a seated goddess on a natural hilltop.
descriptions.b8b9361e-c77d-4e15-b383-04b7aae6927f: 1st–6th century Roman villa in Norfolk, uncovered by ploughing in 1922. Aerial surveys in the 1970s revealed a detached bathhouse and boundary ditches — most still lies underground.
descriptions.83d0776b-8f10-4009-85f3-842a03cb9c30: Alleged megalithic temple on a submerged plateau 2 km off St. Julian's coast, spotted in 1999. Archaeologists remain unconvinced — the 900 by 500 metre shelf may be entirely natural.
descriptions.b3bf097d-fd5d-4473-ab81-ac180e197fd4: 6th-century BC city described by Herodotus as a place where Greeks among the Budini spoke a mixed Scythian-Greek tongue. Possibly identified as the vast Bilsk hillfort near Poltava.
descriptions.45fcb351-64fb-488a-ab19-35741221bf81: 1st-century AD Roman frontier fort on the Sahara's edge, 5 km southwest of modern M'Lili. Evidence suggests a pre-Roman Berber fortification already stood on the same strategic desert site.
descriptions.07c6a59d-7cb0-469b-936c-3bb984dc30a5: 3rd-century BC Thracian burial complex near Sveshtari, where one tomb is linked to Cothelas, king of the Getae. Just metres from this site stands the world-heritage Tomb of Sveshtari.
descriptions.c6a4851c-3ff8-4e60-8744-356cb4040ba1: Northernmost cairn in Kilmartin Glen's Bronze Age linear cemetery. Excavated in 1864, two cist burials were found beneath concentric stone circles — one held a jet necklace and a decorated bowl.
descriptions.180e049b-1586-4a75-8e85-8d771fe7ba69: 4000 BC Cucuteni-Trypillia proto-city covering 132 hectares — vast for its era. One of 2,440 such mega-settlements discovered across the region, suggesting a forgotten early urban tradition.
descriptions.5f3d80f4-5f79-4dfc-b40f-4583a46d316d: Ruins featuring a stone arch, grooved masonry blocks, and architectural fragments of unknown date. The scale of the stonework suggests a substantial ancient structure once stood on this site.
descriptions.64cf6ee2-708e-47c4-a2a6-0ec195d4917e: Bronze Age stone circle on Bodmin Moor, 32.3 metres across — almost exactly 39 Megalithic Yards. Originally 28 stones; 23 still stand atop Shepherd's Hill at 306 metres elevation.
descriptions.1bc69a3e-2ded-4f53-b96e-38811edee56a: Bronze Age settlement on the Araz River, dated 3rd–2nd century BC. Excavations in 1936 and 1967–75 unearthed stone tools, polychrome ceramics, and stone tombs before it grew into a town.
descriptions.94895e29-08e0-45a0-a0c6-8a2417974d42: 5th–14th century walled stronghold with round and square towers, built in the Sasanid period to repel Khazar raids — and later demolished in the Timurid invasion centuries after.
descriptions.1e3e3665-7232-4c54-bceb-9973db4af1e5: Iron Age oval hillfort in Somerset, 270 metres long with a ditch up to 10 metres wide and 2.2 metres deep. A second defensive bank lines the northern and western perimeter.
descriptions.92823e94-ee73-489e-8bab-9ab0e6f3b183: Thirteen granite thrones in two rows at Axum, attributed to twelve judges or early Christian missionaries. The same ceremonial seats were later incorporated into royal coronation rituals.
descriptions.19aa5815-9965-43b3-a2d9-e35190fd50ec: Hundreds of round stone structures spread across 207 square kilometres of Andean cloud forest, claimed as a pre-Columbian Chachapoyas city. The identification remains disputed among historians.
descriptions.6e8d1700-3e9f-4b82-a538-2b77154374d5: 900–1470 AD Chachapoyan complex in the Utcubamba Valley with 15–30 major sites and hundreds of smaller ruins — named the Stairs, the Bishop, the Secret, and a dozen more.
descriptions.2cabda2f-f7d3-4cc4-8346-7afcff7babcf: Built 1353–1336 BC as the main temple of the sun-disc god Aten during Akhenaten's religious revolution. Located in his purpose-built capital Akhetaten, abandoned within a generation.
descriptions.6a55e68c-c08a-4c76-8685-fc501bbc0857: 700 BC tower in the Sabaean style. Rededicated as a Christian church possibly by the 6th century AD — its reuse preserved it for 2,700 years. Considered the oldest standing structure of its kind.
descriptions.b1cb10c0-1b83-4b04-90b0-0bc8fdf946fb: Iron Age promontory fort on Pembrokeshire's south coast, defended by sandstone cliffs on two sides and terraced slopes to the north. Covers 1.8 hectares; now a National Trust scheduled monument.
descriptions.dac9b6e1-a54d-4b9a-b400-5fa295ba2040: Around 4500 BC, Aboriginal people buried their dead in the Maribyrnong Valley terraces. Unearthed during 1960s soil quarrying, this is among the oldest burial sites recorded on the continent.
descriptions.9299ee5a-03c7-415b-a8d2-b8a7b8c71a7e: Iron Age hill fort on a Dart Estuary promontory, 65–80 metres above the sea. Also known as Noss, it commanded sweeping river-mouth views — a natural lookout as much as a fortress.
descriptions.53058d01-7e64-49c7-8dec-2b352a0e9ec6: Stone circle raised before 4300 BC, toppled by a farmer in 1820, re-erected in 1949 just 600 metres from Sellafield. Ten of twelve original stones still stand near the Cumbrian coast.
descriptions.28d08d27-d959-42d0-922c-8e91c795d432: Shaft tomb from 1450 BC near ancient Pylos, unearthed in 2015 with 1,400 intact objects — weapons, jewels, and carved gems beside a warrior skeleton. Among the greatest Bronze Age finds in decades.
descriptions.042d5e49-f491-4b38-9c67-888b9cd39535: 1st-century Romano-British settlement in Warwickshire with a ritual core: a circular wooden Iron Age temple later replaced by two phases of Roman stone temples, plus a bathhouse and ovens.
descriptions.20f1479a-f1f8-46ce-b3a3-05a71847097e: Archaeological site in the commune of Luri, Haute-Corse. Its period and full extent remain unstudied — one of many island sites awaiting proper excavation.
descriptions.fab3989d-2c06-40cc-9d22-c7fb58e5e94f: Cave with parietal art in a limestone massif, occupied from at least 6000 BC. Carbon-14 dating confirmed multiple distinct occupation layers — among the oldest recorded sites in the wider region.
descriptions.0d801018-7183-44a3-97e4-136aa8a374ce: Hilltop settlement northwest of Pallanchacra at 3,167 metres in Pasco Region. Its high-altitude position and commanding views suggest a role in controlling the surrounding Andean valleys.
descriptions.922d8301-02e3-4e2f-946b-3e217fc78307: 2nd-century Buddhist stupa in the Kandag Valley of Gandhara, ruins scattered across 1,500 by 1,000 metres. Partially excavated in 2011, the main plinth measures 17 metres on each side.
descriptions.902d16b9-2e5e-47a0-8782-8dbf99d54b38: 4th-century open-air archaeological complex still being excavated, where mosaics depicting human figures, animals, and fruit were uncovered from the floors of an ancient church.
descriptions.fe61c9c4-97dc-4478-93f8-5cd4a44d8ec2: Fort guarding the Mawal-to-Kalyan trade route through Naneghat Pass, 2nd century BC. The entire structure — gate, sentry rooms, water cisterns, and a rock-cut temple — carved from a single rock face.
descriptions.22dba69d-525f-4b01-9fb7-a8db7036bb0e: Neolithic site near Jambol occupied from the 6th to 3rd millennium BC, where polished stone tools from the Late Neolithic period were found — a rare window into early prehistoric life in the region.
descriptions.b3ebbc47-7624-4ef9-9f6f-bc03eab227f5: Roman-era monument carved into a limestone cliff, compared by archaeologists to structures at Petra. Local legend holds that a mirror once reflected sunlight from the cliff face down into the village.
descriptions.73577152-2aef-4a45-9668-b0404238695b: Ancient Locrian town on the Opuntian Gulf, noted by Pausanias and Strabo. It likely took its name from nearby salt springs — ruins survive near the modern village of Theologos.
descriptions.af1d02d6-bf17-4ce3-bf83-92bb82b8401a: Megalithic temple from 3600–3200 BC with five semi-rectangular rooms in massive stone walls. Built during the Ggantija phase, just 1 km from the Tas-Silg multi-period sanctuary.
descriptions.ba1d0bf4-260a-467e-adaa-2a53d13745aa: 4th-century BC circular ritual space near Apollo's temple at Delphi, where ceremonies re-enacted the killing of the Python — the mythological shift from chthonic to Olympian religion.
descriptions.f1a0b11e-e382-42dd-bfdd-4116409af9ca: Early Christian catacombs at Gudja with carvings so unusual they provoke debate: some historians classify them as paleochristian; others question whether the Christian markers are conclusive.
descriptions.f0059dda-0b8c-4743-91ce-07d50c56ce1a: 3rd–4th century Roman shrine to Zeus with sixteen pillars around a square altar, later reused as a Christian church. Architrave inscriptions survive; the temple was remodelled multiple times.
descriptions.e8904b19-6c54-4560-8438-35ea9fbe8e8d: Roman Iron Age cemetery east of Herning, dated 200–400 AD. Grave 83 yielded only a preserved complex hairstyle — the elaborate coiffure of a young woman archaeologists named the Hammerum Girl.
descriptions.9977d351-4c1a-465f-8928-f84c3a67248f: Remnants of a small underground city beneath the town of Han. The tunnels are poorly maintained and difficult to access — much of what lies below remains unexplored.
descriptions.4c05611f-65b3-4481-a43d-f64e839e0c48: A 4 by 1.5 metre rock relief of the Haron Hell Boatman — ferryman of the dead — set within a natural cave that was later converted into a Christian church, blending pagan and sacred space.
descriptions.18395123-85fc-4c51-b479-1933bfc00aae: One of the most important cities of northern Mesopotamia for 5,000 years. Harran's ruins span Bronze Age foundations through the medieval period, revealing continuous deep occupation.
descriptions.4fe33206-24d7-4d57-9bde-670139eed9cb: Around 2000 BC, a burial ground was established near present-day Sunderland. Excavated in 1911, the cists held prehistoric human remains — the site now buried under a post-war housing estate.
descriptions.5c6a72eb-0584-45d0-9fe7-fdfad15b632f: 1st-century AD Roman rock-cut tomb necropolis on Gelinler Mountain. Most tombs were destroyed before formal study — what little survives hints at a once-extensive hillside burial ground.
descriptions.1db67c2f-5523-4e2c-a953-2824a7cb25ff: Timber trackway from 2900–2500 BC, found in 2004 in a raised peat bog in the Humberhead Levels. Among the oldest ancient timber trackways known, preserved by centuries of waterlogged peat.
descriptions.097bd79b-a0d9-40d1-832d-c8a0671f7ab3: Settlement at Taxila dating to 1000 BC, predating the adjacent Bhir Mound by five centuries. Red burnished ware matching Charsadda pottery reveals deep connections across early Gandharan culture.
descriptions.c73b6ca5-aa7d-4737-af90-1e6cbab06ff5: Built 1478–1458 BC for Pharaoh Hatshepsut, its three massive terraces rise from the desert floor into the Deir el-Bahari cliffs. Connected to a valley temple 1 km east by a processional causeway.
descriptions.2968fd35-9b61-4dfb-bb1b-cc4489827fd6: Inca site at 3,590 metres on the northern slope below Choquequirao, above the Apurimac gorge. A high-altitude waypoint in the Inca road network connecting the empire's mountain strongholds.
descriptions.706c0a4d-f0ba-4970-8744-176841caae61: Andean site in the Ayacucho highlands, declared National Cultural Heritage in 2011. Its position in Lucanas Province places it within the sphere of pre-Inca communities of the southern sierra.
descriptions.7a1fc276-f5b2-42d1-b57f-95f2dc6eb115: Cave with archaeological and paleontological remains at 2,206 metres in Huanuco Region, 500 metres from the town of Ambo. Its deposits span multiple distinct prehistoric occupation periods.
descriptions.21d9af3d-9d4e-4df0-beb1-268486146a61: Inca site atop Jatunhosno mountain in the Ayacucho highlands, active 1438–1530 AD. High-altitude summit sites in the Inca world typically combined administrative, military, and ritual functions.
descriptions.3b7c9b7b-5792-4162-84ed-5663b1760d60: Cave in Cumbria where human bone dated to 11,000 years ago was reported in 2023 — among the earliest known evidence of human presence in Britain after the last Ice Age retreated.
descriptions.6a20e653-5320-440d-ac6c-2e86bb56e09e: 2nd-century AD Roman temple facing Mount Hermon, its doorway aligned to catch the first morning sun over the peak. A large basement chamber beneath the cella may have served as a burial vault.
descriptions.b0138ff7-a0fc-49ca-9df7-35d97a6e36b6: Built 570–550 BC on the Acropolis and named 'hundred feet long' — yet stretching 46 metres. Deliberately demolished by the Athenians in 490 BC, after their victory over the Persians at Marathon.
descriptions.e8740838-159b-4b95-9954-a3f96b68c2c9: Remnants of a 1st-century BC Hellenistic temple where only the lower courses of finely cut smooth stone blocks survive. The precision of the masonry suggests a once-imposing sacred structure.
descriptions.0b18d71c-7057-4b58-9c49-e3dbcb684d46: 2nd-century BC Hellenistic house in the Pathos Archaeological Park — a rare glimpse of domestic architecture from a period when Hellenistic culture shaped the cities of the eastern Mediterranean.
descriptions.f979bda7-ce1e-4000-9f31-996cf1b031da: Iron Age hillfort on a Devon promontory at 137 metres, projecting east off a large hill south of Buckland Brewer. Its elevated position commanded views across the surrounding moorland.
descriptions.c2cd2a6a-8f1d-4fce-9645-234908ef7d37: Stone circle in Wiltshire discovered by antiquarian A. D. Passmore in the 1890s. He noted eight stones with a possible avenue emerging — documented fully only in his unpublished notebooks.
descriptions.bacd75a6-2248-40b9-bc26-c04b3ecaebe4: Iron Age hillfort east of Holbeton in Devon, 95 metres above sea level overlooking the Erme Estuary. The elevated promontory gave defenders commanding views of coastal and river approaches.
descriptions.953e0154-1d30-4502-953d-4de1ff7bda62: 20-metre chambered cairn on a tiny uninhabited Orkney island, built around 3000 BC. Ancient carvings mark its stones — accessible only from Papa Westray, less than 100 metres away.
descriptions.1986f645-dc61-4118-91b1-5138b582b77c: Maya city in the Peten Basin active from 800 BC to 900 AD. Despite modest size, Holmul became a contested prize between the rival Tikal and Kaanul dynasties — its loyalty could tip regional power.
descriptions.9ac08a10-faeb-40fa-b8c8-ba0867bd9446: Iron Age promontory fort in Devon's Chase Wood, 150 metres above the River Dart. Its position used the deep river gorge below as a natural defensive barrier on the fort's most exposed flank.
descriptions.5ac30362-6c6f-412b-857b-3ec51df81f66: 7th-century BC tombs originally built as a place of worship before becoming a burial site. Eight chambers carved into palagonite — volcanic basalt — with three intact burial chambers surviving.
descriptions.4cb532e1-c831-463e-b9bf-a43bcbebeb02: Cliff dwelling with pictographs from 2000 BC, predating the Sinagua people who arrived around 1100 AD. The cave art spans over 3,000 years of intermittent human presence in the red-rock canyon.
descriptions.6768a252-1ad0-4056-a25d-fd8fd1df8525: Late Classic Maya city at its peak 650–850 AD. Structure II has twin false-staircase towers flanking a colossal Chenes monster-mouth portal — among the most theatrical facades in Maya architecture.
descriptions.7f7220d6-c601-4430-81c1-cb22bad26c90: Oval Iron Age hillfort in Somerset, 300 by 150 metres, occupied from 1200 BC into the Roman period. Also called Whitestaunton Camp, it sits just off the Devon border in the valley.
descriptions.54dc63d1-d88f-4d40-976b-460b203a07ef: 3rd-century Roman house in Paphos Park with mosaics depicting three mythological scenes: Orpheus charming animals with his lyre, Hercules wrestling the Nemean Lion, and an Amazon warrior.
descriptions.8636931f-2d42-494a-8c3c-305b9f72de1e: Hilltop settlement at 3,800 metres in the Huanuco highlands, notable for condors that nest in the crags above — drawn by altitude to one of the highest occupied Andean archaeological sites.
descriptions.a3b55317-bae1-42b5-9c64-477749bdc2d5: Pre-Columbian cemetery and hilltop village in Arequipa, on a named hill in Camaná Province. One of the later Andean burial sites, reflecting traditions of the region after Inca contact.
descriptions.7e23ac5b-3d28-4004-842a-6d3514ddd5ed: Andean burial complex with a rectangular tower, several buildings, and chullpa stone tombs in the high Huamalies highlands. The tower form points to pre-Inca cultures of Tantamayo district.
descriptions.04f2ddf1-3539-41e4-bea2-e0f1f9fa0476: Pre-Columbian settlement on Huayrapongo Mountain in the Cajamarca highlands, active around 300 BC. The elevated site commands views across San Miguel Province and the valleys below.
descriptions.bb263810-ca13-4ab1-b97d-d5ce2b2d0ab3: Pre-Columbian city flourishing 1150–1450 AD in the Ica region at 500 metres elevation. Its growth coincided with a wetter climatic phase — when the rains stopped, so did the city.
descriptions.9bf7ac31-4f48-4bbc-ad4b-cbef11d994b9: Settlement with four distinct occupation phases from the 6th century BC to the 6th century AD — over 1,000 years of use on an oval promontory with steep natural defences on two sides.
descriptions.d7a19d68-d432-45d4-bd3d-55430b25ed04: Inca-era village of houses, chullpa stone tombs, qullqa storehouses, and enclosures near Obas. The mix of residential, funerary, and storage structures marks a self-sufficient highland community.
descriptions.2a1d1dfb-474c-44db-a3ea-81758fadf851: Inca-era complex of houses, chullpa tombs, qullqa storehouses, and enclosures near Obas in Yarowilca Province. Residential and funerary structures combined suggest an integrated community plan.
descriptions.8423294a-2f28-4eec-87b0-9d55552cf023: 8th–2nd century BC city on the southern slope of Mount Etna — described as the largest and most considerable of the several ancient cities sharing the name Hybla in the region.
descriptions.70a58246-8b1d-43a5-8ecb-0828ec7cdaa1: One of three ancient Doric cities on Rhodes and part of the Doric Hexapolis. By Strabo's time it had dwindled to a village — absorbed by the rising city of Rhodes just 1,110 metres away.
descriptions.c434e091-07f2-4748-a298-2766e0717bb6: Settled by 700–550 BC, Igeum-dong shows the earliest firm evidence of chiefdom formation on the peninsula — nearly 950 years before the first state-level societies formed in the region.
descriptions.9fbc7054-b246-49bd-a776-ea840fc13591: Late Bronze Age city near Pylos with early Mycenaean palace remains. Excavations found evidence of administrative activity predating the earliest known Linear B archives in the region.
descriptions.1dea486d-6a81-4b61-ac89-bca807ad78ab: Pre-Columbian settlement in the Cajamarca highlands near Pomahuaca. Its mid-elevation position in Jaen Province suggests a role in the exchange networks linking coast and sierra communities.
descriptions.791b7bc8-8015-4715-ae40-50452a4c6fb5: Inca-era site on the Cochabamba Altiplano in Chapare Province. One of many highland stations that formed the administrative and road network connecting Inca territories across the Andes.
descriptions.fe3f5d3d-79d9-4790-b4ca-6b80aec4f558: Inca cave site from 1438–1530 AD in the Huancavelica highlands. Cave sites like this served ritual, storage, or sheltering roles within the Inca road system crossing the high sierra.
descriptions.8590c435-e895-4d7e-9b06-d0f2027c04d7: Burial towers and archaeological remains on the high Altiplano, declared a National Historical Monument in 2008. Adjacent chullpa towers mark a pre-Inca funerary landscape of the Oruro highlands.
descriptions.f9c5d633-ef9c-48e5-aac2-a8802efa3021: Inca rock painting near Ollantaytambo, dating 1438–1530 AD. The central figure likely depicts a noble person — one of the few surviving Inca figurative rock art sites in the Sacred Valley.
descriptions.6ec6df2d-af82-49d5-8e37-1309ddc4793b: Small Inca complex at 3,590 metres on the flank of Inka Wasi, above the Apurimac gorge south of Choquequirao. A high-altitude staging post on the edge of the empire's most dramatic terrain.
descriptions.184dfea2-b710-4c3a-a3e8-d8cea0738290: Inca site on top of Allqu Willka mountain in the Huanta highlands, active 1438–1530 AD. High-altitude summit sites in the Inca world typically combined administrative, military, and ritual functions.
descriptions.a3825cb5-de53-43d4-9561-429dfeb1ffc2: Inca tampu waystation at 2,127 metres in La Convencion Province, built to shelter and supply travellers moving through the empire's mountain road network in the Cusco region.
descriptions.076be159-500d-490f-b804-aea33c1160e9: Inca tampu on a summit in Vilcabamba, where the last Inca rulers retreated after the Spanish conquest. Its mountaintop position may carry both strategic and logistical significance.
descriptions.54bbe431-e520-498c-8413-4bbc23eb4947: Inca-era site between Chucuito and Puno on the Lake Titicaca shore, declared National Cultural Heritage. The lakeside position linked it to the sacred geography and ritual landscape of Titicaca.
descriptions.b306540a-ea4d-4cd9-8ad1-04a57629f65b: Inca elite retreat with a palace, a tower, and baths featuring a carved stone with 13 angles — a hallmark of Inca precision stonework. Active 1438–1530 AD as a residential and ritual complex.
descriptions.169edf74-fc91-4850-aa2a-7d5328c13c02: High-altitude Andean site at 4,400 metres in Lampa and San Roman provinces, straddling two administrative districts. The extreme elevation suggests a ritual or astronomical function beyond settlement.
descriptions.5604de42-1588-454f-8c49-893cc5044855: Andean site at 3,867 metres between Ollaraya and Unicachi overlooking Lake Titicaca. Declared National Cultural Heritage, it sits within one of the densest zones of Andean prehistory.
descriptions.d2403f87-24a1-4f20-bb4c-ffd68ac59268: Rock paintings on Intipanawin Mountain at 3,569 metres, depicting the eye of the sun alongside painted llamas — combining solar and pastoral imagery at the edge of the high Andean sky.
descriptions.6153e9bc-e4b8-468f-8328-878ba9ebd02f: Rock paintings at 3,800 metres in Calca Province's Lamay District. The name means 'corner of the sun' in Quechua — suggesting the paintings may have tracked sunrise directions from the ridge.
descriptions.8de612f7-9569-4b28-9883-3143d47fb309: Roman-era port at the confluence of the Sar and Ulla rivers, seat of the Celtic Capori tribe. Refounded as Iria Flavia on the Via Nova road — later a key early Christian episcopal centre.
descriptions.1be6202f-f47a-40f8-8b07-9fe22cc95000: Inca-era site in Yauli Province near La Oroya in the Junin Region. Its highland location places it along one of the Andean corridors connecting the central sierra to the Pacific coast.
descriptions.5860ecf2-57f8-44e6-93a1-0f6b5d6994e1: Pacific island refuge off the Chiriqui coast, inhabited 500–1400 AD. Its people built a palenque — a fortified enclosure — on the 400-acre surface of tropical forest, mangroves, and beach.
descriptions.28402a1d-9e31-4818-9790-783de876cecd: Andean site on Susupillo's northern slope in Tantamayo District, dense with pre-Inca tower architecture. Its position adjacent to a same-named site suggests a paired settlement complex.
descriptions.0e176a05-5bb7-4b69-a3da-b346599d3910: 1st-century AD Roman stronghold in Lycia. The remnants of Issium mark a frontier outpost of the Roman Empire, its walls still legible in the rugged highland terrain.
descriptions.2a63af83-136d-4c7c-b909-d40ccd3463dc: Active 200-900 AD, Ixkun is the best-known Maya site in Dolores municipality: vaulted palaces, a ballcourt, an E-Group complex, and two mid-size stepped pyramids amid unrestored mounds.
descriptions.d281428b-8acc-438a-9056-7742575b7b8c: 8th-century BC to 5th-century AD petroglyph site on a mountain in the Riyadh Region. Stone drawings of camels and pines, and Badia-Thamudic script inscriptions, cover Jabal al-Baidain.
descriptions.62c99642-3f6b-4122-a872-6c5f452aa35f: Perched 4,126 metres up, Jach'a Phasa holds over 50 chullpa burial towers of volcanic stone and mud-and-straw mortar rising from a mountaintop enclosed by a perimeter wall.
descriptions.48e08ccf-7661-47c1-9a0e-ff9e205530e0: 3rd-millennium BC Dilmun burial mound field in the Northern Governorate. Inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage in 2019 as part of the Dilmun Burial Mounds, it marks a civilisation's funerary landscape.
descriptions.39927155-7597-4da8-9e3f-8c02d3d7a6ac: Amazonian petroglyphs on a giant monolith in the Cusco highlands. Abstract spirals and a shape resembling a key may record ayahuasca visions; the carvings have clear Amazonian cultural origins.
descriptions.4e7592eb-facc-4d84-a019-0d2f2311c1d0: 2nd-century BC hill fortress at 1,145 metres in the Sahyadri range. Jivdhan is one of the Famous 5 high-difficulty treks in Maharashtra, its sheer cliffs forming natural ramparts on all sides.
descriptions.24553e33-f5bd-409d-bf2f-04c193eb63cf: Harappan site active 2600-1900 BC in Balochistan's Nasirabad District. A federally protected area between Jhat Pat and Dera Murad Jamali, occupied through the height of Indus civilisation.
descriptions.17483f6c-6a12-4652-83e1-e0a2f6665429: 3rd-century BC mountain site near Paraćin. A chest found at its peak yielded 14 sets of weapons, harness gear, jewellery, and clothing accessories characteristic of Dacian and Scordisci knights.
descriptions.0569a73d-875d-4d49-bc8a-74c9a7fa4704: 3rd-century BC successor to Hadrianopolis, rebuilt by Justinian I in Epirus. When the bishop's see moved, it went to Dryinopolis, not Justinianopolis — the city was rebuilt but lost its church.
descriptions.a7e18bef-7c15-49cd-9262-41e42bc27690: 9th-century BC settlement near the Danube. Roman tombs with richly decorated wall paintings from the 3rd-4th century AD were discovered here, layering prehistoric and Roman occupation into one site.
descriptions.c48038a4-458a-4de7-acd1-2259721fef62: 13th-3rd century BC site with ruins of the northernmost Ancient Macedonian city yet found. Kale-Krsevica commanded a strategic plateau overlooking the South Morava valley from the Rujan foothills.
descriptions.1e02642d-e3bd-4618-bffe-90fff38516e1: Roman-era trapezoid fortress near Podujevo with towers at each wall end. Cut stone and brick bonded with lime mortar survive up to 4 metres high, the outline of the fortification still legible.
descriptions.a6d480fd-bb81-4339-bb85-59c7e8bf8d63: Early medieval fortress in Kosovo with walls, buildings, and a slag heap indicating on-site ore smelting. Traces of burning on the hillside suggest the village below was destroyed by fire.
