descriptions.d4ead0d9-4f61-4021-a84d-da1b667f002d: Chanka hilltop settlement at 3,935 metres in the Ayacucho highlands. K'allapayuq Urqu occupies a mountain summit in La Mar Province, positioned between two remote Andean communities.
descriptions.8459f1d2-a96f-4c37-a1d3-fb4ebbe3fb2e: Megalithic site and protected nature reserve in the Perm Krai highlands. Kamennyy Gorod — Stone City — is a dramatic rock formation of weathered pillars that gave the site its evocative name.
descriptions.feeb5055-f18a-46f3-82cf-fbdfe23d72b4: Around 1000 AD, Kanichi blended Wari and Chanka influences into one complex: chullpas, ceremonial buildings, service centres, and a water system of wells and springs at 4,000+ metres.
descriptions.40acede4-eb32-4515-9ca4-b44145280678: Remains of the monastery of Karabelli Sion in the Demre valley of Lycia. Stone walls and foundations still trace the footprint of this Byzantine religious complex in the landscape.
descriptions.841c1e8e-6b27-447d-8699-68b4bebd13fc: 3rd-7th century AD Byzantine church at Demre, Antalya. Karabel Kilisesi preserves the stone skeleton of a place of Christian worship that stood through both late Roman and early Byzantine eras.
descriptions.70466849-1cf9-4af9-a442-7a4ffa6e24c9: 3rd-century BC Hellenistic settlement with remains spanning to the 4th century AD. Stone ruins at Karaboluculu mark a hilltop community that persisted through six centuries of occupation.
descriptions.a4b56463-b8e7-48af-80d0-c01b5c9caba9: 4th-1st century BC walled settlement abandoned in the 1st century BC. This fortified Persian or Hellenistic site near Karchaghbyur is currently being excavated in the Gegharkunik highlands.
descriptions.f0b20fa9-aab2-400d-bfa8-24af297bb993: 8000 BC Neolithic settlement at the tip of the Karpasia Peninsula. Three French campaigns between 1970 and 1973 revealed one of the earliest known human habitations on a limestone promontory.
descriptions.6cef20ff-4a03-4476-a80e-b44447f6764a: 1st-millennium BC twin-temple complex near Akrotiri, roughly 100 metres long. A Byzantine church found within in 2018 held mosaics with inscriptions in perfect condition from an emperor's reign.
descriptions.db4c2f3e-2f4a-4dc6-bf01-23f109fe1837: Hellenistic-period rock tombs carved from the cliff face. Kaya mezarlari represents the widespread funerary tradition of cutting burial chambers directly from living rock, practised across Lycia.
descriptions.28fbf63d-5ca4-45fd-a54e-7a660232b148: Active 400 BC-900 AD, Ka'Kabish held 90 structures across 8 groups: two major temples, a ballcourt with circular marker, and large platforms that likely served as royal or elite residences.
descriptions.e2293ae0-0b9a-47cd-869e-971074072947: A 45-metre enigma: three stone platforms joined by a wall, no inscriptions, no known builder. Kbor Klib stands just 6 metres tall now, standing in a farmer's field in remote central North Africa.
descriptions.68c4944b-9e3a-4561-955c-33fa9978fc86: A skull unearthed in 1940 proved nearly 15,000 years old; later digs found hearths from 29,000 BC. Keilor is one of the earliest habitation sites on the continent; megafauna remains suggest hunting.
descriptions.679e85b1-245b-40bc-b815-8cd1ae71ee12: A Lycian island whose northern coast is a sunken city. Kekova holds a port, two docks, three churches, two chapels, a bath, two towers, four production workshops, and Lycian sarcophagi in the sea.
descriptions.f24eeac5-51df-4456-bcee-607d7deacdef: Mitanni palace city on the Tigris built around 1600 BC, destroyed by earthquake c. 1350 BC. Kemune was rediscovered in 2013 only when drought dropped the Mosul Dam reservoir, exposing its walls.
descriptions.0abaf157-35d2-478f-8b19-c142f67aa8c7: Inca sacred maze at 3,800 metres. Kenko Grande holds an amphitheatre, a solar clock, the Temple of the Monkeys, zigzagging stone canals, and a subterranean chamber carved from bedrock.
descriptions.1a877fee-91b8-46ad-bc9b-b94aba8fc197: High-altitude site in the Puno Region at roughly 4,000 metres. Declared National Cultural Heritage by the National Institute of Culture, it preserves evidence of pre-Columbian Andean occupation.
descriptions.8eb1cd28-4302-4acf-be6f-539ce6996e58: 1st-millennium BC Iron Age enclosure on Exmoor's edge at 320 metres. A univallate round on Kentisbury Down sits above an ancient crossroads, commanding views across Devon moorland toward the sea.
descriptions.30dba5dd-d925-4fbf-a84c-ed9c20f1f286: 3rd-millennium BC Neolithic settlement whose footprint exceeded the later Bronze Age Palace of Knossos built on top of it. Kephala became the chosen ground for one of antiquity's greatest palaces.
descriptions.e89143d5-c432-409e-a88d-272b979d262c: 1st-century AD Roman kiosk relocated from Nubia when Lake Nasser rose. Two Hathor-headed columns flank the entrance; four remaining columns bear carvings of date palms and grape vines.
descriptions.1b4ac17d-5b37-4459-b3c6-6722b86aa4a8: Late 4th-century AD Byzantine settlement in the Dead Cities of the Levant. An unusually tall basilica survives; UNESCO World Heritage in 2011 as part of the Ancient Villages of Northern Syria.
descriptions.ef5738eb-4e38-442e-b64e-7a4d8d469f38: Rock paintings and tombs at 3,160 metres on the slope of Mount Kapuliyuq. Khichuqaqa preserves pigment art alongside ancient burial sites near Urubamba communities in the Andean highlands.
descriptions.1ada3660-1f43-4840-b8a0-f75580a45a6a: 1st-millennium BC Phoenician port city later known as Leptis Magna. Khoms began as a Phoenician colony and grew into a major Mediterranean trading hub under Carthaginian and then Roman rule.
descriptions.1a76bfc9-7056-4848-ac12-d24016a923bb: A fortress approach requiring a direct wall-climb. Khuntichi Vaat offers a rare route to Hadsar Fort in the Sahyadri range, where the cliff face itself was the original entrance for those ascending.
descriptions.71d8e2bc-7406-4c4a-b68d-2ff1b71800e8: Museum dedicated to the Orkhon inscriptions, housing the Bilge Qaghan and Kul Tigin monuments from the nearby Orkhon Valley UNESCO site. Copies were erected in their original steppe locations.
descriptions.867f08af-8934-4ec0-bbcc-2c730bb2a93a: Cave paintings and petroglyphs at 3,400 metres in Huancavelica. Killa Mach'ay — Moon Cave in Quechua — shows llamas, people, and abstract lines painted on rock faces above the Acobamba valley.
descriptions.69aaac26-9f4a-47da-beb4-d31ef8d4301f: Inca-era megalithic complex near Cusco with a rock-cut astronomical calendar called The Rock of the Moon. Killarumiyoq shows stonework precision that some researchers attribute to a pre-Inca culture.
descriptions.ddc0a0bf-1313-499a-8ec6-77839727afe1: Inca-period archaeological park in the Anta Province of Cusco Region. Killarumiyuq sits in high Andean terrain in Ancahuasi District, preserved as part of the Sacred Valley heritage corridor.
descriptions.56f6f878-19b8-4098-8e60-347661302422: Late Classic Maya city active 600-900 AD. Kinal is noted for a complete absence of sculpture — a striking anomaly — while its 8th-century building programme shows rapid urban expansion in Peten.
descriptions.20364c84-1e5f-4324-ad5c-be3f0d31586d: Iron Age hillfort later used by the Romans at Buckland Dinham. Kingsdown Camp's drystone wall once stood 4 metres high and 2.5 metres wide, enclosing just 0.15 hectares within a defensive circuit.
descriptions.cfdbdb6f-7420-49f2-9f19-8922851ddc24: 3rd-11th century AD Maya city linked to Dzibanche. Kinichna's acropolis is a three-level pyramid leading to two lateral temples, centrepiece of a ceremonial complex in southern Quintana Roo.
descriptions.43ee9ef2-ada7-4796-98eb-4d2ba9728d74: Iron Age broch on the Sutherland coast, active 800 BC to the 1st century AD. Kintradwell is a northeastern tower-fort of the Highlands, a round defensive structure of the Atlantic Iron Age tradition.
descriptions.4c3d31bc-8f57-44e5-988b-4bb0e3d3d516: Iron Age hillfort with a massive rampart, outer ditch, and natural defences on the remaining sides. Kinver Edge Hillfort crowns the northern end of Kinver Edge in Kinver, Staffordshire.
descriptions.deda1768-dcfc-4b90-859b-bdf579f30baa: Settlement at 3,600 metres in the Huánuco Region, southeast of Llata near the village of Milpo. K'ipakhara is one of many high-altitude sites that mark pre-Columbian presence in the highland interior.
descriptions.2ac1dae4-0ddb-4592-ae5d-1b628466832d: 1st-century AD Lycian city whose history is largely unwritten. Kitanaura's acropolis walls survive 5-6 metres tall in places; two basilicas and cisterns fill a hilltop whose builders remain unknown.
descriptions.8f5e0a0d-a4e5-4c7d-8c73-80695a6a5290: 4th-century AD Roman observation tower with no ground-level entrance; a wooden ladder was the only way in. Kizlar Kalesi has arched vaulted rooms and an inner building still standing in Lycia.
descriptions.fa63f634-1804-4382-9e66-e0e38c5d301a: 2nd-1st-millennium BC fort, tower, and city wall traces in Laconian Sparta. Roof tiles and structural remains at Klaraki hint at a fortified hilltop settlement above the Mousga Stream.
descriptions.2bf56725-c490-4536-9db2-1144983e477f: 9th-millennium BC farming village, the oldest confirmed in the world. Klimonas was a circular subterranean building 10 metres across; cereals came from the Levant alongside domesticated hunting dogs.
descriptions.3d790ba4-199b-4b94-b834-531db02eb066: 320-340 AD underground Roman construction at Carthage reusing a cistern. Kobba Bent el Rey's large hall and two vaulted chambers are the best-preserved residential monument on the Carthage site.
descriptions.ba6d421b-2b19-4634-8cd3-c9be959e041d: Cucuteni-Trypillia mega-settlement of 100 hectares, occupied 3200-2700 BC. Kocherzhyntsi is one of 2,440 proto-cities in a vanished civilisation, when the region held the world's largest towns.
descriptions.d7215ef3-51c2-4b04-9d35-126f058e0bf6: Hastily settled and quickly abandoned during the Bronze Age Collapse, 13th-12th century BC. Pyla-Kokkinokremos sat on a rocky plateau 10 km from ancient Kition — a refuge that ultimately failed.
descriptions.e9eacdcd-80e7-4101-aa88-b942ec755f5c: 1,027 megalithic artifacts across 40 sites in South Sumatra, spread across 12 communities in Lahat Regency. The Tanjung Raja complex sits near the city of Pagar Alam in the highland interior.
descriptions.f1e8a463-b2c4-42c2-a0b8-94e7bf420f6a: 2nd-4th century AD Mithraic temple in the Neretva valley, atypical because its floor sits at ground level rather than underground. The Konjic site shows how the Mithra cult spread via Roman soldiers.
descriptions.730f6c51-c41c-4f6a-9443-31acb7f007a3: From 20,000 BC, Aboriginal people entered Koonalda Cave to mine flint in darkness. Thousands of square metres of finger-groove lines and geometric patterns cover the walls of this Nullarbor cave.
descriptions.3aa70cf2-d56b-4401-8a60-2cd12131827c: Occupied for 1,500 years around 10,000 BC, leaving up to 2 metres of artefact-rich sediment. Koongine Cave's walls carry finger-groove markings left by its ancient occupants on the Limestone Coast.
descriptions.15c7e942-5ff2-4ceb-ae6e-e78cdfbb8b99: Hittite origins to 15th-century AD ruins at one Cilician coastal site: sea castle, Black Castle, port, necropolis, colonnaded street, three baths, temples, and a Byzantine cistern all at Korikos.
descriptions.4c6f2c0a-abdb-4a1d-a12c-a71403776fe4: Minoan through Roman ruins blanket this uninhabited islet 5.6 km off eastern Crete. Known in antiquity as Leuce, Koufonisi bears centuries of occupation visible above and below the Libyan Sea.
descriptions.f9cfcc0f-960a-4184-b72d-ab054ed01221: 5th-3rd-millennium BC Botai culture site with early evidence of horse corrals: curved post-hole rows and nitrogen deposits in enclosed areas indicate horses were penned long before cavalry was known.
descriptions.ba20f54a-5cb3-402c-9ebe-616864703d1b: Illyrian Labeates settlement active from the early Iron Age to the 1st century AD. Kratul's large-block walls are a textbook example of Illyrian military architecture among the tribal confederacies.
descriptions.53fd5500-0ce2-4bd0-a3d3-8ec069605e3e: Pisidian-founded city later rebuilt in Roman grid-plan style. Kremna's walls, two gates, and colonnaded street date to the Roman period, laid over a Hellenistic urban foundation in ancient Pisidia.
descriptions.1567cad6-7871-428a-b923-946a24ef9b8d: 7th-century BC city in Calabria, Magna Graecia. Krimisa was inhabited by indigenous people assimilated by the Greeks; thoroughly Hellenized by the Classical period, it remained so into the Roman era.
descriptions.826407f8-35ca-4423-bd85-5f53a3d95ea2: A Hindu temple erected in 1888 on a hilltop overlooking the Krishna River valley. Krishnabai Mandir marks the venerated source of the Krishna River, one of the subcontinent's most sacred waterways.
descriptions.29b7554d-b821-4aa7-b1de-958cd9398b65: 4th-century AD Berber-Roman estate inside a cork oak forest. Ksar Lalla Fatma includes a two-storey villa, farmhouses, an oil mill, an aqueduct, a cistern, and hypocaust-heated thermal baths.
descriptions.a597e522-3aeb-4680-bb33-44b2502f8579: Cucuteni-Trypillia mega-settlement of 100 hectares, occupied 3600-3200 BC. Ksaverove is one of 2,440 known proto-cities of this culture, whose vast settlements spread across Moldova and the steppe.
descriptions.2bb3d2fe-62b3-4d3f-b12f-e9bdee25f150: Lower Paleolithic cave site at 1,600 metres in the Caucasus highlands. Acheulean handaxes from 40,000-25,000 years ago at Kudaro push early human presence deep into the high mountains of the region.
descriptions.fcd0bf5d-100f-451f-99b9-7d3ecb4335ec: Rock paintings and tombs in the Arequipa highlands. Kukuli is in Caraveli Province, part of a scattered network of Andean pigment art sites where images painted on rock endure across generations.
descriptions.fc514046-4f2c-42b1-a3f6-ca88404d2e18: Andean chullpa burial site in the altiplano of La Paz Department. Kuntur Amaya's funerary towers near Wayllani mark a high-altitude necropolis in Aroma Province at the edge of the Umala highlands.
descriptions.7bcdeff1-fd34-4c0d-a32e-d8f812e64a73: Late Andean settlement of round stone buildings and chullpa tombs in Pasco Province. Kunturmarka's circular architecture is typical of Andean communities in the centuries before the Inca expansion.
descriptions.cfb36f32-10c1-477e-8a10-203dea937c00: Rock paintings at 4,433 metres on a Pasco mountain rising to 4,475 m. Kuntuyuq sits near Iskayqucha — Quechua for two lakes — where high-altitude pigment art endures on exposed Andean rock faces.
descriptions.bdbf1e68-32c8-4571-90c0-ef154d458704: From around 10,000 BC, Aboriginal people hunted wallaby in open tundra near Kutikina Cave on the Franklin River. This Pleistocene rock shelter helped establish the antiquity of Tasmanian occupation.
descriptions.b0db0a0f-c2c3-4119-bf6f-43f2e040119c: 1st-millennium BC Achaemenid-era reinforcement in ancient Bactria. A round building 40 x 40 metres on a 4-metre mound; three concentric outer walls form two vaulted corridors lit by wall openings.
descriptions.27d45d98-0ac5-475c-8b30-68e54947cddc: 4th-century BC Lycian city atop a mountain ringed with sarcophagi, chamber tombs, and Lycian-inscribed rock tombs. Kyaneai's large theatre crowns the summit; Byzantine artefacts fill the slopes.
descriptions.036346d9-313c-4fcd-9649-1aaba368e72e: 4th-century BC cistern cut into bedrock on the summit of Lycian Kyaneai. This water structure kept the mountain city viable across Hellenistic, Roman, and Byzantine occupation spanning centuries.
descriptions.217706bc-155b-44ca-bd4b-9df96e3bc014: Active 800 BC-900 AD, K'axob began as a Late Preclassic Maya village on two pyramid plazas and grew through the Classic Period. It lies in the Pulltrouser Swamp wetlands of northern Mesoamerica.
descriptions.b3ad3302-103a-4bbe-83a5-0f27d63ea8f4: Middle Preclassic Maya site active 900-600 BC, covering over 200 hectares at its peak. La Blanca boasted the highest pyramid on the Pacific coastal plain of Mesoamerica during the Mokaya florescence.
descriptions.1e6efd70-020c-43b7-a63c-495eefa5a972: 5500-5000 BC lakeshore Neolithic village, the only prehistoric lacustrine site on the Iberian Peninsula. La Draga at Banyoles shows two early Neolithic phases with no change in material culture.
descriptions.e6b26bed-47b7-437b-97ab-60d88a018682: 1,600-year-old shaft tomb holding 28 individuals, possibly in two ceremonies. Found sealed and unopened in situ, La Florida may rewrite understanding of burial customs in ancient Zacatecas.
descriptions.672f18a4-e818-4367-b593-fe0432b134a7: Around 900 AD, the Chachapoyas placed mummies in cliff-side tombs above a high-altitude lake. Laguna de las Momias yielded extraordinary burials; condors overhead gave this Amazonian site its names.
descriptions.390afd0a-2366-4e5a-bb13-9d8319568abc: Maya site active 200 BC-1000 AD in northern Peten. La Joyanca sits east of La Florida (Namaan) near the border town of El Naranjo; its central area includes several temple-pyramids and other mounds.
descriptions.498589cb-b378-4a09-adc3-3a911dc1cd77: Basalt stones in two lines shaped like a giant eel, an Aboriginal ceremonial site in Victoria. Stones at Lake Bolac range from 30 to 150 cm, some possibly embedded in the ground as anchors.
descriptions.6dc58d5f-9c58-42da-831d-af82d9c07c94: Indus Valley city covering over 300 hectares, one of the civilisation's largest. Lakhan-jo-daro predates the Mature Harappan period and sits 75 km from Mohenjo Daro, yet remains largely unexcavated.
descriptions.0e627b04-0c07-4967-9b94-0967a2eca175: Minoan settlement just south of Archanes on Crete, occupied 3100-1100 BC. Lakkos was absorbed into the Bronze Age world that produced the Aegean's most sophisticated palatial civilisation.
descriptions.6265475a-0d4e-45a7-b0fd-ad56fa0f4a89: Classic Maya site 250-950 AD, likely a suburb of nearby Dzibanche. Lamay features temples and two plazas under restoration, just 1 km from one of southern Quintana Roo's major ceremonial centres.
descriptions.bdd92d68-2715-4dfe-a956-e2f3a5b77465: Third-largest Maya site in the Three River region, La Milpa was active 400 BC-850 AD. Pyramid-centred and positioned where two major borders converge, it was a key hub in the regional trade network.
descriptions.dde240ca-5969-4123-a842-e7e235f7566b: 5300-4900 BC Bandkeramik farming landscape in the Merzbach Valley. Langweiler revealed 160 houses across eight settlement sites, three enclosures, and a cemetery, a window into Europe's first farmers.
descriptions.4df3dcbd-62d3-4e37-92fe-e79989233f1f: 700-1600 AD rock art site with cave paintings and engravings inside a Sonoran Desert canyon, plus seasonal camps on the alluvial plain. La Pintada spans nearly a millennium of human artistic activity.
descriptions.d98d86bb-989a-424a-bcce-2710f0620ac0: Ancient Cretan city that sheltered refugees of Lyktos after Knossos destroyed their city. Augustus granted Lappa special privileges for opposing Mark Antony, a city rescued twice by powerful patrons.
descriptions.bc7bf3f9-5f9e-41e4-ac6f-c8efd61c388e: One of the eastern gates in the 3rd-century Aurelian Walls of Rome. Emperor Claudius erected it in 52 AD as decorative support for two aqueducts — the Aqua Claudia and the Anio Novus.
descriptions.6ee96ec3-9a2f-41be-ad77-f8187a54e493: 5th-century BC village on the southeast coast of Rhodes, source of a distinctive gray-blue marble, lithos lartios, quarried in antiquity for local use and still characteristic of the island.
descriptions.02a9d200-6a8f-40aa-92a1-79182e38c822: 4th-millennium BC necropolis in Huelva found in 2022. A 2023 stela shows a headdress, necklace, two swords, and male genitalia, described as gender ambiguous by excavators from Seville and Durham.
descriptions.8f53beb3-710b-4ace-9ebd-85757f1542e2: Occupied 1500 BC-1500 AD, a 3,000-year continuum on the Caribbean slope. Las Mercedes has platforms, plazas, terraces, ramps, funerary areas, and paved roads; monumental construction began c. 1000 AD.
descriptions.9b14cbe4-f49c-4abf-8f51-c3bc75f54b00: Maya site 350 BC-250 AD in the Peten Basin. Teotihuacano imagery on La Sufricaya stelae and murals suggests foreign or non-Maya occupation, a rare contact between distant Mesoamerican cultures.
descriptions.57f3306b-9927-46a4-84ef-9688bc9809f5: 1st-4th century AD Roman fort near Hadrian's Wall, incorporated into a Medieval castle. Lavatrae began as a wooden-ramparted waypoint on the road connecting Carlisle to York, later rebuilt in stone.
descriptions.2da62cd0-6900-4668-b490-220fdc6b1b49: 3300-1200 BC stone circle of sixteen stones, six fallen, roughly 24 metres across on Bodmin Moor. Leaze once had an estimated 22 stones; a hedge bisects the ring and a solitary outlier stands beyond.
descriptions.a09044a9-4ff3-4df3-be04-72a953b67429: Nine-terraced megalithic pyramid on the Cibedug River in West Java. Lebak Cibedug has menhirs and altars on each terrace, plus dolmens on site, a sacred complex in Banten regency's highland forest.
descriptions.7895564a-2414-4bd5-a9c7-61e611f9159a: 2nd-century AD Roman camp near Hadrian's Wall with an outwork surrounding its main defences, suggesting specialised use beyond a standard marching camp. One of over 40 camps recorded near the Wall.
descriptions.54e625b7-a84e-4502-b43a-e65734d928c7: 8th-century BC tomb sealed for nearly 2,800 years, found in 1998 inside the walls of city-kingdom Kition. The unlooted Lefkaritis hypogeum held extraordinary gold ornaments now conserved in a museum.
descriptions.5f745388-3793-459b-b55f-90dbb5bfed78: Eastern gate of ancient Nicaea with three arched Byzantine gateways. The middle arch bears a Greek inscription noting construction by Proconsul Plancius Varus in 123 AD, a dated Roman monument.
descriptions.534c1035-fbfe-46fe-8127-a709d32dc1c7: Large Sarsen stone near Newport, Essex, possibly an alms-offering point for a nearby medieval leper hospital. The Leper Stone predates the hospital by millennia; only a fragment of the wall remains.
descriptions.5ea99baa-5ab5-4f9f-adb9-48bc53e97363: 25th-24th century BC pyramid at Abusir, likely built for a wife of King Nyuserre Ini. The largely destroyed 5th Dynasty Double Pyramid stands east of the Neferefre pyramid in the Abusir field.
descriptions.f1ec1e6c-f23c-40a9-ac6e-293965a8bd60: Museum of Leptis Magna layered past, Berber, Punic, Phoenician, and Roman. Statues of Zeus and Apollo stand alongside metalwork, pottery, and jewellery that trace everyday life across successive ages.
descriptions.b202a257-17d5-4bc3-b983-496bc68dfd40: 5th-century BC club and meeting hall at Delphi Sanctuary of Apollo. The Lesche of the Knidians housed two celebrated Polygnotus paintings, the Capture of Troy and the Nekyia, now lost with the hall.
descriptions.ffb9aa8c-0ecc-4510-b18d-8555e319c427: 3300-500 BC Bronze Age settlement clusters on Bodmin Moor at 329 metres. Two settlement areas on the slopes hold field enclosures, cairns, a cist, a propped stone, and associated stone circles.
descriptions.561ba9a0-09a5-4954-b137-f5c7dbdb0349: 6th-century BC Phoenician lighthouse at Leptis Magna Harbour, a port that passed from Phoenician to Carthaginian to Roman rule. The ancient tower that guided ships is now slowly eroded by the sea.
descriptions.34d064de-8773-4d0c-9fff-7e2ea5a1f11d: 4th-century BC Lycian sarcophagus in three sections standing in the middle of modern Kas. The Likya Anit Mezar — the King's Tomb — is a monumental funerary marker once planted in open civic space.
descriptions.4896b11f-df95-41f0-859b-7dc2bdd54b52: Lycian city with over 400 rock tombs, more than almost anywhere in the region. Limyra inscriptions name the occupants in Lycian; its acropolis, Roman walls, and Byzantine remains span 14 centuries.
descriptions.73ebc428-aeb1-4512-9c52-af90a3768431: Named in Homer's Iliad as a city that sent ships to Troy, Lindos was one of the great Dorian cities of Rhodes — famed for its wine, figs, and commanding eastern coastal position.
descriptions.2c2eaf7a-0c07-460c-8893-9a0443f8f9d4: 4500–3000 BC. Bronze Age burial mounds at Ljuljaci define the Racha-Ljuljaci cultural group, a local variant of the Vatin culture. Triballi Thracian tombs were also unearthed here.
descriptions.50b5d70c-f280-4c8c-a3e5-90e7deeca86e: 1st-5th century AD. A settlement in the Amazonas highlands at 1,063 m elevation - Llactan sits at the edge of the cloud forest, one of many forgotten towns hidden in this rugged Andean terrain.
descriptions.82b9ba8e-bc9a-405a-afe2-fcb210a5d278: 1000–1500 AD. Petroglyphs at 3,449 m carve llamas, vicuñas, felines, people, and the sun into Andean rock — a vivid record of life and belief in the high Apurímac mountains.
descriptions.6bedf225-fc80-4324-9f91-eaa70bdcc002: 1st-5th century AD. Rock paintings of llamas line the valley of Wakanwayq'u at 3,535 m. Nearby lies another rock art site, Ayamach'ay - this valley shelters ancient images under the open Andean sky.
descriptions.01f368c9-e567-4557-b5ce-21c6d182305d: Tombs and rock paintings at 4,000 m on a peak called Qucha Quyllur — Quechua for 'lake star'. The dead were laid here among the stars, in a valley the living named Wakan Wayq'u.
descriptions.c54e678e-8662-42cd-8875-fc387cc19fad: 1000–1500 AD. Llaqta Qulluy sits in the highlands of Huancavelica Province — one of several Andean settlement sites whose Quechua name encodes the hilltop landscape it commands.
descriptions.3bdedec1-6321-4560-b986-2ce86b3b5c0d: 1st-5th century AD. Predominantly circular walled structures perch at 3,400 m on the slopes of Conayca mountain - an Andean hilltop settlement commanding the surrounding highland terrain.
descriptions.ec64fd4c-0fa2-4932-9a75-6756b90aed5b: 1000–1500 AD. Llaqta Qulluy crowns a 3,960 m mountain in Tayacaja Province — perched above the community of Llaqta Pata, surveying the high valleys of Huancavelica below.
descriptions.bee72fdb-a761-4a79-90ee-9e98d1d5ad75: 1000–1500 AD. A highland settlement in Vilca District, protected as National Cultural Heritage — one of several Llaqta Qulluy sites scattered across the Huancavelica highlands.
descriptions.753c8b27-50ac-4659-9d58-dd441ced2936: Iron Age, 800 BC. An egg-shaped hillfort set at 120 m, ground dropping sharply on three sides. A scheduled monument, its single entrance points toward the southwest at the narrower end.
descriptions.b7f23683-db44-409d-8326-78af49f5b8a1: Iron Age, 1st millennium BC. A univallate hillfort covering 2 hectares on a low gravel plateau in Hampshire — much reduced by ploughing, but earthworks survive in a small northern coppice.
descriptions.a28e4962-5513-4955-b1e0-d6a8f8f244cc: Around 3000 BC. A Neolithic gallery grave of the Wartberg culture near Marburg — unique for its exceptionally rich ceramic assemblage. Its sunken rectangular chamber measured 5 x 2.2 metres.
descriptions.d0e007ba-24cd-4929-b135-0b907397e531: 3400-800 BC. Two round cairns linked by a bank - a layout unique in the country. The northern cairn reaches 23 m across and 2.4 m high, in the Peak District Neolithic highlands.
descriptions.21f3da5f-262c-46e8-bead-32be438da097: 350 BC-250 AD. On the north shore of Lake Yojoa, Los Naranjos holds the oldest structures still standing in the region - mounds, pyramids, and ceramics built by the Proto-Lenca over 2,000 years.
descriptions.168431d1-ad6c-4a18-9798-2d43d361c5b1: 900–1470 AD. Chachapoya tombs wedged into a rock cleft in cloud forest, painted red, yellow, black, and white. Closed to all but scientific missions — named for their carved wooden phalluses.
descriptions.9f9d3754-8078-4cc3-8afd-b07db05a8598: 2000 BC–16th century AD. Stone carvings and sculptures mark this ancient Maya site near the Copán ruins — one of the longest-occupied ceremonial landscapes in the Copán Department.
descriptions.9e723832-0a2b-43f9-90d1-3743b61b91ed: 3rd millennium BC. A cave believed to be that of Lot, nephew of Abraham. A Byzantine church, reservoir, and mosaics surround it — and an inscription inside mentions Lot by name.
descriptions.70f7fe6d-22ad-4883-9f2f-5d810a16daa5: 1st millennium BC. Where the Cephissus emerged from underground, Lower Larymna sat at the junction of Phocis, Locris, and Boeotia — contested for centuries, then annexed by Rome.
descriptions.3e0ef472-929c-4669-ad45-c7a19c78d25f: Around 1000 BC. A 3,000-year corridor of Gandharan grave culture, Buddhist shrines, and Shahi-period ruins — stretching between Chakdara Bridge and Saidu Sharif in the Swat River valley.
descriptions.bb081dcb-3ede-4494-ad64-23bedb36f5b2: 1st century AD. Luguvalium was a Roman timber fort south of the Eden River that grew into a full town — possibly the capital of the 4th-century province of Valentia, now beneath Carlisle.
descriptions.7de8d13e-49dd-42ca-a5cf-9e8fc614fbd7: Roman period. A rock-carved horse relief 1.85 m long, 10 m above ground, with a 10-line inscription detailing cavalry memorial race rules — a monument to a young rider who died in service.
descriptions.dd538ad7-472a-47b0-8a6c-cfc5244134db: 5000-6000 years ago. Lungkeng dates to the Pre-Ceramic period - one of the island's oldest known sites, near the village of Ehluan at the tip of Hengchun Township.
descriptions.9aaf411b-c038-490f-9891-e259fc66ca97: 4th century BC. The only known Lycian tomb in the Hellenic world - its Doric facade imitating a temple's columns and pediment, built as Alexander the Great conquered Lycia in 334 BC.
descriptions.d2295d88-dbe5-4755-8905-ee782722af30: 4th century AD. Lycian rock tombs carved into sheer mountain cliffs — a burial tradition that turned vertical rock faces into monumental architecture, defying gravity and millennia alike.
descriptions.e7cc2c23-894f-456c-b88b-66bd9e52ad0f: 4th century BC. Discovered by accident, this Macedonian-type tomb near Elafochori has distinct Thracian features — an early Hellenistic burial believed to hold a figure of local importance.
descriptions.59a722b9-4281-4426-8144-284e509f2061: 2nd century AD. Part of Rome's city fortifications, this 48 m octagonal tower was rebuilt after fire in 1894 and damaged by earthquake in 1953 — yet it still carries a working clock.
descriptions.c5b89e54-5127-4500-b6b4-e63f35efdc8d: 900–1470 AD. A Chachapoya settlement on the left bank of the Kuntichaka River at 1,900 m — part of the cloud-forest civilization that flourished in the Amazonas highlands before the Inca.
descriptions.21d1b1fc-7be0-456a-9be2-528bf2e7095a: 1438–1530 AD. An Inca site above the Willkanuta River near Patallaqta — also known as Q'inti Marka, Quechua for 'hummingbird village', in the sacred Machu Picchu district.
descriptions.e3df9803-11c3-47ca-8cd2-39265d32470b: Possibly 48,000 BC. A sandstone rock shelter in Arnhem Land - possibly the oldest site of human habitation on the continent, on Mirarr Aboriginal land within sight of Kakadu National Park.
descriptions.0a1ca287-1945-4b9d-bc6a-001bf2aa34c6: 10,000–4500 BC. A Neolithic settlement on eastern Crete notable for unusually large multi-roomed houses with mud-dried brick — a building style closely paralleling Neolithic Knossos.
descriptions.94b971b9-ea1f-4879-8c25-bf59020f891a: Occupied from before 4000 BC to today, Magh Slécht — the 'grave-strewn plain' — is a County Cavan landscape still crowded with megalithic tombs from millennia of continuous habitation.
descriptions.1ac10af9-1ace-4be6-8e02-88dacc77b6c6: 4th century AD. Caves, churches, and settlements cluster within 3 km of the Court Tree - thought to be among the earliest Christian hiding places from Roman persecution in this remote highland region.
descriptions.9ad64db8-ba14-45f4-b565-7bf2c29db1f1: Around 5000 BC. One of the Cucuteni-Trypillian mega-sites, Maidanetske housed thousands - a Neolithic proto-city on the eastern steppe long before cities were supposed to exist.
descriptions.82f2d8e5-e3fa-4782-b580-a7eca3ecad45: Built around 90 AD. The Main Limes used the River Main as a 50 km natural barrier reinforced by watchtowers. Part of the Upper Germanic-Rhaetian Limes — now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
descriptions.ffd325ad-d579-4510-90c7-acb87b753c88: Dated to 3200 BC. A Blackfoot Nation medicine wheel: a 9 m stone cairn encircled by a 27 m cobble ring connected by 28 spokes — one of North America's oldest ceremonial structures.
descriptions.aff614fc-77c7-476a-8079-d88e28451fb6: 1st-5th century AD. Mallkuamaya lies 15 km southwest of Puno - a National Cultural Heritage site set above the altiplano, declared protected by the National Institute of Culture.
descriptions.6b0c9ab6-58dd-4989-a937-b83a957ef665: 3rd century AD. One of three burial mounds at Bergama — 140 m wide, 26 m tall, 80,000 cubic metres of earth. Believed to be Europe's tallest open pyramid-style tomb, still only partially excavated.
descriptions.4c52711a-1bf8-4dc2-a293-865bbddff257: 1st century BC–1500 AD. A Maya coastal trading post on Ambergris Caye with 49 mapped structures — no pyramids, only low platforms. One of the longest-continuously-occupied Maya sites.
descriptions.e59e7ff4-2392-4365-ab67-2b7fc0d90472: Around 500 AD. Buried deep in Copán's Late Classic acropolis, the Margarita Tomb held one of the largest caches ever found with a Maya woman's burial — she was almost certainly royalty.
descriptions.ab06e877-d8c6-497a-b448-7d35499eadbc: 5th century AD. Ruins of a Christian basilica overlaying temples from the 2nd millennium BC - this layered site served as the ancient Maronite Patriarchate through the early Middle Ages.
descriptions.336a2e13-3348-4c15-a0cb-b5523ac32913: 1st century BC. In 435 AD, the Roman city of Margus — built on lands once held by Thracians, Dacians, and Celts — hosted the fateful treaty between Byzantium and Attila the Hun.
descriptions.5ed144bd-59e1-4611-a462-a3098bea5231: Maria Reiche decoded the Nazca Lines - geoglyphs drawn 1,500 years ago, invisible from the ground. She convinced the Air Force to fly her over them and published a landmark theory about their purpose.
descriptions.6098d612-4f78-437a-87cb-739b74f254a4: 1000-1500 AD. Markansaya sits in Haquira District of Cotabambas Province - an Apurimac highland settlement whose full archaeological record has not yet been documented.
descriptions.a3542353-6daa-4b24-bb8e-4bf0fb8bb3af: 1st-5th century AD. Markapukyu clings to a slope at 3,787 m in the Pasco highlands - a pre-Hispanic settlement in Yarusyacán District whose full extent has not been mapped.
descriptions.1c4b5554-8ffd-45ca-862f-c4c80d9cb627: 2400-2000 BC. The most extensively excavated Early Bronze Age site of its period - an agricultural village with a long stratigraphic sequence revealing how Philia culture developed over centuries.
descriptions.975e371e-6ada-4865-97f0-320c94ea8803: 3200–2200 BC. A fortified hilltop settlement on Amorgos island with ten centuries of Early Cycladic habitation — from the Grotta-Pelos culture to the Kastri phase, then reused in the Roman era.
descriptions.648faca1-d0ae-4830-83f6-54efdf0231fe: 500–900 AD. Hidden along the Cotahuasi Canyon, Marpa preserves Inca road segments, agricultural terraces, staircases, and ancient tombs barely explored by anyone before 1994.
descriptions.71187888-1c5d-4629-9eba-7ca241f2e650: 1438–1530 AD. An Inca complex of 200+ stone buildings and tombs at 3,700 m, with an ushnu platform and three massive towers — overlooking the village of San Antonio in Arequipa Region.
descriptions.5ae4b331-f6a3-4307-9b5a-6c4c65f111b3: 500–1000 AD. The largest complex in the Cotahuasi valley — built by the Wari, held by the Allcca, then seized by the Inca as a center of religious and military control on highland trade routes.
descriptions.69fb2e9b-8dda-4cfa-b5de-63ce3015c978: 1000–1500 AD. Mawk'allaqta in Melgar Province, Puno Region — a protected National Heritage site in the high Andean altiplano, one of many settlements bearing this ancient Quechua name.
descriptions.63b855c8-c281-42d8-87ea-58aeeec070ef: 1000–1500 AD. Mawk'allaqta in Sandia Province sits in cloud-forest highlands — a National Heritage site named 'old town' in Quechua, echoing the people who once built and lived here.
descriptions.10998951-4382-4ed8-89ee-df2831d4d910: 1438–1530 AD. An Inca settlement in Calca Province near Taray — part of the dense constellation of Inca sites surrounding the Sacred Valley, placed above its fertile terraced floor.
descriptions.85a6e978-d910-4e7d-9158-d1f8fae88dc0: 4th millennium BC. Two necropolises straddle the road near Maxta — the Iron Age Qarabulaq necropolis on one side, and an older prehistoric burial ground on the other, in Nakhchivan's plains.
descriptions.b8583e63-17c5-48b0-a4d1-018acaf608c1: 300 BC–100 AD. Two Iron Age villages once floated within Meare Pool on the Somerset Levels — a bog lake now drained. Each village mirrors the nearby Glastonbury Lake Village in form and era.
descriptions.5f22c11c-22a4-4776-9120-75b3b9e33687: 1st century AD. A Medusa floor mosaic in the ancient city of Kibyra, 95% intact. Made by Opus Sectile — red, green, and white marble forming a gorgon's face with serpent hair and petrifying eyes.
descriptions.6eaec8c3-97e1-4e7b-b1d8-96b14c96a323: 4500–3500 BC. A late Neolithic and early Eneolithic site in Šumadija — part of the Vinča culture's final phase, when the first evidence of metallurgy appeared before the culture vanished.
descriptions.e4af0fdf-eef8-4b9f-ae5b-3e9329df9904: Around 2850 BC. A 4,700-year-old Megalithic Plaza crowns a Cajamarca mountain — found by accident. The same site holds cave paintings estimated at 15,000 years old, among the oldest in the Americas.
descriptions.a4d1130a-68fb-4acd-8b77-5088ace9a377: 500 BC-1 AD. A megalithic wall rising through Gubbio in Umbria - a massive pre-Roman stonework structure anchoring one of the most dramatically terraced ancient hill towns of the central peninsula.
descriptions.069317ea-0971-47f0-acf2-306fb08a9ab2: 500 BC–1000 AD. Seven megalithic statues at Rindu Hati, alongside dolmens, menhirs, and flat stones — part of a regional cluster of 1,027 artifacts spread across 40 sites in Lahat Regency.
descriptions.75f8edbd-7b29-4e09-a72a-9dd5f03e5caf: 6th–4th century BC. The Megarian Treasury at Delphi bore 26 inscriptions naming Megaran citizens — the clue that identified it. It stood beside the Sacred Way within Apollo's sanctuary.
descriptions.f74566a1-f68f-4eb8-a766-fab2e2b5d5af: 4th century BC. A burial mound enclosing a chamber with a pyramidal vault, accessed through a dromos of smooth-hewn stone blocks - an ancient burial from the era of steppe kingdoms.
descriptions.63220a54-b953-4e72-a914-8f564b8f3e11: 800 BC–100 AD. An Iron Age hillfort on the Peak District's western edge overlooking the Cheshire Plain — with traces of activity stretching back to 8,000 BC and Bronze Age funerary use on its summit.
descriptions.d7f5b63f-d9a6-41a4-b491-7ba11aa9cc96: 4th millennium BC. Standing stones scattered across Sardinia — difficult to date, often forming circles and horseshoe rings used for religious ceremony and sometimes concealing burial chambers.
descriptions.01c36727-31bd-45ae-9908-5c7043403cd2: Opened 1959. Housed in an eclectic Baroque-Neoclassical palace, the Palacio Cantón museum in Mérida traces Yucatán's pre-Hispanic past through permanent collections and rotating exhibitions.
descriptions.da96e8cb-3233-429c-a7e1-2cc6341b1de3: 800 BC-350 AD. A Nubian pyramid field with around 100 structures in northern and southern cemeteries - the northern group best preserved, spanning over a millennium of burial at this ancient site.
descriptions.78dcb136-e26a-4653-b586-6b75dd96ccb4: 9th–4th century BC. Excavated in 1930 by the Swedish Cyprus Expedition, Mersinaki's river-delta sanctuary yielded large terracotta sculptures of bearded males, now in Stockholm's Medelhavsmuseet.
descriptions.8a803c31-0a18-4f3f-9873-718323e0b3c9: 9th century BC. Bronze Age tombs at Mərdangöl yielded gray and pink ceramics, iron fragments, bronze ornaments, and strings of beads — a burial culture paralleling the nearby Khalikeshan necropolis.
descriptions.cdecef79-7895-4765-af67-14e60868a220: 500-1445 AD. Carved 22 km from Tacna - fighting, dancing, and hunting scenes in low relief. Spanning nearly a thousand years of carving, Miculla ranks among the most-visited rock art in the region.
descriptions.c432a566-45d9-4f37-9d53-58363a10dc8c: 2nd century BC-1st century AD. A La Tene settlement near Vrsac with pottery, jewelry, fibulae, and weapons spanning three centuries - evidence of Celtic cultural presence in this northeastern region.
descriptions.a212357c-20d5-4919-ad73-ce33af5fc23f: 98-117 AD. Built under Emperor Trajan over a 5,300-seat Hellenistic theatre, the Roman venue at Miletus held 15,000 spectators - one of the ancient Aegean world's greatest performance spaces.
descriptions.8ba6876d-8e26-43b8-82fc-2489646c82f0: 600 BC-1200 AD. A Maya site on the North Vaca Plateau with an elite acropolis, ritual courts, and a wider community. Its monuments show Late Classic Caracol-style features and ancestor shrines.
descriptions.68e1b08b-3997-45bf-a5fe-7a6938279ce4: 3rd–2nd millennium BC. A Minoan peak sanctuary on eastern Crete — a high-altitude sacred site used for offerings and ritual, looking out over the Aegean from the island's rugged eastern highlands.
descriptions.6a4de08f-3148-483b-8b5e-ac6ddbc1e8d8: 250–950 AD. A Maya Classic and Post-Classic site just north of Bolonchén — its carved stone facades now mostly eroded. The sacred Caves of Xtacunbilxunan lie just to the south.
descriptions.df891fda-0a06-48a3-a265-97c9b3138d23: 1000-1500 AD. Mirq'imarka overlooks Moho Province in the Puno Region - a National Cultural Heritage site in the high Andes, declared protected by the National Institute of Culture.
descriptions.e84cfda2-96f8-46f8-86ec-1d0c9d62ed1a: 5th millennium BC. A tidal islet in East Lokris occupied from the Neolithic through the Early Iron Age — a Bronze Age boat and burials found here, with settlement evidence spanning thousands of years.
descriptions.6b3ad5d3-b81b-41d1-ad99-b0cf89f78b86: 1st-5th century AD. Miyu Pampa sits at 3,434 m just 500 m northeast of Jircan in the Huamalies highlands - a pre-Hispanic Andean settlement awaiting systematic study.
descriptions.f452eac9-a36e-4315-9dd3-58c2c382837f: Around 1200 BC. A Bronze Age tomb discovered in 1979 during refugee settlement construction - now buried beneath a Larnaca supermarket, its unexcavated layers sealed under the city block.
descriptions.7cecf4ab-47ef-4c15-90bb-e6ba491732e2: 1st millennium BC. An Iron Age hillfort at 310 m on Mockham Down in Devon — a multi-ditch rampart enclosure with a companion fort 2 km to the west, commanding the high ground above Devon's valleys.
descriptions.53044c53-72a0-44aa-a412-73f5dc64414b: 2nd century AD. All that remains of the triumphal arch of Mettius Modestus - a Roman governor's monument standing in ruin, a stone fragment of imperial power long since dissolved.
descriptions.43c12659-d785-44da-ab9b-e0e5fedee349: 1st-5th century AD. Molloko lies 5 km south of Acora in Puno Province - a National Cultural Heritage site on the high altiplano, 5 km south of the town of Acora near the village of Molloco.
descriptions.80a20be9-edef-45dc-9b97-a79c80eafdf3: 2500–1200 BC. Monagrillo holds the oldest ceramics in Central America, verified by radiocarbon dating. This coastal site also provides some of the region's earliest evidence of maize agriculture.
descriptions.e89f8ecd-2c72-4d59-8618-315d5b0e2361: 2500–2000 BC. Known as Su Casteddu, this Copper Age fortress in northwestern Sardinia was built by a pre-Nuragic people using massive megalithic boulders shaped to the natural terrain contours.
descriptions.000da27c-0797-4e58-a979-ae97b3d5016f: 4500–3000 BC. Monte Lazzu is a prehistoric settlement in Casaglione, Corsica — an island whose rugged interior sheltered Neolithic communities long before the wider Mediterranean world took notice.
descriptions.36d0cdd3-3586-46c5-bf1e-8cb4a70e1f6c: 3rd century AD. The last of London's Roman wall gates to be built, Moorgate opened onto the marshy Moorfields beyond the city's edge — standing for fifteen centuries before demolition in 1762.
descriptions.8b1c31bf-cb48-4569-a027-361881157742: Around 2200 BC. A square earthwork 180 m per side near the Wansdyke in Wiltshire - 3.25 hectares ringed by a bank and outer ditch. Its alignment and original purpose remain unknown.
descriptions.b71930be-a00f-44aa-acc0-496e80d3b949: 2nd–4th century AD. A Roman fort at the crossroads of the Fosse Way and the Durnovaria-Isca road — its ditch still visible. A civilian settlement grew nearby, with what may have been a large mansio.
descriptions.86aa32d3-94cb-4b60-a5f0-d6673219ee5e: 19th century BC. The labyrinthine Mortuary Temple of Hawara so baffled ancient visitors that Late Antiquity ranked it a wonder of the world. Its twelve courts and galleries still defy full mapping.
descriptions.62c8bf00-3a7e-46e6-81ac-2c6fc92af03f: 2nd–10th century AD. Mount Namsan was sacred to the Silla Kingdom — covered in Buddhist carvings, outdoor pagodas, and palace ruins. UNESCO called it one of the world's largest outdoor museums.
descriptions.927cd0d5-2d53-456d-b215-deb419ddf0b9: 2nd–1st millennium BC. A conical hill forgotten for centuries — rediscovered in 1990 by Berkeley archaeologists. Plutarch records it as the site of a monument to two heroes of Chaeronea.
descriptions.0eaedf34-031e-4b8f-8fff-2db84a3e6da6: 4th–1st millennium BC. Moylehid in Fermanagh contains the Eagle's Knoll Cairn Passage Tomb — a scheduled monument in a townland occupied for thousands of years; its name means 'hill of breadth'.
descriptions.47c64a3b-69e3-4fb9-b15d-907ff357b777: Circa 1500 BC. Over 400 Aboriginal paintings and stencils cover this rock overhang in Victoria — one of the state's richest rock art sites, with occupation dating back at least 3,500 years.
descriptions.c8855169-8cd1-40ae-9f2a-cfc8be715d8b: 1000-1500 AD. Mulinuyuq lies in Huanta Province, Ayacucho Region - a pre-Inca or Inca-era highland settlement awaiting systematic excavation in one of the Andes' most archaeologically rich regions.
descriptions.54e2461b-5a65-4da6-9e73-10b14a813736: 1000–1500 AD. A pre-Inca site at 4,000 m atop Mullu Q'awa mountain in Espinar Province — near the village of Molloccahua, in a high-altitude landscape that tested everyone who chose to settle here.
descriptions.3f9bdb7e-9739-47db-b323-1935cf6ea8d6: Founded 177 BC. The Roman colony of Luni included an amphitheatre built in the 2nd century AD — still visitable today within the excavation area, alongside finds in the on-site national museum.
descriptions.9108b193-4370-4997-a271-7d20836efeed: Opened 2005. A 17th-century seafront fortress — once the largest of eight bastions protecting Campeche — now displays architectural elements from all four Mayan regional styles found in the state.
descriptions.a457cbdf-37c9-4b06-b59c-fdfecc8ba582: 600–1000 AD. The on-site Wari museum displays ceramics, bone remains, and lithic objects from excavations — visual evidence of a highland empire that preceded the Inca by five centuries.
descriptions.c1e49d01-2e46-4ecc-af7f-1fd39555fc8e: Opened 1980. The second-largest anthropological collection in the country - four Mesoamerican cultures from Tabasco, in a museum in the capital city of Villahermosa on the Gulf Coast lowlands.
descriptions.d48eb704-d535-4be7-9695-868ee650cbb7: Opened 1986. An 18th-century fort turned museum — its standout exhibit is a jade mask pulled from a Maya tomb. Inside: obsidian tools, ceramics, and Maya funeral customs before Spanish contact.
descriptions.fc84c8b7-697c-4ee3-924b-e412f5585c2b: The Mut Precinct at Karnak contains at least six temples - the Mut Temple, the Contra Temple, and Temples A, B, C, and D. One of four compounds that together form the Karnak Temple Complex.
descriptions.7a339d92-507c-43e2-8eef-ff924f8c4231: 1000–1500 AD. An archaeological complex in Uranmarca District, Apurímac Region — whose circular name ('circle circle' in Quechua) may describe the rounded layout of its ancient highland structures.
descriptions.af860ca9-85af-4444-8f71-8e56282d7cb4: 1st millennium BC. A promontory hillfort above the East Lyn River in Devon at 150 m — a spur of hillside naturally defended on three sides by steep valley walls, with an Iron Age enclosure on top.
descriptions.eb9e5db8-a757-4451-8af7-b5eb273a5c9d: 2nd millennium BC. Bronze Age rectangular tombs at Nakhchivan, covered in stone slabs 1 m long, oriented north to south. Excavations found pottery, bronze ornaments, and the bones of the interred.
descriptions.db0c6ae2-38d9-47b7-ae27-e6a960c0294e: 1st millennium BC. A tomb complex near Pyongyang - one of the oldest burial sites on the peninsula, offering rare physical evidence of the ancient societies that preceded the unified kingdoms.
descriptions.4f616866-4a3f-4754-9855-193df8e63fdc: 3rd century BC–7th century AD. Narona began as a Greek trading post on the Illyrian coast, grew into a Roman stronghold, and survived into the Byzantine era — its name still a Catholic titular see.
descriptions.138007c5-f824-446e-84ad-cf44e7cfde76: Built around 500-900 AD. Among the oldest windmills in the world - clay, straw, and wood built to withstand 119 km/h winds. Nashtifan's vertical-axis turbines have milled grain for several centuries.
descriptions.1c573084-c7d7-4072-84c3-30adc4b6c521: Around 100 BC. Dacian stone-and-timber fortresses in the Sureanu Mountains - strongholds of a fierce people who held off the Roman advance for decades before finally falling to imperial conquest.
descriptions.51c8708e-d263-400a-ae34-57d52ca69638: Around 40,000 BC. In 1866, a fragmented human mandible and ulna were found at Naulette cave in Wallonia - an early Neanderthal fossil discovery, now housed in the Brussels Natural History Museum.
descriptions.e4b003f4-3f62-4689-9af9-4b7f120614af: 1st century AD. Recorded by Ptolemy in his Geographia — its Latin name meaning 'dock' or 'wharf', recently linked to Essen. Exact coordinates remain uncertain due to ancient scribal copying errors.
descriptions.221d4702-9626-4430-a71f-d5b70bcb9d4e: 3300–2100 BC. A prehistoric funerary naveta — a boat-shaped stone monument built by ancient Balearic islanders to house their collective dead, in continuous use for more than a thousand years.
descriptions.2a7e3b61-6a76-4f1a-8c4a-e0d895a129a5: Andean settlement at 4,030 m on the border of Cayara and Huancapi, above the Kinwamayu valley. One of several pre-Inca hilltop sites clustered in the remote Ayacucho highlands.
descriptions.9f5cf21d-173d-4387-bbf7-ac5b06ee134b: Pre-Inca highland site in Huanca Sancos Province. Declared National Cultural Heritage -- evidence of Andean occupation spanning centuries in one of Ayacucho's most remote zones.
descriptions.b54d2d6a-d3d4-442e-9cf4-1ddd1bf1073e: Settlement crowning Mount Nawpallaqta in Lucanas Province, southeast of the Puka Urqu site. One node in a network of interconnected pre-Inca mountaintop communities across the Ayacucho highlands.
descriptions.90d24652-a268-43f6-904c-97fdf6e97a9b: Built 900 AD by the Popoloca. A pyramid with two circular altars where prisoners were sacrificed to Xipe Totec after gladiatorial combat. Two large skulls carved from volcanic stone were found here.
descriptions.8e1eefb4-5472-43ee-8963-19e2d5a5ddac: 5th c. BC to 4th c. AD -- the key ruins of Greek-Roman Syracuse: the Latomie quarry, a Greek theatre, and a Roman amphitheatre still partly standing, all on a single rocky headland.
descriptions.0efed5d0-3ba7-4512-bc3f-0f166c290e76: Early Minoan I tholos tomb of river-bed rocks, c. 3000 BC. Only one body and two vases found inside -- yet its design mirrors Cyclades tombs, hinting at Bronze Age contact across the Aegean.
descriptions.d34647f5-e2ba-48e4-a5f1-12eec767b7ed: A grand piano-shaped boulder on Ilkley Moor bearing sparse cup marks. Near the Swastika Stone, its purpose has never been agreed upon by archaeologists who have studied it for generations.
descriptions.74cdba2f-95fb-48fe-a583-5671be149d2c: 6th-2nd century BC settlement on a narrow plateau above two ditches on the Via Clodia. Its fame rests on the spectacular rocky necropoli nearby -- a display of aristocratic wealth.
descriptions.1e8b10e4-1124-4f35-9557-27a57d7dc4a1: Necropolis near Pydna, spanning Bronze Age to early Christian times. Tomb finds reveal a shrinking population during the second colonisation wave -- the dead recording a slow civilisational decline.
descriptions.ca33a292-b102-4efe-b644-48959d8ff741: Built 1279-1213 BC by Ramesses II. Six colossal statues over 10 m tall flank the facade -- unique in ancient art for showing king and consort at identical scale, elevating Nefertari to goddess rank.
descriptions.d3dde28f-ad70-41ce-b5b4-6bb943aebbee: Neolithic cairn 30 m across, excavated 1929 after stone was robbed for road-building. Two cists with grooved joints survive; cup marks and a rare axehead carving decorate the southern cist.
descriptions.7adac3e8-3eef-4c99-a403-e0ef8f6be97e: Neolithic cairn in Kilmartin Glen -- one of five in a linear cemetery stretching across the valley floor, in one of the most concentrated prehistoric landscapes in northwest Europe.
descriptions.4c05fdee-8903-43a8-ab47-0a6d688e04c1: Oldest monument in Kilmartin Glen's linear cemetery -- a 4th millennium BC Clyde-type chambered cairn. Originally 40 m wide and 4 m high, with an inner chamber over 6 m long inside.
descriptions.ad6d3859-ae7c-41cd-9d16-1e13101be9a0: Neolithic standing stones in Kilmartin Glen: four menhirs in pairs 70 m apart, a central menhir ringed by seven smaller stones, and one further menhir pointing northwest toward Temple Wood circle.
descriptions.1c8d0a2b-245b-4b60-877e-92ffbc77117f: Iron Age hill fort on a clifftop 110 m above sea level near Combe Martin, Devon. An earthwork enclosure of the first millennium BC on a hill shoulder above the north Devon coast.
descriptions.fa425008-1b60-43fa-8ac9-31b17fba3821: Cave occupied since 18,000 BC within Krowathunkooloong Gunaikurnai country. Excavations in the 1980s found stone tools and finger-marks pressed into dried mud on the ceiling -- preserved 20,000 years.
descriptions.07dc6a1e-928e-428d-b9d6-804d93a51a3a: Wartberg culture gallery grave, 4th-3rd millennium BC in Hesse. Uniquely important for its sequence of collective burial layers -- a stratified Neolithic archive preserved within one megalithic tomb.
descriptions.afb20664-90a8-4e20-bc76-d6c524f5ede0: Stone chullpa tomb complex in Lucanas Province, declared National Cultural Heritage in 2002. Funerary towers mark the high-altitude burial landscape of pre-Inca communities across the Ayacucho region.
descriptions.50e2e3a4-4f3e-4b1e-bd7a-8b97404f59c8: 2500-800 BC Arctic settlement 15 km south of Sisimiut. Organic materials preserved in permafrost make Nipisat Island one of the best windows into the island's earliest human occupation.
descriptions.b05b08cb-d006-40fb-8488-325f3a94bba0: Settled since 4,800 BC by the Lengyel culture -- nicknamed the local Troy for its multi-layered tell. Millennia of accumulated strata on this mound within what is now the quiet town of Surany.
descriptions.f510b136-b416-4769-b5eb-e9eb314bf001: Maya city founded c. 800 BC with a rare planned urban grid. More than 15 buildings line a ceremonial axis from the Middle Preclassic -- centuries before most Mesoamerican cities achieved such order.
descriptions.d13aa6ef-bc9c-4815-968e-35bbf1543e9a: 3rd-1st century BC Buddhist stupas in Gilgit-Baltistan -- the uppermost valley where trade routes converged at the mountain frontier. A rare early Buddhist presence deep in the high passes.
descriptions.a7e94c62-5d36-44f7-9ee4-4691bdefd1ca: 2nd century BC northern gate of ancient Hierapolis. The surviving archway marks the entrance to a once-flourishing city at the confluence of classical worlds in the uplands of western Anatolia.
descriptions.fe9d2d34-c026-44cd-9883-86b23c96c962: Ceremonial petroglyph site and ancient animal facility listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1996. Its location is deliberately withheld from the public record to protect it.
descriptions.02c9fcff-1d24-401b-913d-67becef3d50d: Built 883-859 BC at Nimrud for Ashurnasirpal II. Throne-room reliefs show the king crushing enemies and performing rites with protective genies -- carved in stunning detail across entire palace wings.
descriptions.46c6cf72-8616-4f4c-8993-73c50abdd6a5: A sanctuary carved into the mountainside at 1,850 m -- a 7-metre sculpture of the Patroness of Shepherds, by sculptor Antonio Duarte. A striking monument set into the living rock of a high ridge.
descriptions.c027b744-d439-4b77-8375-c32f95ebb6f6: Cave burial site, c. 900 AD. Farmers found 167 bodies in a cave in Chiapas -- part of an ancient burial ground. The site lies on the Nuevo Ojo de Agua ranch.
descriptions.59addc11-6d49-46ad-ae86-608c00d56f85: 5th century BC Greek harbour colony on the Illyrian coast, 5 km north of Lissus. One of the earliest Greek colonies on the eastern Adriatic -- a Milesian trading post at what is now Shengjin.
descriptions.af071bf2-f99f-4bf3-84d6-67093c74e5dd: Iron Age hill fort in Cheshire -- one of only seven in the county and unusually low-lying for its type. Scheduled as an Ancient Monument in a region where hill forts are exceptionally rare.
descriptions.ad600526-95f6-434d-9440-38ce0688b441: Late 7th century BC -- Milesian Greeks founded a colony at a Thracian site. One of the oldest settlements in the region; earliest pottery dated 600-575 BC places its founding in the reign of Astyages.
descriptions.0415d29e-5239-40c6-ab1d-5b19e443336b: Minoan religious complex with two tholos tombs used for over 1,000 years in Crete's Asterousia mountains. Finds include gold diadems, a gold bracelet, seal stones, amulets, and stone vases.
descriptions.28a8e565-a9c1-4a1d-90ee-d889b0c372db: 1300 BC Mycenaean palace on Ithaca, believed to be Homer's Odysseus. Excavators found two levels linked by rock-cut stairs, storerooms, workshops, a funerary enclosure, and a drainage system.
descriptions.077ae374-79a5-41ae-9bc0-c547adc3164e: Ruins at 900 m on Mount Oiti's slope, thought to be the ancient Dorian city of Dryopis. Outside Oinochori village in Phocis -- scattered stones from a settlement largely lost to time.
descriptions.8ee50417-7d0d-416f-b3b9-6e1971d7004b: A 3,000-year-old rock carving discovered 2009. The figure wears a jaguar-head belt buckle, comb-like ear ornaments, and a headdress bearing a sprouting corn god's face -- carved on the Pacific coast.
descriptions.11aae1cf-691a-45a5-a873-e4ac938587b2: 3rd century BC to 15th century AD -- Hellenistic, Roman, and Byzantine layers. Polygonal masonry in the oldest houses; smooth cut stone later. Cisterns, sarcophagi, and church ruins mark each era.
descriptions.f9ad013b-8208-4a02-8480-7c865c7577f6: Built 1502 on a steep cliff after a rebel attack. A 1504 ceasefire was signed within its walls -- then destroyed shortly after by mercenary forces fighting for the Norwegian-allied rebels.
descriptions.72ca2dcc-e6fc-44a2-93b1-c575e50929dc: 5th-4th century BC city of the Amantes, on the border of northern Epirus and southern Illyria. Fortified between the late 5th and early 4th century BC at the edge of two ancient worlds.
descriptions.701fb49d-eb89-4c8e-8cb7-972c74ff811b: 1st century BC Celtic oppidum on the Lindenhof hill, likely founded by the Helvetii. The fortified hilltop that became Zurich -- its moraine promontory is now the city's historic public square.
descriptions.b6ebcc56-b637-44ad-9250-de406a647169: Alacahoyuk -- four civilisations in sequence: Late Chalcolithic, Hatti Bronze Age tombs, then Hittite Sphinx Gate and temples. Royal graves here transformed understanding of the Hatti civilisation.
descriptions.7eba70f1-aa71-47c7-9ccd-80ff5f1fb4cf: Early Neolithic settlement at 2,400 m near the Qanligol reservoir, partly submerged today. Artefacts appeared only after riverbank erosion exposed them, revealing a community dating to c. 10,000 BC.
descriptions.f177368d-855d-4e9e-824a-647213ffccc4: 1st century AD village in inland Dalmatia with finds spanning Stone Age to Roman Empire. An early Christian church ruin adds another layer to continuous habitation on this Dalmatian hillside.
descriptions.2051a8ae-6ce5-4a33-bfa6-997ed2479750: Shinto shrine beside an ancient quarry, famous for a huge man-carved rectangular stone of unknown purpose. The massive block cut from the living quarry face has defied explanation since records began.
descriptions.d799bb0f-8ffd-4a29-a516-ffd445f6b699: Largest Anglo-Saxon cemetery in Northamptonshire -- 15 hectares excavated in 2019. Over 160 skeletons and 70 square barrows of the Arras culture, with a range of grave goods.
descriptions.4f5d500f-4c00-48a8-a048-6a3deb43f76a: Prehistoric site in the commune of Sartene, Corsica. One of many sites on this island whose archaeology reflects millennia of settlement in the western Mediterranean.
descriptions.a996a5d6-dd44-441f-9616-b912c06f7f75: 200-900 AD Maya city with temple-mounds 8-20 m high, some atop modified hills. Its upper plaza was built on a reshaped ridge 300 m long and 30 m high -- the landscape itself became the architecture.
descriptions.cb8cc790-ac27-4f13-afb0-b12a3cf4e6db: Pre-Roman megalithic walls near Tornareccio, Chieti. Massive polygonal limestone blocks without mortar in Cyclopean fashion -- among the most striking pre-Roman dry-stone masonry in the region.
descriptions.ab80e2e4-7195-48ad-84fc-582925fe9504: Fishing village, 2000-1200 BC -- the oldest known settlement near Huanchaco. A temple served ritual before shark-hunting voyages, linking today's coastal communities to their Prehispanic ancestors.
descriptions.d7a08c8b-4f1a-4067-a197-11922b0e34c6: 3rd century BC to 2nd century AD -- 24 rock-cut caves on the Trivashmi Hills, excavated by Jain saints. Monasteries, shrines, cisterns, pillars, and Hinayana Buddhist carvings fill the system.
descriptions.daa1ea4b-c002-4552-a4ef-45d996c6cea6: A 12-m, 15-tonne limestone block lying 40 m underwater in the Sicily Channel. The area last stood above sea level c. 10,000 years ago -- possibly one of the oldest submerged megaliths ever found.
descriptions.dcbbad93-6d45-4a6f-93a7-a9a3887295aa: Museum housing elongated Paracas skulls from royalty who vanished 2,000 years ago -- DNA testing of the remains is now being initiated. Five civilisations represented, spanning 2,500 years.
descriptions.e1c3365d-f89e-468e-a928-8e5db1210844: 1000-1500 AD Andean hilltop site in the Arequipa Region with towers, round houses, and distinctive black walls. Set above the Colca River in Caylloma Province -- pre-Inca highland stone architecture.
descriptions.b20cd52c-284d-46fd-9cb9-abefb3a42f9d: Late Neolithic hilltop site on the west bank of the Nestos, 6th-5th millennium BC. Five trenches yielded 400 kg of pottery in 1976 -- extraordinary volume from a densely occupied prehistoric site.
descriptions.317314f2-db25-4249-a5b7-f388a2042839: 5th century BC citadel held for seven centuries on the Lazio hills. Monumental polygonal walls, domus with mosaics, and vast public temples survive -- Norba stood until Rome's civil wars consumed it.
descriptions.9803a37d-458e-445c-9fec-8d94a0f89f1c: Founded 709 BC. Sarcophagi, grave goods, and ancient artefacts have been recovered from this necropolis -- remnants of one of the oldest cities on the Propontis shore.
descriptions.e258fc5f-e771-442a-9c65-3839a084199a: 3rd century BC to 4th century AD. Around 40 houses of polygonal bossed blocks survive alongside cisterns, caves, a Roman Grave House, and the fortified ruin complex Barakciikale.
descriptions.da35c9fa-fd61-4188-96c6-342d9b0789e9: Pre-Classic Maya settlement in the Puuc region, c. 2000 BC to 250 AD. One of the earliest sites in the limestone hills -- Maya occupation long before the great city-building era began.
descriptions.f66cb628-f017-4f87-a2f6-b15da9ec4f8f: Built 64 AD by Emperor Nero. Its podium-and-tower structure on the Lycian coast guided ships along one of the Mediterranean's most important maritime routes -- one of antiquity's key lighthouses.
descriptions.710c3160-5b62-42df-af62-62557101ba13: 3rd century BC Greek theatre at ancient Patara on the Lycian coast. Among the oldest theatres in the region, its stone tiers survive in the ruined heart of this once-prosperous city.
descriptions.925c2577-4b50-4955-a0f0-f6eb032518e3: 2nd-1st century BC parliament building at Patara -- seat of the Lycian League. A multi-phase structure rebuilt into the late Byzantine era, among the oldest surviving federal assembly buildings.
descriptions.90b26e72-6627-453c-8d18-3e472c15a292: 3rd century AD Pisidian city with a basilica, temples, baths, alabastra reliefs, a sanctuary, and tombs. Pednelissos held a hilltop in a region of fiercely independent cities that long resisted Rome.
descriptions.7bbee517-515c-4fe4-9271-036ea36791e1: Bronze Age site on the Kola Peninsula from which ancient DNA was recovered. The genetic material opens a window into subarctic peoples of the 3rd-2nd millennium BC -- Europe's most remote frontier.
descriptions.63bb1b7d-6a64-43d9-8459-1d9606932658: Iron Age hill fort on coastal cliffs around 80 m above the sea near Peppercombe. Much of the site may be lost to erosion -- its boundaries barely traceable on maps, the sea slowly claiming the fort.
descriptions.69dd4372-657e-4a25-99bf-fdc8614a9e97: 4000-3600 BC Cucuteni-Trypillia mega-settlement covering 100 hectares -- a proto-city before cities existed. One of 2,440 such sites across the steppe -- a vast, long-forgotten civilisation.
descriptions.8c54ae5f-16b5-4ac1-9ae7-0d6e0a3eb0a6: 1st-2nd century AD colonnaded street of ancient Perge, linking the nympheum to the acropolis past every major building. The social spine of one of the wealthiest cities on the Pamphylian coast.
descriptions.1249652f-d141-4928-84ca-cc5c310111a3: Called 'Hill of Fairies', settled as early as 4300 BC along the Zhob River. Excavated 1924, it showed strong Harappan resemblance -- a pre-Indus site on the fringes of Balochistan's civilisation.
descriptions.9d0a034a-c362-4f11-a437-76484f145981: 2nd millennium BC fortified settlement on the Ishim River -- namesake of the Sintashta-Petrovka culture. These steppe peoples invented the war chariot, one of history's most consequential weapons.
descriptions.d28a0fac-0bfa-4c3f-a6c7-c616617e9286: Built c. 90 AD on a 42-metre Jurassic hillspur in Bavaria. Double V-shaped ditches cut from bedrock survive. Part of the Rhaetian Limes -- Rome's northern frontier, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
descriptions.de237c9a-268b-41d6-90ad-497adc00a19c: 11th century BC hieroglyphic petroglyph found near Tayma oasis in 2010 -- the first confirmed Egyptian inscription in Arabia. Located 400 km north of Madinah, it rewrites the map of pharaonic reach.
descriptions.d77a438c-c78c-4fcd-9116-7c1cb77e4bb5: 5th century BC to 6th century AD city on the Pisatis isthmus. Medieval builders raised a castle called Pontikokastro atop the Hellenic walls -- two civilisations fused on one ridge.
descriptions.71f6f6f1-0cc8-4e43-9f9f-89ae7a635ffa: Late Minoan IIIA tholos tomb, discovered 1981, with at least 9 burials. Grave goods: a gold necklace of 28 rosettes, 15 seal stones, amulets, bronze weapons, and ivory warrior plaques.
descriptions.a80b06cb-b249-4f98-b9dd-e4bede83b2db: Cave in the Mendip Hills occupied since 33,000 BC -- a scheduled monument on Crook Peak. Named after M. J. Picken, who found badger-disturbed teeth and triggered the first archaeological dig.
descriptions.c70f123f-bf31-4408-8204-1b8ef717e0dd: Occupied 50 BC to 5th century AD, starting as a late Iron Age settlement before Roman construction created a large villa. Its finds are displayed in a deconsecrated 1851 chapel on the village edge.
descriptions.f66a1c0a-665e-4442-88bb-2faee85ebb97: 7th century BC to 10th century AD -- one of the most powerful Maya cities on the Usumacinta River. Its history is written across carved stelae and altars recovered throughout the site.
descriptions.57c8634d-3306-4f87-81e0-fe3f4d07e367: Bronze Age settlement found during road construction, excavated 2009 across 1,000 sq m. In continuous use through a classical farm and a Roman vineyard -- three eras of occupation at one site.
descriptions.1718bb59-ad26-498d-9803-548afc83cca7: Inhabited since the 7th millennium BC at the foot of Mount Olympus. Continuously occupied in the Middle Neolithic (5600-4500 BC); a Bronze Age necropolis of burial mounds was established later.
descriptions.c621bee7-f67e-4969-8bb0-d9b801d14e0f: Radiocarbon dates suggest presence here 22,200 to 14,700 years ago -- among the earliest in South America, though disputed. Part of the Ayacucho cave complex alongside Jaya Machay, the 'pepper cave'.
descriptions.adc55f80-0185-4eae-a227-ccc3885007be: 1st-5th century AD settlement on Mount Pilluchu at 3,800 m in Vilcas Huaman Province. Set southwest of Vilcashuaman, a highland site marking Andean occupation at the limits of the cultivable zone.
descriptions.db9e04a9-afe5-4541-8ae4-0d7c5b14facc: Pre-Inca hilltop site on Mount Pirca Pirca in La Libertad Region. One of many Andean summits bearing traces of occupation that predate the Inca expansion into the north.
descriptions.29efc463-cdf8-4dd6-849b-ff378c87a2de: 1000-1500 AD Andean site north of Lake Paucarcocha in Yauyos Province. Pirca Pirca preserves traces of the pre-Inca communities that occupied remote high-altitude lake-basin landscapes.
descriptions.72b1b9e1-8e84-402b-b1bd-a7161527bca5: 1st-5th century AD site on Mount Pirwayuq at 3,900 m in Tayacaja Province, Huancavelica Region. A high Andean summit site in the Laria District, marking pre-Inca occupation of remote mountain terrain.
descriptions.1b6a888a-c95a-46b3-b798-293b1c2cfe4b: 3rd century BC to 4th century AD Hellenistic-Roman city on a fortified hilltop. Stone walls, west-facing towers, agora, olive workshops, houses, and tombs survive -- all in poor condition.
descriptions.c86e3d9b-38c0-478a-8d06-e91f90c2859d: Discovered 2014 near Pocklington -- over 160 skeletons and 70 square barrows of the Arras culture, 8th-3rd century BC. The largest Iron Age cemetery in the East Riding, with rich grave goods.
descriptions.b3aacfb1-87e7-448e-b6a3-1c394670aad3: Hill fort at Bugojno, first inhabited 2500-1700 BC, abandoned for four centuries, then reoccupied in the Iron Age until the 3rd century BC. Its strata defined a late Bronze Age cultural group.
descriptions.34272ded-e2dd-47ab-b771-f3fc4a68b1bb: Pre-Roman megalithic walls of Amelia -- massive polygonal limestone blocks without mortar encircling a hilltop in Umbria. Among the most dramatic ancient masonry surviving in the region.
descriptions.353aa183-ed5a-4fa8-8894-3f3ff922cb58: 1st century AD Roman military site near Honiton -- fort or marching camp. Timber-and-earth rampart, two deep ditches with ankle-breaker bases, and biological evidence of a cavalry garrison.
descriptions.090861ff-b5c9-4848-84e3-9407cf27189e: 2nd century BC -- Rome's oldest stone bridge. Rebuilt in stone to span the Tiber between the Forum Boarium and Trastevere. Today a single arch survives mid-river: Ponte Rotto, the Broken Bridge.
descriptions.34f757be-a065-458c-9200-05b3beeeca2c: c. 1500 BC Bronze Age cemetery of at least 11 round barrows south of Grantham. Five were quarried away in 1959; the remaining six are scheduled as ancient monuments in Lincolnshire.
descriptions.d0f8e6a4-9c45-4e1a-a4d6-c76efaacc88c: 1st century AD Roman viaduct c. 1,500 m long, crossing the Aude marshes -- longer than Trajan's bridge over the Danube. Today almost nothing remains except its name, preserved by a nearby wine estate.
descriptions.d3a35b0d-cf76-4286-8cd4-2f53e52556ad: 5th century BC Greek acropolis at Selinunte on a hill between two rivers. Post-409 BC houses had 4-9 m facades; acropolis walls of square blocks flanked by towers, repeatedly restored over centuries.
descriptions.60212fa1-b2c0-4262-a434-adb4ade54b04: Iron Age hill fort at 180 m in Devon, unexcavated and bisected by a modern road. An incomplete earthwork enclosure holding undisturbed deposits never formally investigated by archaeologists.
descriptions.dd567577-49dc-45a4-99a9-7beffeb43afe: Built 3838 BC on the Somerset Levels -- about 30 years older than the Sweet Track. Long ash planks on hazel and lime posts at 3-m intervals carried Neolithic travellers across a waterlogged landscape.
descriptions.9aa9f2ff-0dbc-46d3-af26-fea8cafd030b: 5th century BC settlement on the Kupa river opposite Ozalj Castle. The castle museum holds a Neolithic Lengyel stone axe found here -- evidence of prehistoric habitation at this riverside site.
descriptions.c0526e60-577b-4f28-9a07-e3c5739984bd: 1st-3rd century AD Roman encampment on the Old Rhine -- the northern frontier of the Empire. Named after Vipsania Agrippina, mother of Emperor Caligula. A key fort in the Cananefates tribal territory.
descriptions.e6fed564-7213-4395-9814-1c24d0c08287: Minoan settlement on Crete, occupied c. 3100-1100 BC. One of many island sites representing a civilisation that dominated the Aegean for two millennia before its sudden and still-debated collapse.
descriptions.182f18fe-36ea-42c8-9a43-cbbc37d052a6: A Middle Miocene paleontological site -- a major European mammalian locality. Fossils tens of millions of years old, from an era when extinct mammals roamed what is now a quiet village in Blace.
descriptions.42931e1d-8e60-4257-be40-5eb70202aa97: 3rd millennium BC rock-art site in the Alijo municipality with cave paintings. Designated a Special Classification Zone in 2006, preserving hilltop artwork from the late prehistoric period.
descriptions.10be8151-2981-40f5-9f0d-23b66b2d8fef: Iron Age community that continued through the 11th century in Siem Reap. An Angkorian temple was built atop a 1st-6th century cemetery -- the living deliberately building a shrine above their dead.
descriptions.cb688193-2ff5-4535-b1a7-af488587a451: Prehistoric site in the commune of Altagene, Corsica. One of the island's less-documented sites in a landscape that has yielded traces of occupation since the Neolithic.
descriptions.8414ca9b-404d-49df-9aa9-6fe545ccac80: 5th-4th millennium BC unchambered long barrow in Hampshire. A medieval iron spearhead and a seax blade found inside -- later peoples revisiting a Neolithic mound and depositing objects within it.
descriptions.e500a4eb-0731-4902-8380-c5a19a9d2a2b: Iron Age multivallate hill fort on a 133-metre conical hill in Cornwall. Two distinct circular ramparts are visible despite heavy tree cover -- a commanding stronghold above the Cornish landscape.
descriptions.44cb696e-f084-4a89-982c-bcedd857bbea: 6th century BC theatre at Priene -- the ancient Ionian city. Its carved stone seating is among the oldest in the region, a rare survivor from an era of early monumental civic architecture.
descriptions.7b39da13-0cb0-43cd-a3a8-a22b9c990ca1: 1st century BC Roman bridge with a single ashlar arch and brick vault, built to resist flash floods. It carried travellers and trade goods for centuries along this southern road.
descriptions.2b3667ad-f83a-4514-8ef9-62231a454215: Prehistoric site in the commune of Sotta, Corsica. One of many sites in the island's southern interior representing a long tradition of habitation on Corsica.
descriptions.64137ead-762b-4621-a59c-5c7395ef4826: 1000-1500 AD Andean complex in Caylloma Province. Buildings, stone chullpa tombs, qullqa storage deposits, and walls on slopes above the road from Chivay to Coporaque in the Colca Canyon corridor.
descriptions.faf8f8ee-c092-48a8-a712-1133df65badd: 1st-5th century AD hilltop site across three peaks at 3,860 m above the Lucanamarca River in Victor Fajardo Province. Set west of the Qaracha River, commanding the high Andean interior.
descriptions.d1fd88e8-1e77-4bc2-859e-d72632d37500: 1000-1500 AD fortress-settlement at 3,700 m on Mount Pukara in Vilcas Huaman Province. The summit is noted as a natural viewpoint over the surrounding Andean landscape.
descriptions.0f32e3d9-176a-4860-afcf-3994d049b1b1: 1st-5th century AD mountaintop site at 3,800 m in Lucanas Province, north of San Cristobal. The site lies northwest of the Nawpallaqta complex in the high Andean zone of Ayacucho Region.
descriptions.58486903-37c4-4aa4-866f-f7f8d66205ac: 1000-1500 AD archaeological park in the San Sebastian District, on the Pumamarka river. Declared National Cultural Heritage -- an Inca-era site in the heart of the Cusco Region.
descriptions.1cf08f5b-a8a8-4e06-a586-17ae6d0cf153: 1000-1500 AD Inca-period site at the confluence of the Patakancha and Yuraqmayu rivers in Urubamba Province. In Ollantaytambo District, within one of the Inca Empire's densest archaeological zones.
descriptions.ff073eff-d177-480d-85c3-6151ca4ee652: Also known as Castillo de Gorioj or Tucumachay -- a castle-type site at 3,696 m in Huamalies Province, Huanuco. Defensive highland architecture at the fringes of pre-Inca Andean mountain territory.
descriptions.018c0c9d-c85f-4ed9-86eb-8cf350ec83e7: Pre-Columbian cave with rock art, 22 metres deep and 30 metres wide. Bone remains confirm it served as a burial ground for Inca-era communities in the Cusco highlands.
descriptions.dd8e1148-5057-4496-a859-5f28c798a3f6: Maya site active 250–950 AD in the Petexbatún region. Three groups — north, east, and west — share a main plaza and acropolis, arranged across a defended peninsula.
descriptions.99328522-518c-40cd-94a1-b541906c3f00: Inca-era archaeological site perched at 3,267 metres in the Ayacucho highlands. Sits between two ancient villages and doubles as a viewpoint over the surrounding mountain landscape.
descriptions.bc13a236-675e-46b4-8cb1-b5e86d9fbd97: Inca-era site near Cusco consisting of a single monumental wall climbing the flank of Mount Puqin. A sparse but deliberate structure — one wall, one mountain, no clear explanation.
descriptions.357287dd-81db-4190-968d-1bf3b094ab84: Dated 2570–2320 BC, this Late Archaic settlement in Michoacán holds the oldest known burial site in Mesoamerica — predating the Aztec and Maya civilizations by millennia.
descriptions.3b1e3e4c-8a94-4d84-af05-213813dca141: Purépecha settlement covering 2 hectares with houses, temples, plazas, and agricultural terraces. A rival to the Aztec Empire, it was slowly abandoned as Tzintzuntzan rose to power around 1500 AD.
descriptions.251c792e-1079-4785-8e4b-d879c9e1a938: Chachapoya culture site active 900–1470 AD on a cloud-forest mountain in the Amazonas Region. One of two Purunllacta sites — a sister settlement to the larger complex in the Soloco District.
descriptions.6cc29702-81c5-4a0a-bc3e-a62de9545b3a: Deep in Manú National Park, a government permit is required to enter. Over 30 metres of perpendicular cliff face holds deeply incised carvings reaching 2.7 metres high — purpose still debated.
descriptions.1ba7f4a6-05cf-44d6-9a94-0381df32d379: Late Classic Maya city active 570–798 AD. Pusilhá is unique in the Maya world for preserving the only surviving example of ancient Maya bridge construction, positioned at a major trade crossroads.
descriptions.c70fe2a7-a7d0-4b6e-b59d-b4d1510573bf: Wari culture tomb complex in the Huanta highlands of Ayacucho. The tombs date to the Wari imperial period, 500–1000 AD, when this culture dominated much of the Andean world.
descriptions.eb2c2736-4019-4ef4-8e0d-5e444af09de7: 2nd–3rd century AD Roman arch-gravity dam in Aragon — one of the earliest known dams of this structural type, engineered to hold water for Roman agricultural and urban supply networks.
descriptions.765bec0e-b003-467c-aee3-d142f184c66d: 1st-century AD Roman road linking the Iceni capital at Venta Icenorum to the legionary base at Camulodunum, later extended toward Londinium — a lifeline connecting the conquered east of Britannia.
descriptions.2fc65539-6b0f-4073-9db3-76dadc408cc8: 26th-century BC pyramid of Hetepheres I — wife of Sneferu, mother of Khufu, grandmother of Khafre. Her titles included God's Daughter of His Body, set in the shadow of Giza.
descriptions.20f12dcd-f2a7-4014-9dce-160c90b27749: 1st-century AD Roman settlement in Pannonia, sited on the road between Poetovio and Siscia. Believed to lie near today's village of Komin — a minor node in Rome's Danubian road network.
