descriptions.9c3e1746-6da1-412c-aeb3-eb61cb3cafbb: 1st–2nd century AD settlement near Ismailli. In 1899 a silver plate 24 cm across was unearthed nearby depicting a mounted Nereid surrounded by tritons and cupids — Hellenistic art far from Rome.
descriptions.0b54890b-b30b-4836-9c8c-805cf88a4a21: Rock painting site at 3,782 metres above sea level on the flank of Mount Qayakuna in Pasco Region. The paintings are sheltered at the edge of the high-altitude village of Quchaq.
descriptions.9910d3da-4875-49eb-8da4-3f2db69a48a6: Middle Kingdom temple in the Faiyum, dated to the 2nd millennium BC. Its plan links it to an era when pharaonic builders were experimenting with new forms of sacred architecture.
descriptions.60ae4c7a-9c8e-49cf-b85b-d49d8022787c: Two Roman temples near the summit of Mount Hermon, with walls carved directly out of solid bedrock. A contested border dispute between neighbouring states has left the site poorly documented.
descriptions.5a2e082b-8ed8-4116-b5c3-5414826f0d92: Temple of limestone blocks fitted without mortar, with oblique corner joints — a construction technique that has puzzled archaeologists. No inscriptions, no clear date, no identified deity.
descriptions.b6516127-fbfb-4b63-895a-96e3b6c7dd2f: Two Roman temples on a high plateau, one Prostylos with four monolithic columns — one still standing. Excavations nearby recovered a bust of Helios, god of the sun, from the western sanctuary.
descriptions.3ac3c796-1538-47b5-8985-6807adf8dec3: Well-preserved Ptolemaic temple, 323–30 BC, built of yellow limestone blocks 65 km from Fayoum. No inscriptions survive to pin a precise date — its builders left no names, only stone.
descriptions.7240c7dc-cd45-45f3-a291-7db1f48ce667: Inca-period site atop a mountain in the Calca Province, active 1438–1530 AD. One of many high-altitude Inca installations commanding the Sacred Valley approaches near Cusco.
descriptions.23cd75bc-22da-4f28-aa83-f527fdf84e2e: Eight Thule-period Inuit mummies found in 1972 — naturally preserved by cold dry air. Six adults and two children, offering insights into Arctic diet, disease, and daily life 500 years ago.
descriptions.29bbdfce-7b18-4530-b668-8a2fb289694b: Occupied 5500 BC through the Inca era — first Lake Titicaca basin site to be systematically excavated. Archaeologists found 36 distinct cultural strata, from hunter-gatherers to Andean farmers.
descriptions.64ad25a0-6088-470f-a0f0-368159ceb43e: A prehistoric lunisolar calendar carved into rock atop a Canary Islands volcano. The site also features Atlantic petroglyphs, cart-ruts, channel structures, and possible megalithic buildings.
descriptions.b05d0398-066b-453d-8deb-772025b120eb: Rock painting site on a mountainside west of Huánuco at 2,463 metres elevation. The imagery survives on a steep slope, exposed to weather but still visible to those who make the climb.
descriptions.4cab063f-a1a1-4e24-a46a-d609f2f87f53: Rock painting site in the Huamalíes highlands, dated broadly to the 1st millennium BC. One of many rock art sites scattered across the upper Huánuco Region at high altitude.
descriptions.b622ebae-c26d-4aef-a028-15edc1596f02: Classic Maya city occupied 200–1200 AD along the lower Motagua River trade corridor. Its ruler captured and sacrificed the king of Copán in 738 AD — an act that stunned the Maya world.
descriptions.517e41aa-be07-4b3b-9b44-1a6a77de304e: Inca-era site in the Ancash highlands, Yungay Province, in the southern part of Yanama District. Few details have been excavated — it remains one of many unnamed Inca settlements awaiting study.
descriptions.a2b571fa-4aa3-4c23-b5f0-13c5552ce870: Royal estate of Inca emperor Huayna Capac, built 1464–1525 AD in the Sacred Valley at 2,910 metres. Such estates concentrated wealth in the emperor's bloodline and served as fortified country palaces.
descriptions.643fcd04-bed6-4bf0-8362-75ebb0544e1c: Inca site in the San Sebastián District of Cusco, active 1438–1530 AD. One of many administrative settlements that ringed the Inca capital, managing flow of goods and people into the city.
descriptions.80fa4dec-a12f-4604-b92e-bfa32b2e0ef6: Wari-period archaeological zone in the Huamanga Province of Ayacucho. The site sits within the heartland of the Wari state, which dominated Andean civilization 600–1000 AD.
descriptions.c6fa5dc5-1eda-405f-97d2-9338392a8054: Inca-period site in the Abancay Province of Apurímac. Located in the Huanipaca District, it remains among the hundreds of unexcavated Inca settlements in the high Andean valleys.
descriptions.50e8bf7e-7d23-4d69-9526-14c928d81672: Inca site in the Ollantaytambo District, active 1438–1530 AD. Perched on the Rayanniyuq River, it belonged to the community of the same name — a satellite of the great Ollantaytambo complex.
descriptions.6a4cdd7d-42a8-4952-a1b9-7d6bb44f090a: Agricultural terraces 4 km north of Zurite in the Anta Province of Cusco. The terracing system is one of hundreds that transformed Andean hillsides into productive land under Inca engineering.
descriptions.1bc1ab56-9d6f-478e-a4aa-76bdd91f61ee: Inca site with two platforms — Hatun and Huch'uy Quri Wayrachina — near Mount Inka Pallanka, still venerated as an apu by locals. Active 1438–1530 AD in the Lucanas Province of Ayacucho.
descriptions.23098ff4-34c5-4071-8298-97e16d7bae84: Inca settlement discovered in 2001 in the Willkapampa mountains, north of Choquequirao. Close to ancient Inca mines, surrounding hills are littered with stones from over 20 ancient mining shafts.
descriptions.e212d748-501b-4c73-bdf7-7e96fbeabf35: 15th-century Wancas-period site with circular stone buildings at 3,850 metres in Junín Region. The circular plan sets it apart from standard Inca rectangular construction on the surrounding slopes.
descriptions.2dceb336-e4a4-4a99-9f88-00c83aaa0088: 5th–9th century Maya capital near Copán. Abandoned in 822 AD when the Copán kingdom collapsed — one of dozens of satellite cities that fell silent as the Classic Maya world unraveled.
descriptions.d9bf804c-0891-424e-a272-cb3681d3497a: Houses one of South America's finest collections of stone sculptures, mostly from the Recuay (400 BC–600 AD) and Wari (600–1100 AD) cultures. The collection also includes mummies and trepanned skulls.
descriptions.8ece5123-5b53-4545-929d-0519137c13ea: 4th-century BC arch bridge discovered in 1966 near the eastern harbour of Rhodes. The oldest known voussoir arch bridge of the ancient world — a modest span that outlasted every empire that used it.
descriptions.cc700fa7-64f3-46d6-9a97-7223f1c4d15d: Built 2200–1950 BC as the southernmost cairn in a linear cemetery. Later repurposed as a lime kiln, then excavated by Gordon Childe in 1936 — possibly the burial place of a local king.
descriptions.b9b20a90-518f-46c2-9390-6dbded1b148f: Classic Maya city with 53 structures — squares, patios, terraces, residential and ceremonial zones — active 250–900 AD, some 20 km from the Copán Ruins along a key western trade corridor.
descriptions.fac04898-9342-436f-8a58-df8061d72fcc: Early Classic Maya site active 250–600 AD in the Petén jungle. Covers 1.3 square kilometres with 729 major structures, near the borders of two neighbouring countries in dense tropical forest.
descriptions.f4188020-1870-4ba4-ad15-f162b33e1605: Iron Age bank-and-ditch enclosure dated 1200 BC–1st century AD in West Somerset. Almost square in plan with rounded corners, covering just 0.28 hectares — small, defensible, and little excavated.
descriptions.86e1dff8-20ac-4d49-85d8-480ee0b9f3ed: Neolithic causewayed enclosure built 4000–3000 BC, just 4 km northwest of Stonehenge. It predates the great stones by over a millennium — the earliest known ceremonial monument on Salisbury Plain.
descriptions.e8235f8c-e30c-4c97-8297-639b2681d46b: Hunting culture rock carvings from 4500 BC on a 20 square metre field above Malangen fjord. At least 8 reindeer figures, plus porpoise, a boat, and possibly a moose — a frozen glimpse of Arctic life.
descriptions.b8e5e38c-b300-4fdb-8ef1-ab136542504b: Two moose carved onto a rock near the river Fossen — one 31 cm, the other 35 cm. Dating to the 6th millennium BC, their position beside the river leaves them submerged during high water levels.
descriptions.5668cd67-4c06-4795-93f6-5c223e748ba7: One of Northern Europe's largest rock carving sites with over 2,000 petroglyphs, carved 4000–2000 BC along the Frøysjøen strait. Accessible only by boat or a 5 km hike through remote coastline.
descriptions.d8888428-c233-4936-b1c4-7bfc8c4d5bed: Geological formations outside Chattanooga shaped into corridors, balanced boulders, and tight squeezes along a 1,250-metre trail. Over 400 native plant species grow among the ancient sandstone.
descriptions.c663e466-6644-4d97-9fb5-24d85eddb646: Paleolithic rock shelter with an engraved figure — trapezoid head ending in branch-like points, tail and erect phallus — interpreted as a sorcerer. Similar carvings appear in Spain and France.
descriptions.74c2c902-db56-411f-b98f-6711a6825b48: Strange rock formations on private land near the Cypress Hills. Almost nothing is known about their origin or purpose — access requires permission, and researchers have barely begun to investigate.
descriptions.ece7f01a-17bf-4b09-afc9-8368b323a88b: Diorite rock formation where the Killke culture and later Incas carved benches, altars, and steps. The natural polished channels on the hillside — not carved — remain unexplained by any theory.
descriptions.417b5d77-c70a-40ad-adad-7f92ef1a0544: Remains of a Roman agora in active use from the 1st century BC through the 5th century AD. The marketplace served as the civic and commercial heart of the ancient city that once surrounded it.
descriptions.fac932af-fd71-4fca-93a7-508c6fbf5546: Two Roman aqueducts built 1st–2nd century AD to supply Toletum (Toledo). The main reservoir at Mazarambroz included a ruined dam — still partially traceable across the modern landscape.
descriptions.c211a54e-09f3-4a34-a50d-a00ab351c9a4: 1st-century AD Roman bridge over the Oued Mina at the entrance to Relizane. One of the westernmost surviving examples of Roman bridge engineering on the North African frontier.
descriptions.1a26d6f1-d77a-4bb4-a018-afb806a4cd15: Roman kiln complex discovered in 1966 just 300 metres from a beach in Algeciras. Part of Portus Albus, it supplied containers to the processing industries of the neighbouring city of Iulia Traducta.
descriptions.9a47c62e-0961-4e76-b253-a62b8d0bac87: 1st-century AD Roman water chambers beneath Toledo, discovered in 1628. One large arched gallery feeds three parallel vaulted galleries that once supplied thermal baths at the Plaza de Amador.
descriptions.28b7b9c1-3901-4762-a71f-353d6ba8b513: 1st-century AD Roman road, part of Ermine Street north of Doncaster. The bridleway still runs at an angle between modern roads — its Roman alignment cutting through suburban parkland.
descriptions.0b69c962-04ae-4c4a-a624-6398b6f856b1: 1st-century AD Graeco-Roman temple with 30-metre foundations. Its columns were stripped and reused in local construction — the building's bones absorbed into the villages that grew around it.
descriptions.4e168b2a-9dd9-45ee-b569-c126d7e37faa: 2nd-century AD Roman temple, described as well-preserved. The ruins retain enough structural integrity to reveal the original form and proportions, though excavation records are sparse.
descriptions.028c6de5-3b1b-4061-95ba-6ed5896f5030: 1st-century AD system of Roman walls and vaults beneath Calle Nuncio Viejo in Toledo. Part of a network that includes Roman baths and the cisterns of Delegación de Hacienda — a city built on a city.
descriptions.97ecf20f-9ce3-44d1-98ba-931c8335c386: Roman villa occupied 1st–5th century AD in Loures. Excavations in 1995 found burial tombs, salting tanks, incendiary remnants, wall fragments, and a capital — a layered estate ending in fire.
descriptions.ff9059d2-71be-4973-8e79-b9f034f8b772: Roman villa occupied 1st–6th century AD in Cascais. Built at the height of Roman influence on the Iberian Peninsula, the site continued to be used across several centuries of shifting power.
descriptions.d9023096-4bef-47a7-bcb4-2e3f4cf0ba36: 3rd–4th century Roman villa in Amadora linked to a nearby aqueduct. Excavations found a mortar tank and Chalcedony mining evidence — luxury stone extraction alongside ordinary estate life.
descriptions.d4f646ca-4d92-48d8-87a1-6920ff00c3e3: 3rd-century Roman settlement in Meda with mosaics from the 3rd–4th centuries. Earlier occupation may reach the Neolithic, based on silica and quartz fragments uncovered during excavation.
descriptions.cc5593cb-94d3-4c98-a3fa-b71a0a23a44c: Roman villa found during residential development in Cascais. Terra sigillata sherds and a probable necropolis span the Iron Age through Moorish intervention — centuries compressed into one site.
descriptions.77c8e01e-c8c8-4667-99f2-e36c81d6c0f8: Six defensive wall systems built around Rome from the 8th century BC to the 17th century AD. The earliest circuits are still largely traceable — 2,500 years of fortification layered in stone.
descriptions.4b8583a1-da7c-4bf9-a702-05298be4227c: Remains of a fortified Roman city. The theatre is its most visible surviving element, one remnant of a once-walled urban settlement that controlled the surrounding region during the Imperial period.
descriptions.270c2134-0bdc-4874-a038-d1b7c0bd80a4: Paintings found in 2010, making this the oldest known cave art in southeast Europe. Bone tools date to 35,000 BC — yet the cave had been excavated since the 1800s without anyone noticing the art.
descriptions.5fd8a068-ea2a-46e7-a2b3-4ca669d83d1e: Greek colony founded on the Costa Brava, possibly 8th century BC by settlers from Rhodes. Classical sources name it Rhode — a fishing port that became a bishopric and eventually a modern tourist town.
descriptions.95034077-b765-40f7-aefc-7e4f660613f3: 2nd–3rd century AD temple of Mithras at Vindobala on Hadrian's Wall. Located 137 metres west of the garrison — where soldiers worshipped in secret, beyond the edge of the empire's known world.
descriptions.6814a205-8ebc-46b8-8581-94c1cbb06745: 5th-millennium BC copper mine with shafts cut into the hillside and scaffolding for ore access — among the earliest evidence of European copper mining. Pottery links it firmly to the Vinča culture.
descriptions.06704996-075d-49e6-8374-32adb32d8f61: 4th-century AD Roman city of Bobadela preserving an amphitheatre, original columns, and arched structures. A small provincial settlement that outlasted the empire that built it.
descriptions.ac47b022-0aee-44d7-8fbf-87797a6a2589: 1st-century BC Roman city of Emérita Augusta, now Mérida. The site preserves a theatre, amphitheatre, circus, the Temple of Diana, and the towering Aqueduct of Miracles — a full Roman city in stone.
descriptions.acb24767-be50-43e6-8ef9-10ff2f9e810a: Archaeological site at 3,400 metres in Huaytará Province. Ruins on the flanks of Mount Runayuq — one of many high-altitude settlements that dotted the Inca road network through the Andes.
descriptions.0ef8b7fe-16dc-40d6-b75f-1392cce86584: 1st-century AD Roman road running from Deva (Chester) to Derventio (Derby) through the northern Midlands. Victorian antiquarians called it the Via Devina — not to be confused with Icknield Street.
descriptions.fc4faaa4-8ba5-47d3-a055-b194ebc0162e: 4th-century AD Lycian cave and tombs complex. Natural cave formations combined with carved funerary chambers — a blend of geology and ritual typical of the Lycian burial tradition near Antalya.
descriptions.aae112c2-9dcc-4901-a9fe-4f511fe80905: Purépecha city founded around 900 AD in the Lake Pátzcuaro Basin. LiDAR scanning revealed an estimated 39,000 buildings hidden under vegetation — a metropolis invisible from the ground until 2016.
descriptions.5df03f8d-0b22-4188-b7ae-ccd2b00d8f47: Classic Maya city active 550–950 AD, split into five numbered sub-sites along the Mopan River. A triadic complex in Plaza C signals participation in pan-Maya political and religious networks.
descriptions.a978ec11-4ffc-4aee-8052-46dc4fd30785: 4th-millennium BC settlement on the Sadarak plain. A Bronze Age ruin called 'Div hörən' — Built by Giant — was so massive that locals attributed its construction to supernatural forces.
descriptions.1dfccf93-13b6-46cf-a719-8cfd1683e097: Antonine Fountain built 161–180 AD under Marcus Aurelius. Twenty-eight metres wide, nine metres tall, clad in seven-coloured stone and Afyon marble, with sculptures of Dionysus on its face.
descriptions.6cb33a13-f9ad-476e-8ab6-fe2b286103b2: High-altitude Roman city, one of the best-preserved provincial towns of the Imperial period. Occupation began in the 8th millennium BC — by the time Rome arrived, the site was already ancient.
descriptions.64b2e0cd-cd66-4612-802e-d0789d8f8b14: 4th–3rd millennium BC tell near Kandahar, 200 metres square and 8 metres high. Dense Helmand culture Bronze Age evidence — one of the best-documented prehistoric sites in the Kandahar Plain.
descriptions.fc029995-b6bb-4375-a5fa-9a0eb7d0fa85: 7th-century AD stone monument site with multiple carved pieces including turtle-shaped and coin-shaped stonework. The exact purpose of the objects is unclear — ritual function is suspected.
descriptions.0d141532-586a-4a6f-bfa0-78186786402e: Ancient settlement built around the salt marsh of Lake Salpi in Daunia. Mentioned by Pliny, Ptolemy, and Strabo, Salapia had a bishop by 314 AD before the see was transferred to Trani.
descriptions.beb7f985-afb1-48b4-a77c-daffe463deba: Roman port colony of Civitas Salditana under Augustus — a crossroads between eastern and western North Africa. Trade networks here stretched from Carthaginian times through Byzantine withdrawal.
descriptions.85ed945a-9d3c-437c-97b5-adf0cf0b3a9c: Cave at 2,000 metres in Styria with bone tools dated 65,000–31,000 BC — Middle Paleolithic tools found alongside Neolithic hearths. Discovered by hunters sheltering from a storm in 1924.
descriptions.9fadbce6-f8cc-4db8-ba65-c15f6f82dbdf: Late Preclassic Maya site in the Petén jungle with murals showing Olmec influence. A 30-metre pyramid and undeciphered early Maya script — unknown to archaeology until the late 20th century.
descriptions.12d91def-e436-431c-b21b-bba500145eaa: Classic Maya village near flint sources, occupied 200 BC–900 AD. Over 90 structures identified but few excavated — a flint-tool production centre, not a political capital, serving the wider region.
descriptions.8107d407-8094-4f0b-b459-54b2a43e1864: Sacred to Artemis since the Neolithic, with a fortified hilltop occupied 2000–1600 BC. The inlet has silted up since antiquity — the sanctuary now sits further from the sea than when it was built.
descriptions.f29afd0d-6fb8-4405-bee8-c1b17a6989e3: Maya site occupied 800 BC–900 AD, spanning Formative and Classic eras. One of the earliest settlements in the region, 1 km from the modern community that shares its name.
descriptions.37d54e47-00e9-4647-82c8-3ee56814692d: Moche ceremonial funerary complex, active 400–1000 AD. Royal tombs with elaborate burial goods reveal a culture that transformed funerary rites into spectacle, power, and political performance.
descriptions.742f0fe0-05b2-4a5a-9c5b-473bc25f6c40: Cenote 20 metres deep, accessed by rappelling through a village well. Archaeological finds confirm pre-Hispanic ritual use — the dive is dangerous and access limited or prohibited entirely.
descriptions.31c2fc86-3acf-4684-99dc-9f1b35e0f3b4: Mayan shrine to the goddess Ixchel, in use from 2000 BC until the Spanish conquest in 1539 AD. One of the longest continuously active sacred sites in Mesoamerica — over three millennia of offerings.
descriptions.78b62602-3ab7-4e2a-8773-9752ba771aa7: 15th-century Inca citadel built by Emperor Pachacutec in the Sacred Valley. Massive stone blocks form temples, sanctuaries, and water channels that survived the Spanish conquest largely intact.
descriptions.7ef03e67-8439-4a61-84ab-c5e92424e17a: Caudini city near the frontier of Campania, attacked by Rome during the First Samnite War in 343 BC. Ceramic evidence shows Saticula was part of a regional trade network along the Volturno River.
descriptions.626e8712-71b4-48ac-9b58-8440bade0fcc: 3rd–4th century AD Mithraic shrine in Roman Savaria. Two stone altars with relief scenes from the life of Mithras survive, alongside fragments of coffered ceiling paintings currently being restored.
descriptions.f2041141-c82a-4e04-a6e6-d7d2e29f4ea5: Funnelbeaker culture passage grave, built 3500–2800 BC. Reused in the Bronze or Iron Age, excavated in 1969–70, then physically relocated to its current site for long-term preservation.
descriptions.f15d2047-cd5a-4524-b39a-06ab10d77f36: Iron Age hill fort in Devon using a single massive linear rampart to cut off a coastal promontory at 125 metres elevation. Its unusual promontory layout sets it apart from most forts in the southwest.
descriptions.2a956522-6ffd-4ab1-be5c-dc17990dfa79: Early Formative pyramid complex, 2000–1500 BC. The main temple measures 350 by 300 metres and stands 35 metres tall — one of the largest architectural structures in the ancient Americas of its era.
descriptions.803f8912-22af-46a8-82e3-bde675d8e5f3: Greek city founded 550 BC, now the largest archaeological site in Europe. Five major temples crown an acropolis above a walled settlement — an entire ancient city preserved in one coastal park.
descriptions.a2e28715-eafa-4ac4-9bb3-1deaf34864b5: Etruscan stone monument site from around 750 BC. Several carved stones have been interpreted as altars — some possibly repurposed in the Roman period, leaving the site's full history unresolved.
descriptions.934ed584-2c13-46fc-bf38-eadd53b68d6f: Cucuteni-Trypillia settlements, 5500–2750 BC, spanning southeastern Europe. Some housed thousands of people — among the largest Neolithic communities on Earth before vanishing entirely.
descriptions.ebf764c6-27e7-45d9-834a-3f660c82193b: 2nd-century AD complex with three temples, a summit shrine, an altar, and a structure of unknown function. A fourth temple sits at the village's lowest point — an entire hillside built around worship.
descriptions.f967e3c4-fc5b-4cd0-91d1-06030d51e31c: Tell Harmal, 5 metres high and 150 metres across. Excavations 1945–1963 uncovered 2,000 tablets — including versions of Gilgamesh, the Flood, and Creation myths among the oldest literature ever found.
descriptions.898f67da-9f3f-46ca-bc0d-d91d1d58ae45: Karakoram Highway crossing used by traders, pilgrims, and armies for centuries. Sasanian-era rock carvings left by passing travellers make it one of the best-documented ancient crossroads in Asia.
descriptions.c04dfddb-2904-41a4-9351-18f4e6f79907: Bronze Age enclosure of 0.5 hectares near Cerne Abbas, occupied 2500–800 BC. A Martin Down style domestic settlement on chalk downland — one of many such farmsteads once found across the Dorset hills.
descriptions.c3b60256-57d1-4b74-80f0-1a2536795a20: Neolithic village of mud-walled houses occupied 5000–2500 BC in the Bannu District. Stone foundations and wattle-and-daub roofs sheltered a few hundred people over two and a half thousand years.
descriptions.f7fec312-2d2f-4dc7-87dd-a425ddbfa454: Pre-Pottery Neolithic B settlement near Limassol, 9th–8th millennium BC. Cattle were present early on but died out by the 8th millennium — gone entirely until a separate later reintroduction.
descriptions.abfa8b60-ea29-4150-925f-87d4b1fe8092: Carved in 1973 AD, this 12-metre monolithic sculpture of Lord Bahubali ranks 3rd among five such statues in Karnataka. A recently completed stone monument in the tradition of devotional sculpture.
descriptions.a2e7ed0a-b619-4b9c-8626-6bfac777e811: 4th-5th century AD bath mosaic from the era of Lazica. Found in 1961, its apodyterium floor (2 x 3.5 m) lay buried under 15 cm of lime — a rare glimpse of Late Antique bathing culture in the Caucasus.
descriptions.57fdae55-1910-4354-b9d3-76d7525c6bc7: 5th-4th millennium BC Cucuteni-Trypillian settlement, one of 2,440 such sites across the region. Excavations reveal a vanished civilisation of large proto-urban villages from the 5th to early 4th.
descriptions.01e7b609-0bfd-4cf2-b9a6-91553a137fcc: 2nd-6th century AD Roman fort guarding Volubilis. Garrisoned by the Cohors IV Gallorum equitata — Gaulish cavalry at the edge of empire, abandoned after Rome's 3rd-century near-collapse.
descriptions.7f3c0b8d-671f-4daa-9f4c-e1c447bf241b: 1st century BC Lycian ruins with Cyclopean walls, a Temple of the Augusti, a columned stoa, and a theatre. Inscriptions confirm a gymnasium and baths — never found by archaeologists under the rubble.
descriptions.f6b5aa36-d662-4490-a83b-1e5d857afdd5: 2nd century BC Roman colony on the Tyrrhenian coast, abandoned by the 5th century AD. No Italic town predated it here — Rome built Sinuessa from scratch, and by 500 AD it had vanished from the record.
descriptions.818cc875-92d0-4bc3-be80-704620304599: Buddhist city active 450 BC–1200 AD, perched atop three limestone mesas of the Rohri Hills. Stone and mud-brick walls still crown the summits; architectural remains cling to the slopes below.
descriptions.92ccc418-b751-408f-8187-01f2d2fd8ffa: Around 1200 BC, this citadel rose in the late Bronze Age Harappan tradition — baked brick walls, Indus-style. A stupa of unbaked brick shares the mound: fortress and shrine on the Indus bank.
descriptions.50debb04-ae49-4d55-9756-bdfb8fbacf9c: 1st century AD Roman city at the triple confluence of the Kupa, Sava, and Odra rivers. Originally Celtic-Illyrian Segestica, it became the Roman city of Siscia — a key node on the Danubian frontier.
descriptions.248be59c-06f7-453b-9062-9e254c9da942: 6th century BC to 3rd century AD sanctuary town at the crossroads of two ancient routes. Set in the Alpilles mountains, Glanum is unique in the region
descriptions.d206a73b-2dd6-4552-962b-f76b8420ada8: Active 150-550 AD, Altar de Sacrificios is one of the most intensively-excavated Maya centres in the Peten lowlands. Three monumental complexes — Groups A, B, and C
descriptions.7fc0b9aa-387f-4403-992c-b9648b23b870: Around 2000 BC, abstract images and what may be a calendar were carved into rock here — the most intriguing petroglyphs in the region. Whether it charts seasons or stars remains unanswered.
descriptions.de912183-ceb0-4f02-835c-191dcbaeaec7: 300 BC–1300 AD Maya site with an acropolis and three ceremonial plazas in the Peten Basin. El Chal's East, West, and Northeast Plazas ring a civic core that endured for over 1,600 years.
descriptions.65b59599-1041-4c61-b01f-0c23910ea9d0: Active 450 BC-1250 AD, Motul de San Jose was a medium-sized Maya civic-ceremonial centre that rose as a key political and economic hub during the Late Classic period in the Peten region.
descriptions.52583420-ea5f-42ae-933c-4872c54e0676: 1st millennium BC agricultural village 12 km from the Pacific coast of Parita Bay. An egalitarian community — no elite compounds, just farming families until the Spanish conquest erased it.
descriptions.bebaa4d3-fb8e-46a4-b9cb-fe6589925889: Megalithic site near Pagar Alam City containing several single-chamber megalithic tombs known as dolmens — compact stone burial chambers built from large slabs, grouped on the hillside.
descriptions.cf3b581a-c47f-41c6-9922-48c6e3b8d3a0: The Tebingtinggi megalithic site near Pagar Alam City holds diverse large stone remains: a human figure riding a buffalo, a figure wrapped in a snake, flat stones, a stone mortar,...
descriptions.0e01dd33-edd6-4259-91af-cd6501cd86ef: Iron Age and Romano-British settlement 3.2 km from Corfe Castle, Dorset, with an associated field system. A scheduled monument — a rare, well-preserved example of subsistence farming from 800 BC.
descriptions.019573c7-aff6-4aab-848e-99063cc00b09: Iron Age hill fort near Bratton Fleming, on a hillside promontory about 200 metres above sea level. The surrounding area is rich in small enclosures
descriptions.a7700568-ec6e-45c4-80e9-f4ee85fe31df: Known as the City of Prophets, Sogmatar contains rock tombs, reliefs, and a sacred Chalcolithic mound. Legend holds Moses lived here; Assyrian-era walls still crown the hilltop above ancient wells.
descriptions.ec4ea862-5a28-420c-932a-53c82693b471: 850-300 BC settlement and burial site in Buyeo-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, the type-site of Middle Mumun Culture. Archaeologists use its material culture as the prehistoric Bronze Age benchmark for the.
descriptions.d8cae4fd-fcca-4187-9194-e89fa474bb49: 2500-1300 BC Beaker culture dolmen and associated settlement on the north-west facing coast near Valldemossa. Excavations by Professor Bill Waldren revealed a nearly complete prehistoric settlement.
descriptions.f18385af-ee2f-4a53-8782-5e296874b14c: 4th century BC Lycian settlement noted for its Temple of Apollo with a fish oracle — a dependency of Myra. On site: large sarcophagi, the ruined acropolis, Temple of Apollo,...
descriptions.b2341e58-d5c1-4c9e-8e7a-05a2bc1857f3: 2500-800 BC Bronze Age enclosure on Cranborne Chase, Wiltshire, in the Martin Down style. A scheduled monument with a cemetery of six round barrows nearby, on a gentle slope above a dry valley.
descriptions.14570acc-bcd9-43b4-abca-f7a2a8d9035b: 3300 BC Neolithic long barrow near Beckhampton, 43 metres long and 17 metres wide, 70 metres from the cove of The Longstones. Excavated 1964-66 by Paul Ashbee — no burials found, purpose unknown.
descriptions.03ae634b-9c91-450a-89eb-9e9f79bdb726: 4th millennium BC kurgan cemetery — the oldest known in Transcaucasia. Nine mounds discovered in 2006 by a joint French-led team, linked to similar kurgans at Kavtiskhevi in the South Caucasus.
descriptions.39461539-85ee-47d9-9f64-b6a6587844ec: 8th-4th century BC cult site at Spartia hill near Sesklo, Magnesia. An inscribed dedication names Heracles and Alcmene — found during a rescue excavation alongside the railroad,...
descriptions.9c64a3f6-8874-4441-b6c8-52428a1d45e5: Occupied 12,000-7,000 years ago by Hoabinhian hunter-gatherers at 650 m elevation in Mae Hong Son Province. Excavated in the 1960s by Chester Gorman; the Salween River flows less than 50 km away.
descriptions.639cad5c-6019-4516-92d2-deeb2227db41: 2nd century BC stadium carved into a natural depression in Laodicea ad Lycum, a Phrygian city. Ruins of a gymnasium with a large swimming pool stand on the northeast side — sport and bathing in stone.
descriptions.75385942-4463-40aa-b258-80ff49a77917: Promontory hill fort at Halwell, Devon, on the western edge of a hill about 200 metres above sea level. Stanborough was first listed as a historical heritage in 1923
descriptions.540f24d5-bf3d-40b8-81f7-349d5107fd24: Mega-settlement of the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture, dating 3600-3200 BC, covering 100 hectares. Stina is one of 2,440 such proto-cities discovered so far
descriptions.631de534-1de5-4dbc-ac03-ac5ee63eb84f: Bronze Age settlement in Lower Silesia with occupation continuing into the Early Middle Ages. Stobno has archaeological sites from both eras; first recorded in writing in 1259 under Piast dynastic.
descriptions.d3789a45-3747-4bae-8b9e-88f359f5561d: 1st-5th century AD Wielbark culture site in Pomerania with 10 preserved stone circles, 15-33 metres in diameter. Each ring holds 16-29 upright boulders ranging from 20 to 70 cm above ground level.
descriptions.22bc5858-875a-4603-b94a-866aaf0a14e1: Around 1500 BC, one of inner Caria's most important city-states rose here. The site of Stratonikeia contains a plethora of structures spanning its long history of occupation in western Anatolia.
descriptions.debb506e-ab0d-4e03-876e-320c31ee59d2: Minoan cave 400 m above sea level on Mt. Juktas, Crete. Used from Neolithic times as refuge and burial, then inhabited in Early Minoan times.
descriptions.761f4227-befb-435c-b967-9ebd61c06f8f: Iron Age hillfort enclosing a 14th-century manor house in Dorset. The southern end survives as a two-storey roofless ruin — probably the service range with a room above
descriptions.6faee7c5-517c-4de4-9809-b98a481fff2a: Late Roman settlement whose stone houses were likely summer residences for the Harran Plain. A cave here is venerated as the Prophet Shuayb's dwelling — no comprehensive archaeological research done.
descriptions.838d58ef-f389-42b1-8740-198904bf1cc1: 2nd century BC–3rd century AD hill fort in Maharashtra with temples to Lord Shiva and the patron goddess Bhoraidevi. Sudha Gad fuses military and sacred purpose — fortress and shrine on one summit.
descriptions.6fa3017d-6545-48c6-b54b-c041b9f860b8: 450 BC–1200 AD Buddhist stupa on a mound near Tando Muhammad Khan. Locally called the Tower of Sudheran — believed by some to be a cinerary stupa containing the ashes of the dead.
descriptions.5067da0a-d681-4fe3-91e5-e2dc7c0656d7: Built in 1756 AD, the Sundarnarayan Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. A modest 18th-century shrine marking the continuing vitality of stone temple construction in the region.
descriptions.3bffe60d-acd5-4420-ba6d-7419cb42aee9: Three Bronze Age round barrows near Sunningdale station, dating 3300-500 BC. Excavations on one barrow located cremations, mainly inurned — a long-lived burial ground in what is now Berkshire.
descriptions.f1b3fa7c-d237-4d82-8d06-831a376ce267: 25th-24th century BC sun temple at Abu Ghorab, one of only six or seven built by the Fifth Dynasty for Ra. The tradition vanished — until Akhenaten revived solar worship a thousand years later in.
descriptions.ba23010b-c042-4557-a580-384f2262febf: Built at the start of the 25th century BC by Userkaf, founder of the Fifth Dynasty. Called Nekhen-Re — Stronghold of Ra — standing between Abusir and Abu Gorab, declaring solar devotion in stone.
descriptions.01ad8566-fa7f-4e8b-9c45-dc790c324ca8: 4th century AD Lycian settlement of Sura, noted for its Temple of Apollo with a fish oracle — a dependency of Myra. On site: large sarcophagi, the ruined acropolis, Temple of Apollo,...
descriptions.03fdf67f-1fcc-49ae-b6c8-ed3aff640d30: Cucuteni-Trypillia mega-settlement dating 3600-3200 BC and covering 100 hectares. Sushkivka is one of 2,440 proto-cities of this vanished culture, discovered across Moldova and the steppe region.
descriptions.571c2899-adaa-4520-b758-3bdcaaf8d503: 2600–1900 BC westernmost known outpost of the Indus Valley civilisation, 480 km west of Karachi on the Makran coast. Sutkagan Dor's stone walls protected a 4.5-hectare frontier settlement near Iran.
descriptions.1cef558f-8c07-494e-b32a-6bb5690934a7: Two man-made caves carved into the Vaibhar Hills at Rajgir, Bihar — also known as Son Bhandar Caves. Some authors suggest they date to the Maurya Empire,...
descriptions.251ac618-a557-4c31-9129-65afc47b649d: Founded 446-445 BC by survivors of destroyed Sybaris, this colony on the Traeis river was short-lived. Most Sybarites were soon massacred by rival colonists from Thurii
descriptions.829e47ff-5760-4865-96ec-05ed93bd4399: 5th century BC city at the foot of Mount Ossa in Thessaly. During the Third Macedonian War, Perseus camped here between the mountain and the Peneus — overlooking Thessaly's plains and Larissa.
descriptions.91ecc1cb-6fa2-49f6-9d48-16f5bd7651f6: Founded 2nd century AD, Tabasqueno peaked in the 7th–10th centuries. Its most striking feature: a two-story Chenes Maya temple with a zoomorphic facade and rain god masks atop a multi-chambered base.
descriptions.82ee2c4b-cc3c-4f7f-a2b3-b9b1a47ec13e: 100-850 AD Maya cave complex in Yucatan with stone temples, small pyramids, and a causeway. Parts of the Tahtzibichen labyrinth can only be reached by divers — the site is not open to the public.
descriptions.2cb52ee9-dbd0-4437-8c4d-4fafeda01936: 9th century BC–10th century AD site with both Olmec and Maya features. Takʼalik Abʼajʼs 6.5 km² core holds 70 monumental structures, a dozen plazas, 2 ballcourts, and over 239 known monuments.
descriptions.2217d95d-950a-4073-8c3b-82d80d890111: 4th century BC city in the Koksu River valley of the Dzungar Alatau. Discovered in 1982, excavations began in 1985 under Professor A. N.
descriptions.f6b7b220-e370-4418-ba9d-d0f58e6f4c9d: 6th century BC stone platform 80 metres long and 15 metres high, built from 20 layers of slabs up to six tonnes each. Never finished — the Throne Hill likely inspired palatial design at Persepolis.
descriptions.8646c0ed-3749-41e2-ad61-986adb0b7d76: 1438-1530 AD Inca religious centre in the Cusco Region, about 48 km from the historic capital. Located in the Anta Province, Zurite District
descriptions.3af61846-6fa1-42b2-83a1-6046f3dc727e: Archaeological site in the Huancavelica Region, Tayacaja Province, near the main square of Acostambo at an elevation of about 3,400 metres
descriptions.3a75476c-410d-4a37-9858-b0733fc6965d: Declared a National Cultural Heritage. Tanqa Tanqa sits in the Zepita District, Chucuito Province, Puno Region — an archaeological site on the Andean altiplano near the frontier with Bolivia.
descriptions.a3e4eae7-5dbb-4e10-be96-065f54ce7e02: Iron Age hill fort shaped like a letter D, about 50 x 50 metres, in North Somerset. Also known as Chelvey Batch Settlement, Taps Combe Camp sits 2.9 km from Brockley — a compact Iron Age enclosure.
descriptions.218a4df9-1bc1-43ce-a054-1d964d7232a4: From 9000 BC, Aboriginal peoples camped in these limestone caves near Cape Bridgewater, Victoria. Stratified deposits 11,300 years old, shell midden deposits, and earth ovens over 11,...
descriptions.a5009e55-a34f-4568-9d9b-1d86d1082a9b: 400 BC–1539 AD Maya city with plazas, palaces, pyramid temples, an acropolis, defensive walls, and a cenote. Fifty burials and twelve caches recovered — Tayasal endured from Preclassic to Postclassic.
descriptions.ed7a8c35-1066-4b08-8bf4-3496a1ad0c81: Settled around 1000 BC and abandoned by 300 BC, Tayata predates the Mixteca Culture Classical Period. Grave goods and housing patterns suggest a political centre
descriptions.ce4058e7-7631-40ad-beb1-188e3cd27232: 3rd century BC city of Apulia, submitted to Rome in 318 BC as the region's primary settlement. Its ancient coins bear Oscan legends under the name Teate — a pre-Roman identity that outlasted conquest.
descriptions.2a9a96d5-f85c-4ff5-b2ef-1e92c5c9b6ca: 1st century AD Roman theatre ruins in the city of Rome — one of the entertainment venues of the imperial capital, now standing in partial ruin among the monuments of the ancient city.
descriptions.0d8af59c-71cb-4ff6-9620-3eb1faf2ebd3: 3250–2115 BC administrative centre of the Eshnunna Kingdom in Baghdad al-Jadeeda. First inhabited in the Akkadian age, Tel Harmal grew in the Old Babylonian period — original name Shadobom forgotten.
descriptions.fe3d5d3e-fef4-4ae8-bda9-bc41909c732e: 6th century BC Doric peripteral temple — oldest in Magna Graecia and the only surviving Greek religious structure in old Taranto. Medieval spoliation stripped it to fragments; its exact plan is lost.
descriptions.43600d73-1ab7-41bd-99cf-55af6c76f07f: Begun 480 BC, the Temple of Olympian Zeus was the largest Doric temple ever attempted — and was never finished. Its unfinished columns in the Valle dei Templi: a monument to overreaching ambition.
descriptions.ac3e720b-9c22-4757-ae62-6e29730c2dce: 11th century BC Nuragic sacred well in Sardinia — probably the best-preserved of its kind, though poorly maintained. Built during the Bronze Age for the cult of water
descriptions.1d578399-9992-4c37-ad18-5fba658492c7: 1st–5th century AD Roman fort at Rotherham, built in earth and timber around 43–68 AD and later rebuilt in stone. Occupied until Rome's withdrawal from Britain c. 410 AD — Latin name unknown.
descriptions.f4cce19d-39f9-460e-8ed4-37972063b966: 3rd century BC Temple of Apollo at Didyma. The temple is surrounded by 124 columns on a raised platform that can be climbed by steps on all four sides — a monumental Hellenistic sanctuary.
descriptions.4624b081-fd19-48f9-a93d-a6f74ede6c01: 2nd century AD Roman temple in Melite, built from marble with a tetrastyle portico — possibly on an earlier Punic sacred site. A 1747 inscription confirms a private benefactor funded its construction.
descriptions.556ae8b8-dacf-4bad-ba3a-5b05551f1f99: 3rd century BC–4th century AD — the fourth largest Ionic temple in the world at Sardis. A massive archaic limestone altar at the west end predates the temple, hinting sacred to Artemis far earlier.
descriptions.76a5a42b-f24e-4a03-8e19-e32c1493eb1b: 1st century AD Roman temple built under Tiberius in Lusitania's capital. Its columns survive intact — preserved because a 16th-century palace was built around them, shielding from demolition.
descriptions.67215100-355e-4586-ae41-00838c8e1566: Megalithic Greek temple in Sicily dedicated since 550 BC to a local form of Artemis, worshipped here as Diana. Used for nearly a thousand years, blending pre-Greek megalithic and classical traditions.
descriptions.0458351c-5185-4eca-9929-c5357a98557a: Around 630 BC, the Temple of Khonsuirdis was built for an important official of the 26th Dynasty reign of King Psamtik I. Located in the Luxor Governate — a private monument of the Late Period.
descriptions.47e69f36-27eb-4f43-be08-b99edb0a1b19: 2nd century AD temple dedicated to Nabu or Nebo, characterised by its eastern architectural style. The temple's cultural and architectural features still exist at the site
descriptions.6bea0e78-6584-474a-b7b4-b7eace0e81c9: 5th century BC temple at the tip of the Mani Peninsula, dedicated to Poseidon Asphaleios — Poseidon of Safety. The nearby cave was believed the entrance to Hades. Sparta blamed it for 464 BC quake.
descriptions.d8af7833-8171-40a3-a24c-cd3fff898c07: Built by Thutmose III on a Middle Kingdom foundation and enlarged by the Ptolemies, this Karnak shrine honours Ptah, Sekhmet, and Nefertum. Its history spans roughly 1800 BC to the 1st century AD.
descriptions.4290304f-a120-40b4-bf61-9ebc7d52673c: Built around 420 BC on a hilltop above the ruined city of Segesta. A well-preserved Doric temple possibly by an Athenian architect — commissioned by the indigenous Elymians for reasons still debated.
descriptions.3f793103-342f-40ca-a0fa-96b1065ad986: Built 1435–1425 BC in the final decade of Thutmose III's reign at Deir el-Bahari, above Hatshepsut's temple. Destroyed by earthquake in the 21st Dynasty — wall reliefs survive as painted fragments.
descriptions.bf538bd9-912c-471a-964a-f94842e17491: 6th century BC Doric temple, rebuilt by Rome in the 2nd century after the Jewish Revolt of 115 AD — given a new marble frontage. Destroyed again by a 4th-century earthquake,...
descriptions.1560f618-3e00-433c-9728-a9d86471fe4a: 1st century AD temple to Olympian Zeus in Jerash, on a high pedestal visible across the city. Its 15-metre Corinthian columns survived multiple earthquakes. Processions climbed stairs to reach it.
descriptions.11ac5108-ad13-4b42-babc-ed1e298bebe3: 13th-16th century AD Inca temple of pink granite at Machu Picchu, with windows aligned to the solstice sun. The Incas used it to honour the sun and Viracocha, the creator god
descriptions.31db21b8-df02-47a5-948d-a9ca1ef55531: 450–650 AD apartment complex beside the Teotihuacan pyramids, likely barracks or a warrior academy. Military murals of armed figures suggest Teotihuacan trained or housed its fighting forces here.
descriptions.04216aab-70cd-4488-a78e-468e4a6c1988: 100 BC-150 AD four-stepped pyramid built by the Teotihuacan culture, then abandoned. The Aztecs later reoccupied the site and probably built a temple on top
descriptions.4ccebe8e-9f02-4188-b9f1-431108bbcd58: An ovoid stone 80 cm across beside the ahu, Te Pito Kura — navel of light. Legend says founding king Hotu Matu'a carried it from his homeland.
descriptions.b465f4ec-0cf5-49a7-8a9b-9d4214e24bc8: 3rd century BC Founder's House in ancient Pisidian Termessos — a Roman-type villa whose 5-metre front door still stands. One of the better-preserved structures at this highland city of ancient.
descriptions.9ba3bc23-ac5b-489a-9038-bc65a5784e35: 3rd century BC theatre of the ancient Pisidian city of Termessos, set high in the Taurus Mountains. The theatre ruins command views over the surrounding mountain landscape of ancient Pisidia.
descriptions.3e22cce9-f37a-4838-a839-c388a90ac69e: 400 BC–600 AD town in Puebla with two Teotihuacan-style pyramids: the 14-metre Pyramid of Shells and 7-metre Pyramid of Rattles. Occupied over 1,000 years, Teteles was a regional centre.
descriptions.2a37333e-17ba-4a27-8084-3759d0b8501f: Inhabited from 36,000 BC through the Holocene, Tham Lod Rockshelter in Mae Hong Son Province served as cemetery and stone tool workshop.
descriptions.673332a5-3a27-4045-a929-ddbf7ff7e824: 5th century BC acropolis on Thasos with stone walls, an amphitheatre, a castle, and a temple to Athena. What survives is fragmentary — restoration preserves what remains of this hilltop sanctuary.
descriptions.4c5103a2-0ae8-443d-9203-f3a4bf4bbd6f: 15th-14th century BC Lycian burial monuments, buildings, and an amphitheatre woven into a living modern city. Funerary structures and contemporary streets share the same space
descriptions.e607e5aa-4028-4ffc-89ed-bae34f368810: 650–480 BC tower of Thimonia with no signage and no excavations ever conducted. Yet the original scale is legible in the standing stonework — views from this unresearched hilltop are worth the climb.
descriptions.4687a49a-c987-4c56-bc6e-5094aa57667d: 703–690 BC aqueduct of Sennacherib, built from over two million dressed stones with stone arches and waterproof cement. Part of the Atrush Canal, it carried water 50 km to Nineveh's gardens.
descriptions.218340f9-7b59-4e98-a13a-31452278ae01: 1st century AD Roman city of Ammaedara with a large Byzantine fort and underground Roman baths. Haidra preserves layers from Roman colony to Byzantine stronghold
descriptions.68ff480b-a02b-4458-b131-22dff4a00df6: 1860–1814 BC Black Pyramid of Amenemhat III at Dahshur — the first to house both pharaoh and queens together. Originally called Amenemhet is Mighty, it earned its dark name from centuries of decay.
descriptions.bcfba32b-fa88-44a0-8dc9-ace3a9416bb9: Archaeological park near the Western Wall with finds spanning the First and Second Temple periods, Byzantine, Muslim, and Crusader eras. Every stratum at this site represents a different civilisation.
descriptions.9ed175c7-a706-4a71-b10a-f93a68734afc: 5th-4th millennium BC Neolithic cairn in the Clwydian Range, Flintshire — the second-largest Neolithic mound in Britain after Silbury Hill.
descriptions.a6e95853-236b-4de9-b496-1491fd915423: 4th century BC Lycian city of Theimussa in the Demre/Antalya region. The ancient city's remains are modest — a small settlement within the wider Lycian cultural landscape of the Teke Peninsula.
descriptions.2a453751-5937-45b7-ac50-a5e5bab66680: Iron Age hillfort atop a cliff above Deborah's Hole cave on the Gower Peninsula, active 800 BC-1st century AD. Also known as Deborah's Hole Camp — the coastal path crosses the ancient site.
descriptions.752fc778-3443-43b9-9a4b-065fab448fd8: Celtic Iron Age hillfort near Trellech — one of roughly 300 registered by Cadw, though archaeologists believe nearly 600 once existed.
descriptions.ce507a92-23cf-49e2-ada8-734277dee902: Five Bronze Age burial cairns aligned over 5 km through Kilmartin Glen. The southernmost — Nether Largie South — is Neolithic, rebuilt in the Bronze Age: later generations buried beside the ancient.
descriptions.567bb6c8-7bd6-4bc9-aa27-f75ab92ea358: 6th century BC gateway to the Apollonia acropolis, its lintel carved with a lion devouring a bull. The Lion Gate seen today is a medieval reconstruction — violent archaic imagery across two millennia.
descriptions.46da573c-31ab-4f88-85e3-56ecf56334be: 1st century AD Roman road running westward from the fort of Derventio through Derbyshire to Rocester and on to Middlewich (Salinae). The Long Lane is its Medieval name — its Roman name is unrecorded.
descriptions.881f7aef-1b97-44e7-b41f-34636751e690: A cave carved into bedrock on Philopappou Hill in Athens, said to be where Socrates was allegedly imprisoned before his execution in 399 BC.
descriptions.8f2e5638-90d2-49a8-b5c8-8d425f75756f: 1st century AD Roman baths, active until an earthquake struck in 551 AD. The ruin of one bath hall is occasionally used as a performance space — reflecting the ancient traditions of the site.
descriptions.8b32820a-13d2-41c9-b96a-173a567582e8: Founded 631 BC as a Greek colony of Thera, Cyrene became one of the principal Hellenic cities of the ancient world. Romanised and thriving for a thousand years until the 365 AD earthquake ended them.
descriptions.2dcdec07-a26e-42bc-9490-b277628835f5: Silla Kingdom mountain fortress at Myeonghwal, part of the Gyeongju Historic Areas designated by UNESCO in 2000. Temples, palaces, pagodas, and statuary — one of the world's largest outdoor museums.
descriptions.a24e51aa-ecb6-4ba4-8d14-5ccabaf4aa56: 1st century AD semi-circular Roman Water Temple built under Emperor Hadrian, a monument to the spring that supplied the city of Carthage. The distinctive structure still stands at its mountain source.
descriptions.e8bc112c-9e95-4728-b181-e78d7de1fa26: Silla Kingdom site at Banwolseong — Half-moon Palace Fortress — part of the Gyeongju Historic Areas, UNESCO-listed in 2000. Palace ruins open to the sky in one of the world's largest outdoor museums.
descriptions.50cbcf03-2e37-4f82-9705-a55c9264b3d5: 3000–2800 BC megalithic tholos tomb in Seville Province — found in 1868 but unexcavated for decades. Resumed in 1980 due to urban sprawl, Montelirio remains closed; objects now in Seville museum.
descriptions.e7e09ce8-c980-405f-a877-ebb3c90dc7a2: 3rd-century AD Mithraic temple, one of only four mithraea found here. Undiscovered until 1998, its ritual pit yielded feasting remains revealing the secret banqueting rites of the Mithraic cult.
descriptions.34f1acbd-b1d2-4349-9946-75a36f323d6b: 1st-century AD Roman fort, the oldest in the Valea Timacului - a Balkan trade-axis node pairing a permanent garrison with large-scale mining and road construction across the region.
descriptions.248e424b-0b3a-4767-bfac-b4097709c43d: Inca storehouses on a mountain in the Ayacucho highlands, active 1438-1530 AD. A supply node in the empire's redistribution network, stockpiling goods for Andean communities across the region.
descriptions.cc5d75b4-88ed-4293-934c-c599bb13b7c1: 250-950 AD Yacata pyramid with a rare rectangular-plus-semicircular base, 4 m tall across six tiers. Possibly Teotihuacan-influenced, it may have been a Classic-period ceremonial centre.
descriptions.f42a2997-d354-48b1-99b5-1a38cef7d01c: Maya site on the Macal River, with Chaa Creek and Cahal Pech located further downstream. During the colonial era, Tipu played a major role in delaying the Spanish conquest of the Peten region.
descriptions.bb312418-3990-4a2a-86a3-5f3bc9c1c7b2: Archaeological site in the Cusco Region, situated in the northeast of Cusco city - a settlement in the heart of the Inca imperial core.
descriptions.e3c407dd-513d-4344-8155-7bcc5db65b54: Neolithic tomb in southern Corsica, excavated from 1960. The finds proved prehistoric links between Corsica and Sardinia - island neighbours sharing Bronze Age burial traditions.
descriptions.021307e1-d101-463b-a4ec-0c6cfbad0b7e: 4th-century AD Berber mausoleum near the Saharan oasis of Abalessa. Attributed to Queen Tin Hinan, ancestor of the Tuareg - a multi-chamber monument blending Mediterranean and Saharan traditions.
descriptions.90e808a1-7ea7-44ce-a1c9-05cf10c133be: 358-338 BC rock-cut tomb near ancient Persepolis, ascribed to Artaxerxes III. Carved in the Achaemenid royal necropolis tradition - a cliff-face grave at the heart of ancient imperial power.
descriptions.4cf11aeb-7f27-42f4-aca4-2717a41fa515: Etruscan tomb in the Necropolis of Banditaccia, 9th-3rd century BC. Named for its carved stone funeral beds - a record of how the Etruscans furnished the afterlife as a permanent home.
descriptions.f80ffef9-a3c9-472f-a429-dd591ce7372b: 5th-century BC monument - the only structure surviving from ancient Sparta's agora. Its purpose remains debated: cenotaph, temple to Karneios Apollo, or the tomb of King Leonidas himself.
descriptions.1290975e-81bb-498e-a002-fd7fddb5f4fa: Late 4th-century BC Macedonian tomb at ancient Lete, with a monumental facade and two vaulted chambers. Discovered among cist graves on the road between Thessaloniki and Langadas.
descriptions.c95bfa77-3206-4e97-af5e-dab113e81b8d: Known as the Tomb of the False Door - an Aksumite monument with finely dressed stone blocks, antechamber, inner chamber, and surrounding passage. A damaged sarcophagus can still be seen inside.
descriptions.3cb40a58-d0d1-4094-bb78-2398d60dbd5c: 2500 BC tomb beneath the Giza complex. Archaeologists found millions of mummified birds in labyrinthine caverns - a cache revealing industrial-scale preservation practices of the pharaohs.
descriptions.351a3b2e-3492-4b92-adf0-700269fb06c7: Talayotic settlement built 1700-1400 BC with two talayots, a hypostyle room, and a taula - the T-shaped stone monument unique to Menorca. Among the best-preserved Naviforme sites in the Balearics.
descriptions.3315cd99-84ed-4e95-b743-fe75fb4c7654: Roman watchtower built over a temple base, confirming a full Roman city once stood here. Occupied 2nd-10th century AD, its temple-plan granite foundations are still visible in the standing walls.
descriptions.3d68442a-8cd7-4679-8845-189db9470f27: A Bronze Age tell-mound formed by mudbrick settlement collapse and rebuilding - the Aegean equivalent of a Near Eastern tell. Each layer conceals a distinct era of prehistoric northern occupation.
descriptions.2372d1b2-ce2b-4e66-8779-4d1ac95ba052: 1st-2nd century AD museum in ancient Palmyra - once one of antiquity's greatest cultural crossroads. The city's art fused Graeco-Roman technique with local traditions and Persian influence.
descriptions.dcfca154-a46b-4515-849a-e9248d470e07: 1st-century BC triumphal arch - once the central opening of a three-arch granite gateway into an imperial temple precinct, a monument believed to honour the emperor Trajan.
descriptions.f1bf0bf8-26a8-4e50-ab3d-702b208bdad5: Roman auxiliary fort built in the 70s AD, housing up to 800 infantry across a 2.1-hectare enclosure. Abandoned ~130 AD, it once supported ~2,000 people overlooking a Roman bridge over the river.
descriptions.ff136c0c-2d3a-4621-b27b-294758b9cc4d: 4th-century BC treasury at Delphi, built ~334-322 BC by Cyrene in gratitude for the wheat it donated during a lean period. The last treasury raised in the sanctuary of Apollo, facing the god's temple.
descriptions.a6f66111-c0d1-4c01-a49a-eb2d476a33d0: 5th-century BC treasury at Delphi, built by Acanthos to commemorate its joint victory with the Lacedaemonians against Athens. A monument to the moment one city switched sides in the Peloponnesian War.
descriptions.a926a42b-701d-453b-9f9a-f9e58225bdd2: 2nd-3rd century AD city whose acropolis is honeycombed with chambers - first tombs, then dwellings. Roman and Byzantine layers overlap here, a small ancient city that outlasted both empires.
descriptions.5a3da9b9-6d74-4991-bfa3-3e41f600bcdf: 4th-millennium BC site on north Anglesey. The surrounding landscape holds Neolithic remains from one of the earliest-settled coastal zones on this part of the island.
descriptions.78c9f0a2-2247-4159-87ce-9a0e69e88e28: ~3000 BC dolmen above Casaglione village in Corsica, with a distinctive semicircular capstone. One of the island's inland megalithic monuments, raised by communities known only through their stones.
descriptions.b740c74a-83ce-4e01-a07c-87ab90574750: Maya site dated to 400 BC with three stelae and an altar arranged as an E-Group astronomical complex. A monument to Maya celestial observation, active from the Late Preclassic period.
descriptions.d074c899-cdcb-48db-9207-1ebea88ce927: 3100-1100 BC Minoan settlement on a 135 m hill in the Mesara Plain, 800 m from the sea. Three freshwater springs fed this Cretan outpost, inhabited through the height of Minoan civilisation.
descriptions.da102984-38e2-45d9-b411-bb0bbadfb6e1: 1875-1700 BC Minoan settlement - the easternmost section of ancient Archanes. Multi-storey buildings with paved courtyards, light-wells, and ashlar walls mark a sophisticated Bronze Age community.
descriptions.4d446438-7613-43d2-b95e-c6f1acf9109d: ~10,000 figures carved across 15 sq km in the Tsagaan Salaa valley of Altai Tavan Bogd. A UNESCO site spanning Neolithic to Bronze Age - one of Central Asia's largest petroglyph archives.
descriptions.c30712db-a675-4203-a442-cb3f9b1c5848: ~50,000 BC cave at 2,100 m - one of the world's highest known archaeological sites. Tsona Cave preserves Palaeolithic remains from communities navigating the high Caucasus mountain passes.
descriptions.c254f03d-ccce-4588-8094-5a11fbe67b6f: Neanderthal cave at 320 m above the Chishura River, inhabited from ~48,000 BC. This karst cave yielded artefacts confirming human presence in the Imereti highlands long before farming began.
descriptions.5741eec1-d6ca-4a63-b0cb-f9a106a4acca: Neolithic settlement occupied 6000-4300 BC near modern Skopje - the most significant in the valley. Found during motorway construction in 1961, its stratigraphy maps layers of early farming life.
descriptions.58dd6a0b-4c70-4eee-824f-a270800ef886: Karst cave in Ojcow National Park with 15 archaeological layers in 4.5 m of sediment. Cultures include Lengyel, Corded Ware, Funnelbeaker, and Lusatian - a Central European prehistoric archive.
descriptions.c24ada61-f1a4-4b32-b66b-bd72d68ad0d8: Iron Age univallate hillfort near Camerton, Somerset, now nearly ploughed flat. Its faint earthwork traces are all that remain of a 1st-millennium BC fortified settlement on the hilltop.
descriptions.723dad90-4cd2-42ca-a8d1-9cf8fe11f1f0: Inca-period site in the Puno Region near Lake Titicaca, c. 1400 AD. In Yunguyo Province, it was part of the altiplano's dense Inca administration - high-altitude settlements tied to the sacred lake.
descriptions.24a45da1-8a7e-4f93-8a04-03e3e29a2376: Rock painting site on Mount Saywa at 3,150 m in the Urubamba highlands. It shares a ritual landscape with the Ayawayq'u site 800 m away - two painted stations on the same Andean sacred route.
descriptions.7a0fa7b4-88fb-49d0-bfd7-9ebe9c5109d8: Ancient town in the Phoinix district of Caria, always inhabited across the historical ages. A node in the regional settlement network where successive ancient powers left overlapping traces.
descriptions.7244b9b6-0f20-413f-b646-06a60f11b23c: Hopi petroglyph site at Echo Cliffs, used from ~1200 AD into the 1950s. Over 5,000 clan symbols on eight boulders - a rite-of-passage registry for young men making pilgrimages to the Grand Canyon.
descriptions.368b8086-0cd2-4d5d-9a8a-3afb582b2e81: 4th century BC-4th century AD Lycian hilltop city with rectangular stone walls. Sarcophagi and rock tombs with inscriptions cluster its slopes - a city that recorded its dead for seven centuries.
descriptions.8044f723-251d-47db-9036-4839b2d4dc96: 4th-century AD Lycian rock-cut tomb at Tyberissos - one of the most distinctive burial forms on this coast. Its carved facade survives as a monument to the Lycian tradition of cliff-side burial.
descriptions.9294a69f-56f7-4011-b296-f0e17a0aeb15: Ancient Lycian city on rocky Asarlik Tepe, with a bedrock-cut acropolis entrance and well-preserved baths on the southeast slope. Active 500 BC-300 AD, it survived successive empires on its hilltop.
descriptions.51aa1b30-451a-4cab-a0fb-50710f87e13a: 4000-2000 BC settlement excavated 2015-2017 by an international team. Kura-Araxes ceramics link it to the nearby Duzdagh salt mine - placing it within a regional Bronze Age exchange network.
descriptions.88821924-cf89-499a-956d-55214bf9882c: 7th-century AD Maya city with two irrigation channels, 114 structures, and 150+ residential groups. Covering 2.6 sq km with temples, palaces, and ballcourts near the source of the Belize River.
descriptions.521d852a-e3f0-4d19-a084-2143d6b25a97: 1st-century BC Roman municipium that remained loyal to Caesar when most towns switched to Pompey. Caesar rewarded it with the title Fidentia - preserved in its full name, Ulia Fidentia.
descriptions.86055e38-1e16-4ba3-8c67-c1768f1a7d4e: 3rd-millennium BC basalt quarry on Gebel el-Qatrani in the Faiyum depression - one of antiquity's earliest industrial quarrying operations, supplying dense black stone for Old Kingdom construction.
descriptions.ad967817-008f-4cb3-9302-e8b0ef460788: Dilmun burial mound field from the 3rd-2nd millennium BC, inscribed UNESCO World Heritage in 2019. Part of the Dilmun Burial Mounds - monuments of an ancient Gulf trading civilisation.
descriptions.57a2ea53-edcb-4096-8b4a-f5e0a7e23ddf: Hellenistic salt mine dated to 300 BC, first mapped by a Danish team in 1968. Square building footprints hint at an organised operation - the oldest known salt extraction site in eastern Arabia.
descriptions.173c03f1-90d6-41d4-93d3-2bded70d2489: Inca-period chullpa tomb complex southwest of Chivay in the Caylloma highlands, c. 1200 AD. Stone burial towers mark the pre-Hispanic tradition of entombing the dead above ground near communities.
descriptions.810d09d7-37a5-443b-84de-e1101e44e855: Pre-Hispanic site in the Huanuco highlands at ~2,833 m in Pachitea Province. Perched above the Amazonian lowlands, it preserves Andean settlement traces from a rugged mountain transition zone.
descriptions.f057c595-7ea4-42ce-bf5d-734fad5a1e47: Late Inca site near the main square of Tamburco in Apurimac, c. 1400 AD. Positioned in the province bordering Cusco, it represents a formally settled community in the Inca imperial heartland.
descriptions.97e6920e-fb90-41d1-9e6c-38a76029e782: Inca hilltop site at ~4,400 m in Lucanas Province, known as Inti Watana II and III - invoking the Inca sun-tethering ritual. Straddling three district borders, it held ceremonial importance here.
descriptions.b287e7d6-f61a-4397-b847-56ce0419dd0c: 1st-century AD Roman-Berber city with an amphitheatre, capitol, baths, cisterns, an aqueduct, and wealthy villas. Uthina shows Roman urban planning grafted onto North Africa within a generation.
descriptions.ea95860c-6226-406e-b606-4d8ee4e8f6a3: Bronze Age megaliths from ~1200 BC carved with animals, weapons, human faces, and patterns. Used in shamanic ceremonies - sentinel stones still standing after three millennia on the open steppe.
descriptions.7f4d97ca-67d4-419e-b156-9bd2ee77dea6: Middle Bronze Age settlement near Aghdam with a cultural layer ~3.5 m deep - one of the region's earliest known urban sites. Excavations uncovered a circular brick wall enclosing the upper hill.
descriptions.bbb154a9-15fc-4c3a-b0ca-8b46a26a3af7: Built 2570 BC as a mortuary complex for Pharaoh Khafre and his family. Part of the Giza complex, the Valley Temple served as the ritual entrance gateway before the ascent to the pyramid.
descriptions.7753067f-ce23-4def-81de-184ce34eefce: Multi-period site where Bronze Age and early Christian layers stack atop one another. Three distinct occupation epochs were identified, spanning several millennia.
descriptions.db120341-8ea9-4841-9e41-6c9d9df171b3: Prehistoric site in the commune of Sotta in southern Corsica. Part of a network of ancient settlements scattered across the island's interior, attesting to occupation before recorded history begins.
descriptions.a36bb548-bebc-4606-af26-9cded2b3cded: 5th-millennium BC earthwork complex near Vatin - four concentric earthen circles ~150 m in diameter. Thought to be astronomical observatories, predating Stonehenge's first phase by over a millennium.
descriptions.19f1118c-190f-47f7-a161-8d6cd52277e7: Occupied from 21,000 BC, this elliptical cave on Korcula island is 40 m long and 17 m high. Oldest known habitation site in the eastern Adriatic, with two natural openings in the cavern roof.
descriptions.5b24d3c4-1382-434d-a177-e09fb0b8778d: Palaeolithic site in Limburg province spanning 50,000-12,000 BC. A Stone Age camp reused across tens of millennia - one of the oldest known human activity sites here, with ice-age hunter evidence.
descriptions.1ac1779a-749a-4726-a671-d49a3d1b16e2: Ancient Ausone city destroyed by Rome in 340 BC, with pre-Roman walls surviving near the Garigliano river. Vescia was one of the Auruncan Pentapolis cities absorbed in Rome's southward expansion.
descriptions.a9dea7fa-8e85-4c6d-82c1-4c16b1a000b3: 9th-3rd century BC Etruscan necropolis at Cerveteri's Banditaccia. The oldest section held Villanovan burial grounds; the Zona del Recinto contains ~2,000 tombs - a city built for the Etruscan dead.
descriptions.c485a7c6-0006-4f6f-8dd7-f5f39a427d84: 1st-century AD Roman city whose ruins scatter across 800 m, with a temple and basilica still traceable. A North African outpost revealing the early empire's reach deep into the interior.
descriptions.1830d83f-cbbc-4d15-b37d-950c8282fa07: Iron Age univallate promontory hillfort at 230 m in north Devon, close to Beacon Castle. Rare for Devon - a slight fort type with an outer earthwork - commanding the eastern side of Heale Down.
descriptions.bbae3db6-eb55-418c-9478-babfe5e087d2: A Karelian plateau strewn with Sami sacred stones (seids), boulders balanced on smaller rocks, and twisted trees. Called a Place of Power, its stone arrangements resist all archaeological explanation.
descriptions.480b7897-a76a-406c-9991-7c1c8228f905: 3rd-4th century AD Roman mausoleum complex spanning 25 hectares. Built during the Tetrarchy in Dacia Ripensis with 32-bastion walls and a crypted basilica - discovered by Dragoslav Srejovic.
descriptions.d9413d19-05a0-4bac-bed2-da8462ca46b6: 3rd-1st millennium BC Minoan mountain citadel above the Gulf of Mirabello in eastern Crete. Perched 1.5 km from another early site, Vrokastro commanded a coastline dense with Bronze Age settlement.
descriptions.03b7e28c-db24-4b69-9cc7-234ffc80053c: 3rd-millennium BC Dilmun burial mound field, inscribed UNESCO World Heritage in 2019. Part of the Dilmun Burial Mounds - Bronze Age mortuary traditions on the Persian Gulf coast.
descriptions.0a05d7ed-33cc-432a-b831-c67cf546593f: Capital of the Waithali Kingdom 370-818 AD in northern Rakhine State, 70 km northeast of Sittwe. Like its predecessor Dhanyawadi, only a few temples survive from five centuries of rule.
descriptions.5169991f-862a-451b-b76f-9a49a8bc5f8b: Inca-period site on Mount Wamanilla at ~4,200 m in the Ayacucho highlands. Straddling two provinces, its name is shared with the mountain - where Andean landscape and identity are inseparable.
descriptions.301aec5d-a2ce-42e2-9a76-41c781cd9ace: Pre-Hispanic site in the Cusco Region's Chumbivilcas Province at ~3,600 m. Part of a rugged highland zone south of Cusco where scattered sites mark successive Andean cultures before Inca expansion.
descriptions.00c2b26f-d007-4c02-a5da-403f14f8daa5: Pre-Hispanic site in the Yauyos highlands at 3,800 m above sea level. One of many high-altitude communities occupying Lima Region's mountain ranges before Inca unification of the Andes.
descriptions.ddbaa0c7-7d30-45fa-ab80-71b0d49d8dec: Inca-period site declared National Cultural Heritage in 2003, in Lucanas Province, Ayacucho. Near Andamarca, Waman Pirqa sits in a region of continuous Andean identity from prehistory to the present.
descriptions.9aaa53a6-b89d-4511-b9ae-e5e89e640bea: Pre-Hispanic site in Chinchao District, Huanuco highlands, at ~3,359 m. Perched above the cloud-forest transition, it marks the edge where Andean highland culture met the slopes toward Amazonia.
descriptions.9effdfa3-4808-45e7-be9a-578a870e1899: Andean burial complex with stone walls and round chullpa towers in the Junin highlands, c. 1200 AD. Chullpas were built above ground so the dead could be revisited - a tradition outlasting the Incas.
descriptions.84e58c4d-9c61-4454-b165-041371c9b2c1: Late Inca site near Cusco city, c. 1400 AD, on the San Jeronimo-Saylla district boundary. One of many settlements in Cusco Province forming the capital's agricultural and administrative hinterland.
descriptions.0e5f74c4-f35a-4f3b-8875-98c3c91da9fe: Pre-Hispanic site on Warahirka mountain at ~3,400 m in the Yarowilca highlands. Part of a cluster of highland settlements near Pampamarca that pre-date Inca conquest of the Huanuco region.
descriptions.7268effd-38c0-4961-a203-561e19982b1f: Archaeological site in the Cordillera Blanca at ~4,600 m in Chavin de Huantar District. Waraqayuq overlooks valleys that connected coastal and highland worlds in the Andes' most storied range.
descriptions.417b5b9b-3654-4525-b6be-cc39df900ba3: 13th-century AD Chanka site at ~3,852 m in La Mar Province, Ayacucho. Belonging to the Chanka confederation - rivals of the rising Inca - in the highlands before Inca unification of the region.
descriptions.a4f216bd-ef7d-4764-aa03-c88b3d5a588e: The oldest known inland habitation site, occupied 49,000-10,000 years ago in the Flinders Ranges. Artefacts here include the earliest known evidence of key technologies in the continent's prehistory.
descriptions.553ad771-5748-4cb7-a03f-10362f5253df: 1st-5th century AD Roman auxiliary fort in Gateshead, found from the air in 1970. Trapezoid-shaped at 149 x 125 m across 1.8 hectares, it has never been excavated - its story locked beneath the Tyne.
descriptions.d6bc5056-b3e5-4038-86f4-cdb08090202a: Iron Age hillfort at ~90 m above Silverbridge Lake, 1st millennium BC. Southeast of Plympton near Blackpool hamlet, Wasteberry Camp commanded the high ground with few earthworks surviving today.
descriptions.0a6e70ea-022a-4035-a866-0e54efff533d: Late Inca archaeological zone near Huarocondo, c. 1400 AD, with five named sections: Wat'aq'asa, Willkapata, Qhawarina, Qullqa, and Saksaywaman Pata - preserving Inca ceremonial and storage functions.
descriptions.660397b7-a480-4ae7-9742-5ff0970c8e31: Inca-period site near Machu Picchu District, active 1438-1530 AD. Above the Willkanuta River left bank, it neighbours Machu Q'inti, Willkaraqay and Patallaqta - Quechua names evoking the hummingbird.
descriptions.14aacb74-9cd3-4766-b74b-4911d804c415: Ancient drover's road moving cattle from Wales to southeastern markets. Merging with Watling Street at Shrewsbury, it passed through Cannock Chase - a well-worn economic artery used for centuries.
descriptions.06b4c496-930b-45ac-a8f4-3e4831de1a50: Iron Age univallate hillfort in the Mendip Hills, Somerset, 1st millennium BC. Its narrow summit bank suggests a dry-stone rampart; the northeast defences have been progressively quarried away.
descriptions.cfffa587-4250-43cb-89c2-84cad4e21c8a: Neolithic stone circle beneath Corndon Hill, 4th millennium BC. Near the Hoarstones and Mitchell's Fold circles, the Whetstones formed a cluster of ritual monuments on the border with Shropshire.
descriptions.b0676488-4c32-4b8c-857c-eba8d6db4f59: Ceremonial centre active 1200-800 BC during the Kishka Pata Period in the Ayacucho Valley. One of the region's earliest known ritual sites - organised ceremonial activity five centuries before Chavin.
descriptions.f3a9d429-16b9-4ecd-97de-26319d3552ea: Rock art site in the Tacna highlands with paintings dominated by hunting scenes featuring camelids. A window into the lives of ancient Andean hunters tracking llama and vicuna across the high plains.
descriptions.45762448-5303-4e98-a999-e6aa22f63595: Late Bronze Age hillfort near Letchworth, dated to ~700 BC. One of six similar forts along the northern Chilterns - its concentric banks and ditches now detectable mainly as aerial cropmarks.
descriptions.47396b3b-88aa-4d18-a7ac-8bec4154c19d: Pre-Hispanic site in the Amazonian foothills near the Cajaruro-Bongara border. A frontier zone where highland Andean cultures met the lowland forests - a threshold between two worlds.
descriptions.e8234ff9-0b4e-4961-a0ca-f15d09232a0a: Neolithic henge in Wiltshire's Vale of Pewsey, known only from aerial cropmarks - a broad circular ditch near the River Avon. Positioned south of the massive Marden Henge in a dense ritual landscape.
descriptions.87ea9721-2bb2-456a-b1e6-8a44dbde62d3: Stone circle near Avebury dating 3300-500 BC, with evidence of an outer ring, inner ring, and central stone. Only six stones remain, none upright - 5.5 km north of Avebury's vast henge complex.
descriptions.1130f0c2-f133-4699-b2ea-c93999faa564: Mountain at ~3,600 m in the Cusco highlands where two summit rocks resemble toads - one faces Ausangate, the other Huaro. The lake Quyllur Urmana at its feet marks a site of Andean sacred geography.
descriptions.faab0d7b-1f66-45b9-8b1b-95697a3fc320: Pre-Hispanic site at 3,781 m in the Huancavelica highlands, with an ancient town, a stone forest, and caves with rock paintings. A rare combination of settlement and cave art at high altitude.
descriptions.eb13e438-eba3-44d7-8189-9365e245f0b8: Known to the Maya as Bahlam Jol, Witzna flourished 1st-8th century AD near the Holmul-Ixcan confluence. Inscriptions confirmed the city's own name - palaces and pyramids fill its unexcavated centre.
descriptions.8153d20b-c794-4c70-9269-7f20884d5149: Iron Age promontory hillfort at ~145 m in Stoke Fleming parish. On Norton Down's southern side, Woodbury commanded coastal approaches to Dartmouth - one of the southwest's finest natural harbours.
descriptions.3a5a2af9-ac8c-4e1c-82ed-bfa765c0796d: 4th-millennium BC settlement on the Aras River bank in Nakhchivan. Linked to the Xelecler - a Turkic tribe who served Caliphate armies - where Bronze Age roots gave way to medieval memory.
descriptions.c2e69ada-5d35-4852-8b60-dddc32cb540d: Rock shelter in the Rio Balsas valley, occupied 8900-8600 years ago. Starch and phytolith evidence here yielded some of the earliest known proof of domesticated maize and squash in the world.
descriptions.d217ef2a-7e8f-4ec6-8635-8c1970713899: Maya settlement beside a cenote near Libre Union, active 250-1697 AD. Stone carvings beside the sacred sinkhole document 1,400+ years of occupation - from the Classic period past Spanish conquest.
descriptions.47c3b2a4-e476-4d38-b390-280c136fd1c5: 600 BC-550 AD Maya city 40 km northeast of Tikal, with a 35 m pyramid, two ballcourts, and 24 stelae. Its Los Arboles complex bears Royal Jaguar Cult stucco imagery still being decoded by scholars.
descriptions.02f1050b-2a58-41c6-86b2-62481e249e05: Hilltop necropolis at ~3,820 m in the Ancash highlands with rectangular, semicircular, and quadrangular stone structures. The twin villages of Yanaque and Quilcamarca share a mountain and a myth.
descriptions.0057a907-515b-4bdf-9ca2-72c9004796b3: Iron Age hillfort near Bigbury in Devon, at ~80 m above the Avon Estuary. A compact 1st-millennium BC defensive site commanding river approaches along a long-used inland route.
descriptions.2bbc9730-d938-4fd5-a8e5-594ea046d183: Submerged stonework near the Yarrows Archaeological Trail in Caithness, possibly a docking area dating to ~200 BC. These sunken remains hint at a harbour serving Iron Age communities of the far north.
descriptions.24f1c052-5bc8-490e-9b1e-ccce0c05611b: 7th-century AD royal seat of Bernicia, built over Mesolithic remains. Its Anglo-Saxon timber halls were among the grandest in early medieval Northumbria - a power centre recorded in Bede's writings.
descriptions.f50ba7d8-09e1-4c03-8661-84d6b6d4eadd: Iron Age enclosure or hillfort on Cutwell Hill at ~155 m, south of South Brent. A 1st-millennium BC defended site above the Dartmoor foothills in a landscape rich with prehistoric earthworks.
descriptions.d7c001c0-c499-4c06-a756-2ceca75092d6: Minoan cemetery built in Early Minoan I and used through Middle Minoan IA. Near Lendas, south of the Asterousia mountains, Yerokambos preserves some of Crete's earliest known burial evidence.
descriptions.7f89584a-ea4f-4f5b-85ce-a64710721157: 2nd-millennium-8th century BC stone quarry and statue school with sphinxes, gate lions, and war reliefs in situ. Yesemek is thought to have supplied monumental sculptures across the ancient Near East.
descriptions.8c8da405-a1d6-41c6-9460-c77dc999a673: Bronze Age dolmen complex dated 3300-1200 BC near Yongin, designated Gyeonggi-do Monument in 1974. The two megalithic tombs are the largest and best-preserved in the province - twelve once stood here.
descriptions.c624f12f-6c16-4b2e-9f8d-11095901b8f8: Ancient ruin sometimes called Jonah's Pillar, active 5th century BC through 4th century AD. Little survives, but its longevity across Lycian, Hellenistic, and Roman periods speaks to local endurance.
descriptions.33dcafa5-a28f-40c6-a1a3-32d01501c6f2: Rock painting site at ~3,991 m on the slope of Pukara, north of Cerro de Pasco. At extreme altitude, these paintings preserve the visual language of highland communities who made art in thin air.
descriptions.f82d4a70-4581-4e06-858a-d52019ecbd0f: Maya city active 1000 BC-950 AD, one of few communities that maintained independence into early Spanish colonial rule. Zacpeten's groups are enclosed by a defensive wall with two parapets and a moat.
descriptions.e7e75467-cc43-437e-9221-5ed85c050e63: 8th century BC Thracian settlement that became a 35-hectare Late Roman fortress with 32 bastions, a civic basilica, an early Christian basilica with crypts, and a water reservoir.
descriptions.2da98755-bd8f-4281-a7d6-b271dac1bc4e: Upper Palaeolithic cave inhabited 48,000-10,000 BC with paintings, flint knives, arrowheads, bone combs, and milling boards. Excavated 1981-1987 - one of the Caucasus's oldest known inhabited sites.
descriptions.fa9441c6-255f-4fc3-aaba-8aa8b43759ac: Byzantine cave settlement with fifteen cave churches, now an open-air museum. Zelve's rock-cut rooms and chapels document centuries of Christian monastic life carved into Cappadocia's volcanic rock.
descriptions.f1326949-db93-4012-8d4e-f38836149b93: 4th-century AD Byzantine village in the Dead Cities region, with a tall basilica and two churches - one 4th century, one 6th - plus a cistern and household ruins from a community that never recovered.
descriptions.1203a68d-5c19-4f8e-828f-053129f79a63: 3rd-millennium BC village at 820 m in the Kakheti highlands, investigated since the 1960s. Stone artefacts at Ziari testify to Palaeolithic workshops - a site far older than its Bronze Age occupation.
